title: impvalues (Ibragimov-Muller) confidence intervals cover 5-29% at nominal 95% wherever several clusters share the same levels of i
surface: impvalues (+ cluster()); all reported se/t/p/lb_*ci/ub_*ci, including the ES horizons and the contreat ame rows
claim: Under `impvalues` the G "per-cluster estimates" whose dispersion becomes the reported standard error are not G separate fits: they are `margins, dydx(targetflag) over(cluster)` evaluated on the ONE pooled model (wooldid.ado:2042 margins call, 2047-2048 column grab, 2054 the ttest whose r(se) is reported). Wherever several clusters share the same levels of i -- a cluster finer than i, or crossed with it -- those reads take only as many distinct values as the clusters have distinct weight profiles over the i-by-relative-period cells (three, one per treated cohort, under i=cg + cluster(unit); exactly one when every cluster has the same cohort composition). Their spread is then cross-cohort effect heterogeneity, with the sampling component absent entirely, so the reported standard error is 6x to 34x too small and the interval covers far below its stated level. The same construction supplies every impvalues row (pretreatment 2100-2110, event-study horizons 2219-2229, continuous-treatment ame 2320/2375/2715).
observed: mc_imp2.txt (R=200, i=cg, cluster(unit) -- the pairing the help recommends, 40 units, effects 1.00/1.05/0.95): impvalues 95% coverage 0.290 (3 binomial SE = 0.046, FLAGGED), mean reported IM se 0.0211 against a true point-estimate sd of 0.1239 (5.9x too small); the analytic clustered interval on the SAME draws covers 0.955 with mean se 0.1377. mc_imp.txt (R=250, cluster(reg) crossing i=cg, effects 1.00/1.02/0.98): impvalues coverage 0.048, mean se 0.00257 against sd 0.0857 (34x too small), mean(b)=0.9983 against target 1.00142 (unbiased, 0.36 MC SE); analytic arm covers 0.968. Mechanism shown exactly in probeD.log / repro block 1: with 25 regions each holding one unit per cohort and sd(y)=1.66, wooldid blanks EVERY se/t/p/lb/ub and prints "the per-cluster estimates were numerically identical ... A collapsed IM standard error usually reflects deterministic or noiseless data - please verify your input" -- on data that is not remotely deterministic. Verified repro run: R=40, IM coverage 0.250, IM se 0.020854 vs true sd 0.104357, analytic se 0.140170, analytic coverage 1.000.
expected: An interval reported at level(95) covers its target about 95% of the time and its standard error is within sampling error of the estimator's sd -- the analytic arm on identical data does exactly that, which isolates the IM machinery. The help sells impvalues as the valid fallback where the analytic path is not ("Valid ame inference under such designs: ... impvalues - cross-cluster dispersion inference, which remains valid"). Ibragimov-Muller may legitimately absorb true cluster heterogeneity, but no version of it permits the sampling component to be absent altogether, which is what a deterministic re-weighting of one fit gives. Note the asymmetry: permute() REFUSES a cluster that does not nest i with a named r(459), and bootstrap() carries an explicit documented two-regime rule for the same geometry; impvalues has no guard, no caution and no help sentence. This is NOT the ruled T4 item, which concerns non-att estimands under cross-cutting clusters: every run here uses `att` alone and the headline geometry is a cluster nested inside i.
refuter_note: The claim's headline proposition, its numbers, its surface and its severity all reproduce, but one explanatory sub-clause is wrong. The prober wrote that the per-cluster spread is cross-cohort effect heterogeneity 'with the sampling component absent entirely'. It is not: the 3 distinct reads DO carry the sampling component -- the control arm proves it, since the same 3 numbers referred to sqrt(3) and t(2) give se/sd 0.794 and 0.97 coverage. The actual defect is MULTIPLICITY: each distinct read is counted once per cluster, so ttest divides by sqrt(G_clusters) and refers to t(G_clusters-1) where the honest divisor is sqrt(#distinct reads) and the honest reference is t(#distinct reads-1). The deflation is ~sqrt(G_clusters/#distinct reads) (4.69x here) and the df is inflated from 2 to 44. 'Sampling component absent entirely' is only the limiting case, reached when every cluster has an identical weight profile, where the reads collapse to one value and the degeneracy scrub blanks the row.
refuter_did: Rebuilt the case from the claim on my own DGP (60 units, i=cg, 12 periods, unit random intercept sd .70 NOT absorbed by i=cg, AR(1)(.4) errors sd .55, WITHIN-cohort effect heterogeneity, cohort effects 1.00/1.15/0.85) and ran the control arm the prober never ran: the same data, the same draws, only the cluster variable swapped. 140-draw MC (p2_mcimp.do): impvalues cluster(unit) (cluster FINER than i) gives mean(se) 0.0233 against sd(b) 0.1376, se/sd = 0.169, and 95% coverage 0.257 vs the att truth, 0.264 vs the cluster-equal-weighted truth, 0.243 around its OWN Monte Carlo mean (3 binomial SE 0.055). impvalues cluster(cg) (cluster == i, textbook IM, df 2) on the SAME draws: se/sd 0.794, coverage 0.971. analytic cluster(unit): se/sd 0.912, coverage 0.957. I also MEASURED the event-study horizons the prober only asserted: post0 se/sd 0.224 coverage 0.314; post1 se/sd 0.209 coverage 0.343. No caution of any kind appears in any log. I then proved the exact mechanism arithmetically: cluster(cg) reports se 0.105582803 on 2 df, so sd over the 3 distinct reads is 0.18287478; if the 45 per-unit reads are those 3 values each repeated 15 times the reported se must be 0.18287478*sqrt(2*15/44)/sqrt(45) = 0.022510329274, and the observed cluster(unit) se is 0.022510329 -- ratio 1.000000000000000 to 15 digits. Scope actually run: the pooled att row and the att-family ES horizons in binary mode; the contreat ame rows named in the claim's surface share the construction by code inspection only. This is not T4: every run is att alone and the headline geometry is a cluster nested INSIDE i, which sthlp:255 calls the intended practice.

lens.impact: A user who follows the help's own recommended clustering (cluster below i) and the fallback the help and the runtime caution both name (impvalues) gets a 95% confidence interval roughly ten times too short — the standard error is ~4.7x too small on this geometry and the t reference is 44 df instead of 2 — on every row of the table including the pre-trend rows, which turn spuriously significant, with no caution, no guard and no help sentence anywhere.

title: contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) silently gains a baseline dose control on the customvce()/unconditionalse/poisson paths, and the reported ame is arbitrary (sign-flipped on the linear path, driven to zero under poisson)
surface: contreat() + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) with unconditionalse, customvce() or poisson
claim: With contreat() + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero), wooldid inserts the pooled `basic' baseline dose control i.null##c.(ringer) whenever unconditionalse, customvce() or poisson is in force, because the gate at ado:1234 is `strpos(contreatcontrols,"basic") | unconditionalse | customvce() | poisson' with no untreatedZero exclusion, and the untreatedZero branch at ado:1313 rewrites contreatinj but never clears contreatcontrolinserterFE/ABS. Under untreatedZero the dose is exactly 0 off treated cohort-periods, so that pooled column is NOT redundant: it lies in the span of the cell#dose columns, the engine drops one cell slope to compensate, and the reported average marginal effect becomes mean(beta) minus the dose slope of whichever cell the collinearity screen happened to drop. On the absorbing (poisson) path the pooled slope is partialled out first, so the visible cell slopes estimate deviations from it and, under a homogeneous true effect, the reported semi-elasticity is driven to zero regardless of the truth. The default reghdfe path is unaffected and correct, so the same specification returns two different answers depending on an option that ought only to change the variance estimator.
observed: Exact-fit design (dose == 0 on every untreated observation; y = a_i + g_t + kappa_it + beta_it*dose), TRUE ame = mean(beta_it) = 0.9325000000. Reported ame: `robust' (default reghdfe) 0.9325000000 (rel err 5.4e-16); `ccnoabsorb robust' 0.9325000000; `customvce(robust)' -0.1075000000; `customvce(cluster unit)' -0.1075000000; `unconditionalse robust' -0.1075000000 -- all three 111% off and sign-flipped. The arithmetic is exact, not approximate: the cell the engine drops is (i=2, relyr=2) whose true slope is 1.0400000000, and 0.9325 - 1.04 = -0.1075 to every digit (probe24_uz_cautions.log prints both quantities). Poisson twin on an exact-fit log-linear design whose true dose semi-elasticity is 0.20 everywhere: `poisson robust' reports 0.0187049681 (se 0.0752, p 0.803) and `poisson ccnoabsorb robust' the same 0.0187049681 -- the mechanism predicts exactly zero under homogeneous effects and that is what comes back, presented as an insignificant null. What the user sees (probe24 run noisily): on the customvce leg a GENERIC caution, 'a treatment period coefficient interacted with something (likely, a term implementing a continuous treatment variable or an interactive control variable) was dropped for multicollinearity ... This could imply your results are not identified, depending on exactly what was dropped', and then the row `ame = -.1075, se = 3.216e-14, t = -3.3e+12, p = 0.000'; on the poisson leg the ppmlhdfe rc-3200 fallback caution plus the same generic one; on the default reghdfe leg no caution at all and the correct 0.9325.
expected: untreatedZero must take the same control set on every engine: none. ado:1311-1313 states the design ('if always zero when not treated, the only thing to do is not control for anything!') and sthlp:995 says untreatedZero 'cannot be paired with any other type', so the user cannot even ask for the control that gets inserted. The expectation holds because the exact-fit design makes the truth computable in closed form and because the default reghdfe path -- the same specification, same data, only the variance estimator differs -- returns that truth to 5e-16. A point estimate that moves by 111% and flips sign when the user switches from robust to customvce(cluster unit) cannot be right on both paths. The poisson case is the canonical untreatedZero use (a count outcome with an intensity that is zero before treatment, which is sthlp:1551's own worked example), so the wrong answer sits on the option's main intended application.
refuter_note: The claim is right and the arithmetic identity reproduces exactly on independent data, but two things need correcting. (1) SCOPE, upward: the defect is not confined to the ame row. R8 shows the ATT row is corrupted too: DGP true ATT 2.5494633489, default path 2.6743762849 (se 0.180, 0.7 sigma), customvce(robust) and unconditionalse robust both -0.5331814282 (se 0.633) = 4.9 sigma off and sign-flipped. The headline treatment effect moves, not just the marginal-effect row. (2) POISSON MECHANISM: the claim that 'the pooled slope is partialled out first, so the visible cell slopes estimate deviations from it and the reported semi-elasticity is driven to zero regardless of the truth' is wrong. What actually happens (R2, R9) is that ppmlhdfe fails r(3200) on wooldid's OWN one-level absorbed term i.<null>##c.(ringer) and the rc-3200 fallback moves the control into the main equation, where the identical collinearity-drop mechanism as the reg path applies. On a heterogeneous-effect poisson DGP wooldid returns -0.5506611369, which equals my ORACLE-POIS B (-0.5506611369) exactly, against ORACLE-POIS A 0.0454169223 and DGP truth 0.1587 - not zero. 'Driven to zero' is only the homogeneous-effect special case. Also worth noting for the author: the prober's se of 3.2e-14 was an artifact of their exact fit; on noisy data the wrong answer carries an entirely ordinary-looking standard error, which makes the defect LESS visible in practice, not more. Nothing rescues the user because sthlp:906 states the structural-zero ame screen is deliberately not armed under untreatedZero.
refuter_did: Built my own NOISY panel (6 cohort groups x 12 units x 10 periods, 3 never-treated groups, dose==0 off treated cohort-periods, heterogeneous beta_it, N(0,0.5) noise) instead of the prober's exact-fit design, and built two OLS oracles by hand outside wooldid: ORACLE A = reghdfe y ib0.cell ib0.cell#c.dose, absorb(i.i i.t) (the model ado:1311-1315 says untreatedZero is supposed to fit) and ORACLE B = reg y i.i i.t c.dose ib0.cell ib0.cell#c.dose (the same model with the pooled baseline dose slope pasted in front, as the reg path builds it). Results: ORACLE A ame = 1.0162389082; ORACLE B ame = -0.6495711425; the pooled dose slope in ORACLE B is 1.6658100507, which is EXACTLY ORACLE A's slope for the cell the collinearity screen drops (cell 15), and ORACLE_A_ame - b_dropped = -0.6495711425 to every digit. wooldid `robust', `ccnoabsorb robust' and `cluster(unit)' all return 1.0162389082 (== ORACLE A); wooldid `customvce(robust)', `customvce(cluster unit)' and `unconditionalse robust' all return -0.6495711425 (== ORACLE B). DGP truth 0.916, customvce se 0.29-0.32, so the wrong answer is ~5 sigma off with the sign flipped. In R8 I then checked the ATT row, which the prober never measured. In R9 I isolated the poisson mechanism with two controls.

lens.impact: An applied user running the help file's own untreatedZero poisson example, or switching from `robust` to `customvce()`/`unconditionalse` on the same linear model, gets a headline ATT and a dose marginal effect that are wrong by roughly the entire dose contribution — sign-flipped, or reported as a clean null with an ordinary-looking standard error and p-value. On the poisson path there is no correct path at all: the gate fires on the `poisson` option alone, so even a wary user cannot obtain the right number from wooldid.

title: contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) is silently ignored on every non-reghdfe estimation path: customvce(), unconditionalse and poisson estimate the contreatcontrols(basic) model instead
surface: contreat() + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) combined with customvce(), unconditionalse, or poisson; ado:1234 vs ado:1313
claim: With contreat() + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero), any run that leaves the reghdfe path -- customvce(anything), unconditionalse, or poisson -- returns the contreatcontrols(basic) point estimates for main_att, main_ame and every post-treatment event-study horizon, with no caution, the same e(N), the same e(r2) and the same e(df_r) as the correct run, and with the pre-treatment rows identical to 10 decimals.
observed: One hospital-year panel, one seed (8640 rows, i=state, dose = hospital exposure x post, true AME = 0.8). An independent hand-built saturated regression implementing untreatedZero's own documented equation (sthlp:997) gives ame 0.9127941639, att(dose-zero intercept) -0.1141627684. DEFAULT path + untreatedZero: main_ame 0.9127941639 (matches the oracle to 10 dp), main_att 0.8064147779. robust (still reghdfe): identical. customvce(ols) / customvce(robust) / customvce(cluster hid) / unconditionalse cluster(hid), all + untreatedZero: main_ame 0.4766147418, main_att 0.3661964684. DEFAULT path + contreatcontrols(basic): main_ame 0.4766147418, main_att 0.3661964684 -- the same numbers. VERDICT_cv_equals_BASIC_ame=1, VERDICT_cv_equals_BASIC_att=1, VERDICT_un_equals_BASIC_ame=1 (reldif<1e-9). VERDICT_same_N=1 (8640), VERDICT_same_r2=1 (0.236832847), VERDICT_same_dfr=1. Every post-treatment ES horizon moves with them (e.g. ES_att_post0 0.8093214015 -> 0.3672012341; ES_ame_post0 0.8568093277 -> 0.4206299056) while ES_att_pre4/pre3/pre2 are byte-identical across paths. Ratios here 0.522 (ame) and 0.454 (att); NOT a fixed shrinkage -- on a differently-seeded draw of the same design the regress path returned main_ame = -0.3095 (r4_boot.log section E), the wrong sign relative to the known truth of +0.8 (that draw's DEFAULT comparator was not run, so the flip is against the truth, not against a measured default). Controls that hold: binary treatment agrees across the two paths exactly (VERDICT_binary_paths_agree=1); a dose nonzero in every period with contreatcontrols(basic) agrees across the two paths exactly (r6_customvce.log section 4). Poisson: poisson+untreatedZero and poisson+basic return identical numbers (att .02056812, ame .02649715); scope honestly -- both poisson runs printed 'initial estimation of ppmlhdfe failed' and took the rc-3200 explicit-regressor fallback, so that equality is measured on the fallback, the ppmlhdfe-absorb path is code-implied by the same ado:1234 condition but unmeasured, and no poisson oracle was built. CAUSE, read in the code: ado:1234 inserts the pooled baseline dose control whenever strpos(contreatcontrols,'basic') | unconditionalse | customvce() | poisson -- its own comment says it is there to manipulate reg and poisson's collinearity drop rules for the basic-type controls -- while the untreatedZero branch at ado:1313 rewrites only `contreatinj' (its comment: untreatedZero works by 'just not having contreatcontrols of any kind') and never clears `contreatcontrolinserterFE'/`ABS'. Under an exposure x post dose the reinserted baseline slope is exactly collinear with the treated-cell dose terms, so the FIT is unchanged (identical r2/rss/df) while the ame/att decomposition is not.
expected: customvce() is documented as a variance switch only (sthlp:270-273: 'passes the user specified text without modification into the vce() option'; sthlp:264 documents only a fixed-effect-nesting df divergence between the paths). unconditionalse is documented as changing the variance and the estimation command, not the model. Nothing in the help says contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) means something different on those paths, and untreatedZero's own entry (sthlp:995-997) defines the model as the saturated equation with NO g(f(contreat)) term -- which is exactly what my oracle implements and exactly what the default path reproduces. A point estimate must not depend on which solver computes the same specification.

title: The ruled subgroup-degeneracy guard misses on ordinary ragged panels, and wooldid then prints a subgroup-contrast p of 0.000 where the truth is 0.25
surface: subgroups() + cluster() at or above i, analytic path (wooldid_sgdeg ado:11092); it also sets the boottstat studentization denominator for the contrasts
claim: On a staggered panel with holes in it (some (unit,year) rows missing, varying units per cluster), with i = state, cluster(state) and subgroups(), the analytic pairwise-contrast standard error wooldid prints is 4x to 15x smaller than the same contrast's bootstrap and robust standard errors and than its own realized sampling SD, and wooldid_sgdeg's ruled tolerance of 1 - 1e-2 does not fire, so the row and the across-subgroup equality test print with no caution -- producing a false 'these subgroups differ, p < 0.000001' with a confidence interval an order of magnitude too narrow.
observed: repro_sk01_sgcontrast.do (20 states, 2-5 units each, 10 years, 8 percent of rows dropped at random, 640 obs): ANALYTIC cluster(state) b=-0.32158562 se=0.0258871171 t=-12.423 p=0.0000000, implied rho=0.978609958, e(wdid_sgdegenact)=NONE, and the run prints 'p-value for joint test that all SGs have the same att: 0.0000'. BOOTSTRAP(standard) reps(399) on the SAME data and cluster: se=0.310519665 t=-1.036 p=0.250627. ROBUST: se=0.273380161 p=0.240035. SK01_SE_RATIO_boot_over_analytic=11.9951, SK01_FAIL=1. Sweep over 8 independent ragged designs (r07_sgdegsweep.log, G=20/30, T=8/10, 8 or 15 percent rows dropped, 2 contrast rows each): 8 of 16 rows blanked correctly, 8 of 16 LEAKED, and on every leaked row the analytic SE is 4.1x-14.5x below BOTH oracles (cell1R1 .01466/.21269/.29610 ana p .0104; cell3R1 .02589/.31570/.27338 ana p .000000000; cell3R2 .03302/.28022/.33143 ana p 4.5e-5; cell5R1 .02439/.31278/.25676 ana p .000000000; cell6R2 .02788/.27920/.29694 ana p 1.2e-7; rho 0.9137-0.9895, none flagged). 5 of the 8 reject at 5 percent, 3 print p <= 5e-5. Independent oracle needing no other VCE: across the 8 cells the realized main-att contrast estimates are {.0417,.2562,-.3216,.2640,.4102,.0263,.2734,.0929}, sample SD 0.226, against leaked analytic SEs averaging 0.028.
expected: wooldid_sgdeg (ado:11092, author ruling BS-15) exists precisely to withhold a pairwise contrast whose standard error is 'cancellation residue rather than an estimated variance', and the help promises inference here is either valid or withheld. Its own source comment anticipates this exact failure -- 'A cut at 1 - 1e-3, tried first, caught the main row and left the pretreatment row reporting a contrast standard error twenty times too small, which is the defect the ruling names. The cut is a judgment call on a number the ruling did not fix; it lives in ONE local below so it can be moved.' The oracle is the remedy wooldid's own caution names for this design (bootstrap() WITHOUT boottstat, same cluster()), corroborated by robust and by an independent 8-draw Monte-Carlo SD of the statistic itself. This is NOT known_bydesign section 1: if it were section 1's 0.66-0.75 understatement, the level SE and the contrast SE would be understated by the same factor, and on the same run they differ by six times -- the level SE is 0.55 of its robust counterpart while the contrast SE is 0.09 of its own.

title: semielasticity divides the effect by a prediction that excludes the absorbed unit and time fixed effects, so the default engine and the explicit-dummy engine silently disagree by 65%
surface: semielasticity (default reghdfe engine); by extension contreatelasticitytype(eydx)/(eyex), event-study horizons, subgroup rows, histogramcohorteffects, makecfxplots
claim: wooldid's default engine is reghdfe with absorb(i.i i.t), so the fixed effects are not in e(b) and predict,xb returns _cons+Xb without them. margins, eydx(targetflag) averages ln(yhat|tf=1)-ln(yhat|tf=0), so on the default path the reported semi-elasticity measures the treatment effect against the sample GRAND MEAN rather than against each observation's own predicted outcome. The identical model estimated with explicit i.i/i.t dummies (customvce() or unconditionalse, ado:1484-1485) divides by the true fitted value and returns a different number. Nothing warns the user. Falsifiable: run the same data both ways; the dydx (level) answers must agree bit-for-bit while the eydx answers differ, and the difference must vanish when unit levels are made homogeneous.
observed: ARM1 (30 units, y in ~10..230, constant level effect of 5, no calendar trend): LEVEL reghdfe=5.198696458 explicit=5.198696458 ratio=1.000000; SEMIEL reghdfe=0.048760539 explicit=0.080343215 ratio=1.647710. ARM2 (control, every unit at the same level): SEMIEL ratio=1.002512. A third arm, unconditionalse robust, returns 0.080343215 and 0.039776647 -- identical to customvce(robust) on both arms (repro_semielas_fe.log:309,495). Mechanism, computed by hand on the same fit: CORR(reghdfe xb, true fitted value) = -0.001479; SD(reghdfe xb|post)=1.77908 vs SD(true fitted|post)=56.88270; mean[ln(xb_hdfe)-ln(xb_hdfe-b)] = 0.048760539 reproduces the DEFAULT answer and mean[ln(yhat)-ln(yhat-b)] = 0.080343215 reproduces the EXPLICIT answer. A second, independently generated design (dataE, esprelength(3) espostlength(4)) splits by a factor of 1.414 (0.036668142715654 vs 0.051863777168292). MEASURED reach: main_att, pretreatment_att, every ES horizon, and every subgroup row (resH1.csv vs resH2.csv) -- ratios 0.15 to 6.95 including THREE pre-treatment coefficients that CHANGE SIGN with the engine (ES_att_pre2, ES_att_SG0_pre2, ES_att_SG1_pre2); also att_it (run7.log:213-276). The only message a default semielasticity run prints is the cell-collapse caution, whose text reads 'the run is slower, and no answer changes'. INFERRED but not run: histogramcohorteffects and makecfxplots consume the same margins call. Contrast that proves the mechanism: ppmlhdfe IS called with `d` (ado:1462,1468) and the poisson family agrees across engines to ~1e-9 with and without semielasticity (run5.log:2023-2247).
expected: The two engines estimate the same model, so every reported quantity must agree. The level (dydx) answers do agree to ratio 1.000000 exactly because the fixed effects cancel in a difference; eydx divides by the prediction so they do not cancel, and the explicit-dummy arm is the correct one because its denominator IS the fitted outcome, which is what sthlp:243-245 promises ('the average percentage change ... between the two sets of predicted outcomes'). The author already knew margins needs the whole prediction: ado:1459 states 'ppmlhdfe requires d for predict, which margins requires' and passes `d` to ppmlhdfe but not to reghdfe (ado:1476). Under plain dydx that omission is harmless, which is why it survived. This is HIGH rather than medium because the pre-trend diagnostic is engine-dependent in DIRECTION, not only magnitude.
refuter_did: Built my own DGP from the claim's terms (40 units, 10 periods, UNIT-LEVEL intercepts alpha_i=60+2*(i-20), calendar trend, staggered onset t=4/t=7, level effect 8, sigma 1) and ran four arms. LEVEL: default 8.219294310 (+1.070475805f158X+003) vs customvce(robust) 8.219294310 (+1.070475805f170X+003) -- agree to 2 ulp. SEMIELASTICITY: default 0.116514051 vs explicit 0.162023562, ratio 0.7191. HOMOGENEOUS-LEVEL CONTROL ARM: 0.125533755 vs 0.125907468, ratio 0.99703 -- the gap collapses exactly as the claim predicts. Second independent seed (pA_semielas.log): level 7.885943102 both sides, eydx 0.111828326 vs 0.155101018 (ratio 0.7210), control 0.99777. MECHANISM PROVED WITHOUT WOOLDID: reghdfe y post, absorb(i.i i.t) + margins,eydx(post) vs reg y i.i i.t post + margins,eydx(post) on the same data gives dydx ratio EXACTLY 1.000000000 (8.216934249 both) and eydx 0.118799295 vs 0.133531105; corr(reghdfe prediction, true fitted value) = -0.354195138; SD 3.94 vs 21.64; and the hand oracles mean(b/xb_hdfe)=0.118799295 and mean(b/xb_full)=0.133531105 reproduce the two margins answers to 9 dp. Independent arithmetic check on the pA design: mean(y)=69.36, mean(post)=0.3575 so reghdfe's _cons=66.5 and ln(74.5/66.5)=0.1136, which is the 0.1118 the default arm reports -- the effect is measured against the sample GRAND MEAN. Also verified the only printed message is the cell-collapse caution whose text ends 'the run is slower, and no answer changes'. EXTENSION I MEASURED that the seeded finding only inferred: contreatelasticitytype on a 30-unit continuous-treatment panel -- dydx ame 1.972616603 on BOTH engines (ratio 1.000000), eydx 0.020997076 vs 0.027770557 (0.7561), eyex 0.051142250 vs 0.067165897 (0.7614). Exactly the ey* operators split. I also checked review_process/ and wooldid_ado_review.md for eydx/semielas/xbd/predict-near-reghdfe: the only prior record is the poisson xb-scale remap BS-6; the absorbed-FE issue on the linear path is nowhere on record.

lens.lens: INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION — rebuilt the case a third time from the claim alone, with my own DGP and one test neither predecessor ran
lens.impact: A user who asks for `semielasticity` on wooldid's default (reghdfe) engine gets a number whose denominator is a sample-level constant — reghdfe's _cons plus the cell effects — instead of each observation's fitted outcome, because the absorbed unit and time fixed effects are not in e(b) and so are missing from `predict, xb`. The resulting error is design-dependent in both size and sign (def/exp ratios measured from 0.607 to 1.023 across three independent designs), needs only a calendar trend to appear at all, propagates to every event-study horizon and subgroup row, and can flip the sign of a pre-treatment coefficient — turning the pre-trend diagnostic that justifies the whole design into an artifact of whether the fixed effects were absorbed or written as dummies. Nothing warns the user; the one message printed says "no answer changes." Reporting the same model two defensible ways gives two different published semi-elasticities, and neither is the quantity the help file promises.

title: The bootstrap's two-regime unit rule is a single GLOBAL flag on a PER-UNIT property: one straddling unit out of 96 cuts the att_i bootstrap SE by 20-29%, silently
surface: bootstrap(standard) + cluster() + att_i / att_it / att_itime (the physical re-identification leg, ado:8986-8995 and 9346-9349)
claim: ado:8991 (`cap assert wdbcmin == wdbcmax if smp`) reduces a per-unit nesting property to one all-or-nothing flag, so a single unit that straddles two clusters puts EVERY unit under the keep-i rule -- the rule the code's own comment at ado:9331-9334 says 'collaps[es] the composition variance of att_i toward zero'. The bootstrap standard error of att_i/att_it/att_itime therefore falls 20-29% on a one-unit data change, with no message, no caution and no e() record.
observed: p08_dose.do (24 industries x 4 firms, T=8, i=firm, cluster(ind), reps(120), rseed(8081)); k = number of firms reclassified into a neighbouring industry halfway through the panel. k=0 PREDNEST=1 se(att)=0.13112922202932 se(att_i)=0.13203513225887; k=1 PREDNEST=0 se(att)=0.13248661337362 se(att_i)=0.10490369831254; k=5 se(att)=0.13620837148465 se(att_i)=0.10527886564326; k=20 se(att)=0.12888153528240 se(att_i)=0.10489112931816. se(att_i) steps down at k=1 and is then FLAT to three decimals (0.10490 / 0.10528 / 0.10489): one straddler out of 96 buys the whole effect and the next nineteen buy nothing. Independently at reps(300)/rseed(4242) (p04_regime_measure.do): A (k=0) 0.14110902275043, B (k=1) 0.10057797358284, ratio 0.713; identical point estimate 1.01724741722359, identical N=768, identical e(N_clust)=24. Direction tell: on the same A->B change the ANALYTIC clustered SE went UP 10% (0.04087189780308 -> 0.04498845544402), which is the sensible response to reassigning four rows; the bootstrap went DOWN 29%.
expected: Approximately A's / k=0's value. Ninety-five of the ninety-six firms still nest wholly inside one industry, and for them the re-identification rule is the one the package itself says is correct: ado:9326-9334 states that under nesting `group(__wdbns, i)` is 'what makes a twice-drawn cluster's cells count twice in the equal-cell weighting', and that keeping i there 'would make a twice-drawn cluster's cells identical duplicates that the equal-cell weighting counts ONCE, collapsing the composition variance of att_i toward zero'. An independent hand-rolled pairs-cluster bootstrap confirms both arms: ORACLE_NEST SD 0.1317, ORACLE_KEEP SD 0.1026 (p04_regime_measure.do, 300 draws, seed 90210). Arithmetically the keep-i rule replaces each cluster's Poisson(1) multiplicity (variance 1) with a Bernoulli(1-1/e) indicator (variance 0.2325), so the composition component of Var(att_i) is cut ~4.3x; the SE ratio tends to sqrt(0.2325)=0.482 as that component dominates. Taking the nesting arm as calibrated, a nominal 5% test on the reported keep-i SE rejects about 16% of the time (2*Phi(-1.96*0.713)); that implication is conditional on the nesting arm itself being calibrated, which this probe did not establish.
refuter_note: Two corrections, neither of which touches the claim itself. (1) THE ARITHMETIC IS WRONG. The claim gives the limiting SE ratio as sqrt(0.2325)=0.482 (Bernoulli(1-1/e) variance over Poisson(1) variance). That drops the renormalisation: under keep-i a twice-drawn cluster contributes identical cells that the equal-cell weighting counts once, so the replication statistic is sum(I_c*thetabar_c)/sum(I_c), a ratio over the REALIZED number of included clusters, with variance sigma^2(1-p)/(pG) against sigma^2/G. The limit is sqrt(0.3679/0.6321)=0.763. Measured 0.766 (my dose) and 0.765 (my isolation); the claim's own 0.713 brackets it from below. 0.482 describes nothing either of us saw. The implied size of a nominal 5% test is therefore 13.3%, not the claimed ~16%. (2) NOT A DOC-VS-CODE DIVERGENCE. sthlp:532 states the rule as a property of where cluster() sits relative to i -- 'where the cluster is finer than i, OR CUTS ACROSS IT' -- and one straddling unit does make the two partitions cross-cutting, so the code does what the help says. This is a design defect (a per-unit property collapsed into one global flag, resolving the trade-off the wrong way when 95 of 96 units nest), not a documentation mismatch. Also: known_bydesign section 7's 'bootstrap(standard) at cluster()==i OVER-covers' does not rescue the keep-i number here -- at cluster()==i, group(drawid,i) degenerates to the drawn id and the composition object is a different one.
refuter_did: Built my own DGP (24 counties x 4 plants, T=8, i=plant, cluster(county) COARSER than i, county-level and plant-level effect heterogeneity) in which `county` enters the command ONLY through cluster(), so reassigning a plant cannot move the point estimate. Dose k=0/1/8/24 straddlers at reps(250), identical rseed: b(att_i) bit-identical at every k (+1.10f479964ed18X+000); PREDNEST 1/0/0/0; se(att_i) 0.12595 / 0.09646 / 0.09760 / 0.09411 while se(att) rises 0.12820 / 0.12844 / 0.13545 / 0.13773. One straddler out of 96 costs 23.4%; the next 23 buy nothing. I did not take either arm on faith: (a) a hand-rolled pairs-cluster bootstrap run entirely OUTSIDE wooldid's engine (draw 24 counties with replacement, joinby, then `wooldid ... fastnose`, 250 draws) gives ORACLE_NEST 0.12717 and ORACLE_KEEP 0.09632 against wooldid's 0.12570 / 0.09616, so wooldid implements BOTH rules faithfully and only the choice is wrong; (b) this dataset's 24 county means of the plant-level effects have SD 0.5950, so the between-county component is 0.5950/sqrt(24)=0.1215 and with estimation noise 0.049 the pairs bootstrap should land near 0.131 -- the nesting arm does, the keep-i arm is ~21% below it; (c) a 400-dataset Monte Carlo gives SD(att_i - superpopulation ATT)=0.1797 and SD(att_i - own-sample mean)=0.0491, confirming the bootstrap is conditional on the sample. The decisive argument is structural rather than calibrational: under a cluster coarser than i every cell lies wholly inside one cluster, so duplicating a cluster cannot move a cell mean and keep-i can only REMOVE variance -- always anti-conservative. Separately measured (r05) that the keep-i rule IS calibrated where the cluster is genuinely finer than i, which sharpens rather than softens the claim.

title: The regime predicate is evaluated on `smp`, which is NOT the estimation sample, so cluster values on rows the regression never sees change the reported att_i bootstrap SE by 25-30%
surface: bootstrap(standard) + cluster() + att_i / att_it / att_itime; the sample concept at ado:8911-8924 feeding the regime detection at ado:8986-8995
claim: `smp` (ado:8911-8924) is ((if)==1) & !missing(clustervar) and nothing else -- no markout for missing y, missing controls(), missing dose or zero weights -- yet it is the sample the nesting predicate is computed on (ado:8989-8991). e(sample) is a strict subset of smp, so the misdetection is one-directional: it can only report keep-i where the estimation sample nests, and that direction understates. The code comment at ado:8975-8985 claims the `if smp` placement handles exactly this case ('a cluster that nests i within the sample but straddles two i's only through rows the sample excludes would be misclassified as non-nesting'); it does not. sthlp:532 likewise says 'Where the cluster nests i, each drawn copy of a cluster becomes a fresh set of units' -- in the repro the cluster DOES nest i on the estimation sample and the copies do not become fresh units, so this is a documented-vs-actual divergence on top of a wrong number.
observed: Two datasets identical wherever the estimator looks. C0: firm 1's outcome is missing from 2005 on. C: the same, and firm 1's industry code changes on exactly those missing-outcome rows. Both N=764, both att_i = 1.01054627838245 to every digit, both analytic clustered se = 0.04030370871346, both e(N_clust)=24. Regime: NEST on smp = 0, NEST on e(sample) = 1; rows in e(sample) but not in smp = 0; rows in smp but not in e(sample) = 4. wooldid's bootstrap SE of att_i (p04_regime_measure.do, reps(300), rseed(4242)): C0 = 0.14122699826312, C = 0.10043761347134, ratio 0.7112. DECISIVE CONTROL (p06_estimand_split.do, reps(120), rseed(31337), all four estimands in one run): main_att = 0.12587695969826 in BOTH runs, BIT-IDENTICAL, so the two runs saw the same cluster draws and the observation-weighted estimand is untouched; main_att_it 0.12587695969826 -> 0.09632508066525, main_att_i and main_att_itime 0.12579454738696 -> 0.09837740349041. The same phantom fires through a missing CONTROL, not just a missing outcome (p02_edges.do T9/T9B, controls(x)): 0.13822686104741 -> 0.10399078061065, ratio 0.752, same N=764 and same point estimate. By contrast a missing CLUSTER value produces no phantom (T6, 0.13549772259762, nesting arm) -- the one markout the screen does implement is the one that could not have produced a phantom anyway. repro_FCM2.do printed its whole setup block live but its two reps(200) bootstraps had not completed at write-up (14-19 competing Stata processes on a 10-core box); its bootstrap lines are the same code that produced p04's completed reps(300) numbers.
expected: Identical to C0. Nesting is not merely the design's stated intent here, it is actually correct on C's data: the four phantom rows drawn under industry 2 would receive their own `group(__wdbns, firm)` code, carry a missing outcome, and be dropped by the replication's own markout, so re-identification changes nothing for them and restores the correct rule for the 95 firms that nest. The independent oracle brackets both arms (ORACLE_NEST SD 0.1317, ORACLE_KEEP SD 0.1026).
refuter_note: One sub-claim is an overread, and the door list is wider than stated. OVERREAD: the claim says the code comment at ado:8975-8985 'claims the `if smp` placement handles exactly this case; it does not.' That comment says the smp placement beats evaluating on the RAW FRAME, which is true; it never claims smp is the estimation sample. The genuine documented-vs-actual divergence is with sthlp:532 ('Where the cluster nests i, each drawn copy of a cluster becomes a fresh set of units') -- on arm B's estimation sample the cluster does nest i and the copies do not become fresh units. That part stands. WIDER: a MISSING WEIGHT opens the same door, which the original claim did not test -- [aw=wt] with wt missing on the phantom rows moves se(att_i) 0.12638 -> 0.10528 with se(att) bit-identical (r04_record_df.log, WMB0/WMB1; also in repro_FCM2.do as DOOR 2). So the doors are: missing outcome, missing control (the prober's) and missing/zero weight (mine). A MISSING i is NOT a door -- gegen ... by(i) puts the missing-i rows in a group of their own, so the predicate still sees nesting (r00_struct.log, D5_PRED=1).
refuter_did: Built the isolation on my own data. Arm A: plant 1 shuts down, y missing from 2005 on. Arm B: identical, plus the registry records it in county 2 on exactly those already-excluded rows. Both N=764; b(att) and b(att_i) identical to every hex digit (+1.14de160001d06X+000 / +1.118bfbe772b97X+000); analytic clustered SEs identical to every hex digit; e(N_clust)=24 both. Regime: NEST computed over all rows A=1 B=0; NEST computed over the rows with a non-missing outcome A=1 B=1. Bootstrap at reps(250), same rseed: se(att) identical to 3 ulps (so the two runs saw the same cluster draws), while se(att_i) and se(att_itime) fall 0.12570 -> 0.09616 and se(att_it) 0.12859 -> 0.09839. I also verified the one-directionality analytically: e(sample) is a subset of smp by construction, so straddling on e(sample) implies straddling on smp, and the misdetection can only run toward keep-i, i.e. toward the smaller SE. I then probed the door list further than the original claim did.

lens.impact: On a bootstrap(standard) run with cluster() and a cell-weighted estimand (att_i / att_it / att_itime, or boottstat + cluster()), a single stray row outside the estimation sample can silently rescale EVERY reported bootstrap standard error in the run by ~0.71 — anti-conservative, one-directional, with no message, no caution, and no e() record of which rule was used. In my run one firm's four missing-outcome rows carrying a changed industry code moved se(att_i) from 0.14074 to 0.09955 (-29.3%) for all 96 firms, while the point estimate, the analytic clustered SE, N, and e(N_clust) were bit-identical. The user's confidence interval narrows by 29% and they have no way to see it happened. The trigger is narrow but real: a within-unit change in the cluster variable confined to rows the estimator drops for missing outcome, missing controls(), or missing/zero weight — the administrative pattern of a plant acquired, relocated or re-coded at the moment it stops reporting.

title: A cluster with no rows in e(sample) is still a resampling unit and still sets bootdf(clusters), leaving e(df_r) inconsistent with e(N_clust)
surface: bootstrap() + cluster() + bootdf(clusters); the map-frame cluster count at ado:8946-8957
claim: `wdb_C` (ado:8954), the resampling-cluster count that becomes bootdf(clusters)'s G, is counted on `smp`, which does not markout missing outcomes. A cluster whose rows are all dropped by the estimator is therefore still drawn (and contributes nothing when it is), and e(df_r) = wdb_C - 1 disagrees with the documented G-1 rule read off the posted e(N_clust).
observed: p11_finer.do block F (i=cgrp, 12 cohort groups of 8 firms, cluster(firm)=96, the eight firms of cohort group 1 have no outcome at all): plain run N=704 e(N_clust)=88; bootstrap run with bootdf(clusters) N=704 e(N_clust)=88 e(df_r)=95, printed as 'e(N_clust)-1 = 87 vs e(df_r) = 95'. Smaller version in p02_edges.do T10 (one dead industry out of 24): N=736 e(N_clust)=23 e(df_r)=23 where the stated rule gives 22. Eight of ninety-six resampling units in the p11 case contribute nothing to any replication. NOT MEASURED: what those wasted draws do to the standard error itself; only the df inconsistency and the wasted-draw count were established.
expected: G should be the number of clusters in the estimation sample. sthlp:532 documents bootdf(clusters) as 't with G-1 degrees of freedom ... G being the number of resampling clusters', and the posted e(N_clust) is the only cluster count a user can see, so e(df_r) should be e(N_clust)-1.
refuter_note: FRAMING: the claim calls this a documented-vs-actual divergence, and it is not. sthlp:532 documents bootdf(clusters) as 't with G-1 degrees of freedom, G being the number of RESAMPLING clusters', and under this code a dead cluster IS a resampling cluster, so help and code are self-consistent on their own terms. The defect is that a cluster contributing nothing to any replication is a resampling unit at all, and that the only cluster count a user can see -- the printed header and e(N_clust) -- contradicts e(df_r) in the same output. SEVERITY UP from medium to high on the strength of the many-dead-cluster case (t(19) for t(4), a 25%-too-narrow wald interval on a default-resolved bootdf), with the boundary stated honestly: the DEFAULT bootdisplay(percentile) table is rank-based and unaffected by the df. THE UNMEASURED ITEM, MEASURED: the wasted draws DO move the SE. 500 reps, three seeds, se(att_i) padded vs dropped: 0.40684/0.41155 (0.989), 0.44773/0.39996 (1.119), 0.47193/0.40140 (1.176), mean ratio 1.094; and the padded arm's across-seed spread is 16% against the clean arm's 3%. Mechanism: drawing 20 slots when only 5 can contribute makes a replication's live-cluster count Binomial(20,.25) instead of a fixed 5, which fattens and destabilises the replication distribution and costs 1-2 replications per 500 to draws that catch no live treated cluster. Direction (conservative on the SE, anti-conservative on the df) and the instability are established; the +9% magnitude is indicative only, since a bootstrap SE at 5 live clusters is noisy.
refuter_did: Reproduced the mild case on my own data (one dead county of 24: e(N_clust)=23 while e(df_r)=e(boot_df)=23, where the visible cluster count gives 22; consequence t(23)=2.0687 vs t(22)=2.0739, negligible). Then built the realistic severe case the claim did not: 20 counties in the file, the outcome collected in only 5 of them (an ordinary merged administrative file). wooldid prints 'N clusters = 5; N = 160 (480 obs dropped from initial sample)' and posts e(N_clust)=5 with e(df_r)=e(boot_df)=19. The control with the same estimation sample and the dead rows physically dropped gives identical point estimates (att_i = 1.0836262589 both) and e(df_r)=4. t(19)=2.0930 against t(4)=2.7764: a bootdisplay(wald) interval 25% too narrow (ratio 0.7539), and every consumer the run's own footer names as reading e(V) with e(df_r) -- hand test/lincom, esttab, coefplot, honestdid -- inherits the wrong reference. Confirmed that bootdf(clusters) is the DEFAULT whenever cluster() is given (ado:423; my r04 NESTRUN/KEEPRUN passed no bootdf() and still show boot_df=23), so this is not a two-opt-in corner. Finally measured the claim's own 'NOT MEASURED' item at 500 reps x 3 seeds.

lens.lens: REALISM AND IMPACT — how likely is a real applied economist to hit this, what exactly do they lose, and would they notice
lens.impact: An applied economist merges an outcome or a covariate with partial coverage onto a panel — or simply has a cluster emptied by reghdfe's singleton drop — clusters at state/industry/region level, and runs the ordinary `cluster(c) bootstrap(standard) reps(n)` call with no further options. wooldid prints the correct live cluster count in its header, posts the correct value in e(df_r_analytic), and then posts e(df_r) = (clusters in the FILE) - 1 instead of (clusters in the ESTIMATION SAMPLE) - 1. The direction is split and that split is the precise loss: the printed default (percentile) table is unaffected and in fact slightly conservative (my 4-live-cluster arm prints [.607, 1.279] against the control's [.664, 1.279], the SE inflation acting alone), so the front page of the paper is safe; but every number that leaves through e(V) + e(df_r) is anti-conservative. That is the path wooldid's own footer names: a hand `test` or `lincom` (verified: t(23) where the estimation sample has 4 clusters and 3 residual df), and esttab, coefplot and honestdid exports. Under the bootdisplay(wald) opt-in the printed p and CI are wrong directly. In the common mid case (say 51 states in the file, an administrative series covering 12) a "95%" exported interval really covers about 93%; in the small-G case (4-6 live of 24) about 87-91%, roughly 20-35% too narrow before the offsetting SE inflation, and in exactly that case both few-cluster cautions — including the MacKinnon-Webb few-treated-cluster warning — are silently withheld. Nothing errors and nothing warns; the only visible trace is the run's own footer announcing "referred to the t(23) distribution" three lines under "N clusters = 4", which a careful reader could catch and almost no one will.

title: A partially-missing subgroup variable silently turns subgroup att_i / att_itime into a share-weighted average
surface: subgroups() x att_i / att_itime x missing subgroup values
claim: When the subgroups() variable is missing on only SOME of a unit's rows (item nonresponse: the unit's subgroup is known in some years and not others), wooldid accepts the run with no error and no caution, and the subgroup att_i / att_itime it reports are NOT the equal-unit averages those estimands are defined to be. The unit enters its own subgroup weighted by the share of its post-treatment sample weight on which the subgroup happens to be observed. wooldid REFUSES (r459, default safety) the adjacent case -- a unit whose subgroup value CHANGES over time -- and its own error text names exactly this distortion as the reason: 'att_i and att_itime enter a split unit into each subgroup weighted by its share of sample weight there, rather than with the equal unit weighting those estimands normally imply'. The missing-value case reaches the same place unguarded and undocumented. Mechanism: w_att_i = w/(total post weight of i) is built once on the whole estimation sample, and margins, over(sg) renormalises within the over-group, so a unit observed in the subgroup on a fraction s of its post rows contributes total weight s instead of 1.
observed: Noiseless design, 5 units in subgroup 1 with unit effects (5,1,1,1,1); unit 1's subgroup value blanked in 5 of its 6 post years. run A (clean sg): att_i(sg==1) = 1.8000000000. run B (sg partly missing): att_i(sg==1) = att_itime(sg==1) = 1.1600000000, which equals the share-weighted figure (s*5+4*1)/(s+4) with s=1/6 to 8.19e-14, and misses the equal-unit definition 1.8 by -0.64. run C (same rows, sg CHANGES 1->0 instead of going missing): r(459), refused, with the text quoted above. No caution of any kind in run B. NOTE att and att_it also read 1.16 in run B and that is CORRECT for them (att_it is 29/25 by cell count, att is the row-weighted mean) -- the coincidence is this design, not evidence they are affected. The discriminating number is run D on NOISY data (y + N(0,0.7)): wooldid reports att_i(sg==1) = 0.9545 where the equal-unit average of the same five units' own e(histogramestimates) effects is 1.7485, a 45% departure. (The exact share-weighted figure there is 0.9486 rather than 0.9545 because unit 1 also contributes only its single in-subgroup cell rather than its 6-period average; the noiseless run B is the exact algebraic check.) Also measured on ordinary noisy gen_core data in p07_stress.do section N7: per-unit weights inside the subgroup run from 0.2 to 1.0, mean 0.707, total 3.53 across 5 units instead of 5.
expected: Either the equal-unit average over the units in the subgroup -- the documented meaning of att_i ('simple mean of cohort-specific effects') and att_itime -- or the same refusal/caution the value-changes-over-time case already gets, since the consequence is identical and wooldid's own error text says so. The help only says 'Observations with missing subgroup values remain allowed and belong to no subgroup', which reads as benign; nothing tells the user their unit has been down-weighted in its own subgroup. The author may instead rule this a documentation gap, but the number under the printed row label is not the estimand that label names.
refuter_note: The claim reproduces exactly and the stated mechanism is right. Two corrections, both of which make it WORSE not better. (a) Their note 'att and att_it also read 1.16 in run B and that is CORRECT for them' is true only because their design has exactly one row per (i,t) cell. With several rows per cell and only some labelled, att_it -- documented as the simple average of cohort-period effects, each CELL equally weighted -- is itself cell-share-weighted: see new finding skp-01, where it reads 7.0 against an equal-cell target of 6.0. (b) Their noisy run D benchmarked against e(histogramestimates), which is the wrong oracle: the margins call that builds the histogram (ado:12405) carries no subgroup term in its subpop, so it averages each unit over ALL its post cells, labelled or not. That is why their 0.9545 did not match their own 0.9486 prediction. The right oracle is e(gteffects), which carries the w_att_i column directly and matches to 4e-16. Severity stays high and sits at the top of high: the trigger needs subgroups() plus item nonresponse on the subgroup variable, but when it fires it is a silently wrong number on realistic input whose reported interval stops covering, and wooldid REFUSES the structurally identical split-unit case with r(459) while saying nothing here.
refuter_did: Built my own designs from the claim's terms; never ran their script. (1) r01: five sg1 units with five DISTINCT effects (1..5) and five DISTINCT observed shares (.125/.25/.5/1/1), so equal-unit=3.0 and share-weighted=3.8695652174 are far apart and the share prediction cannot be hit by accident. Clean run: att_i=att_itime=3.0000000000 (dev -7.1e-15). Missing run: 3.8695652174, dev from SHARE -3.1e-15, error vs equal-unit +29%. sg CHANGES on the same rows: r(459). No caution; header 'N=240 (0 obs dropped)'; e(N_dropped)=0; nothing in a full ereturn list records the lost mass. (2) r02 PART1 identified the MECHANISM, which their equal-period design could not: an UNBALANCED panel separates three candidates -- equal-unit 5.0, share-of-own-post-weight 3.6666666667, row-weighted 3.0. att_i and att_itime land on SHARE (dev 1.3e-15); att and att_it land on ROW. So it is specifically w/(unit's total post weight over the whole estimation sample), exactly as claimed. (3) r04, 90 units, staggered onsets, unbalanced entry/exit, N(0,0.6) noise, oracle built from e(gteffects)'s own w_att_i / w_att_it columns: clean arm reported==share==equal to 4e-16; MCAR 15% gives -0.115 SE (-0.47%); label-stops-being-collected gives -1.468 SE (-7.1%), per-unit weight mass 0.20-1.00 mean 0.292. (4) r05, truth known by construction (sg1 unit effects spread 0.5..5.5 so equal-unit truth is 3; the ten largest-effect units lose the label from relative year 2): 58 of 1260 rows (4.6%) lose their label, nothing about the outcome data changes, and att_i(sg1) goes 3.018843 -> 2.409209 (-20%) while att_i(sg0) stays bit-identical at 0.922207. The reported e(pwsgs) contrast goes 2.09663544 (CI [1.953,2.240], covers truth 2) -> 1.48700193 (CI [1.334,1.640], excludes the truth by 8.3 SE), with no caution. Code corroboration read-only: w_per_i at ado:1621 is gegen total(w*esamp) by(posttreatment i) with no subgroup term; subgroups is deliberately absent from the must-be-non-missing markout list at ado:~703; the F13 split guard at ado:12266-12280 folds missing via cond(sg>=.,.,sg); subgroup margins at ado:2819 use over(subgroups) on the full post subpop. Not covered by known_bydesign.md (its §3 entry is the WITHIN-CELL straddle, which is refused).

lens.lens: INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION — built the case a third time from the claim alone; neither prior agent's script was run or read for design
lens.impact: An applied economist whose classification variable has item nonresponse — one of the most common features of administrative and survey panels — gets a subgroup att_i / att_itime that silently down-weights each unit by the share of its post-treatment sample weight on which the label happens to survive, rather than the equal-unit average the label names and the help documents. In my run, 12 blanked rows out of 540 (2.2%) turned a correctly null subgroup contrast (p = 0.909) into -0.739 at p < 0.001 with a confidence interval excluding the true zero by 8.3 standard errors, on identical outcome data, with no caution printed, nothing in e() recording the lost weight mass, and the header still reading "0 obs dropped". The structurally identical case — a unit whose subgroup value changes over time — is refused r(459) with an error naming exactly this distortion, and reaches a bit-identical number under safety(off), so the user is protected from one route to the wrong figure and not from the other.

title: contreatelasticitytype(eydx)/(eyex) divide by a prediction that omits the absorbed fixed effects on the default reghdfe path, so the reported elasticity is not the quantity the help defines
surface: contreat() + contreatelasticitytype(eydx|eyex) on the default reghdfe path (and the binary semielasticity option)
claim: On wooldid's default estimation path the reported elasticity and semi-elasticity of the continuous treatment are computed as the marginal effect divided by reghdfe's `xb', which excludes every absorbed effect (i.i, i.t, fe(), and the absorbed dose control). The help (sthlp:905-907) defines eyex as '% change in y / % change in contreat' and eydx as '% change in y / unit change in continuous treatment'; the shipped number is instead a percentage of a partialled-out residual index. The cause is that ado:1476 calls reghdfe without any arrangement for the sum of absorbed effects, while the poisson twin at ado:1462/1468 passes `d' to ppmlhdfe with the comment 'ppmlhdfe requires d for predict, which margins requires'. dydx and dyex, which do not divide by the prediction, are unaffected -- which is exactly the pattern measured.
observed: Exact-fit panel, 20 states x 5 counties x 10 periods, staggered onsets, R2 = 1, so E[y|x] == y and the truths are closed form. cluster(unit) [reghdfe] vs customvce(cluster unit) [plain regress] vs truth: dydx 1.320000000000 / 1.320000000000 / 1.320000000000; dyex 2.647372379686 / 2.647372379686 / 2.647372379686; eydx 0.016412789649 / 0.019020203082 / 0.019020203082; eyex 0.032813176169 / 0.038004324224 / 0.038004324224. The reghdfe path is 13.7% too small on both elasticity rows. Graded mechanism test (probe06_eydx_scale.do): scaling the absorbed part of y by s gives eydx relative error 1.8e-09 at s=0 (nothing to absorb -- exact), 1.72e-03 at s=0.1, 1.30e-02 at s=1, 2.48e-02 at s=3. Mechanism reproduced digit-for-digit outside wooldid (probe23_reghdfe_d.log): `reghdfe y ib0.cell##c.dose, absorb(i.i i.t i.nullv##c.ringer) vce(robust)` then `predict, xb` leaves y - xb with mean 0 but sd 17.336133, and `margins, eydx(dose)` on it returns 0.016412789649 -- exactly wooldid's default-path number. A bare `d' is refused by reghdfe 6.12.3 with r(198), so the remedy is savefe/d(newvar) plus a rebuilt prediction, not a one-token copy of the poisson line. Second surface, same mechanism, measured only as a path disagreement: the binary-side `semielasticity' gives robust 0.322104771542 == customvce 0.322104771542 at s=0, then 0.191049620678 vs 0.191768105033 at s=1 and 0.104915119469 vs 0.104942900858 at s=3.
expected: Under an exact fit the conditional mean IS y, so the semi-elasticity is mean(beta_it / y) and the elasticity mean(beta_it * dose / y) over the treated post rows. Both engines fit the identical model to identical data and differ only in how the variance is computed, so a point estimate that moves between them cannot be right on both; the plain-regress value matches the closed form and the reghdfe value does not. The divergence vanishing exactly when there is nothing to absorb (s=0) and growing with the absorbed share of y's level pins the denominator as the cause. Nothing in known_bydesign.md, in the ado comments, or in sthlp:245-249 (which discusses only sparse-y estimation failure and the poisson xb-scale remap) says the linear-path elasticity denominator is the partialled-out index. In real panels the unit fixed effects usually carry most of the level of y, so the error is bounded only by how large the absorbed level is relative to the residual index.
refuter_note: The mechanism and the direction are right; two descriptive corrections. (1) MAGNITUDE: '13.7% too small' is design-specific, not the rate. On ordinary panels I measure 2-4% (R5: 2.4% at four different absorbed-effect dispersions; R5b: 0.0215677240 vs its regress twin at ymean 47, rising to 0.0503237247 at ymean 13). The error is second-order in the dispersion of the absorbed part rather than 'a percentage of a partialled-out residual index' - reghdfe's xb has the SAME MEAN as y, only a shrunken sd - so it is unbounded only when the partial index approaches zero on some rows. (2) The prober's BINARY-semielasticity evidence was self-contradictory (their binary gap SHRANK with their scale knob while their contreat gap GREW, which one shared mechanism cannot produce), but the extension is nonetheless real: on my fixture semielasticity att = 0.087622452771 (robust) vs 0.085833510361 (customvce(robust)), a 2.1% gap of the same size and sign as the contreat-side eydx gap. One thing the prober missed that strengthens the case: ccnoabsorb gives a THIRD elasticity (0.034803487530) from the identical fit, because it moves the ringer into the main equation so it enters xb while i.i and i.t still do not - so the same specification returns three different elasticities depending on options that should only change the variance estimator or the absorption bookkeeping.
refuter_did: First pinned wooldid's exact model spellings outside wooldid (R4): reghdfe y ib0.cell##c.dose, absorb(i.i i.t i.nullv##c.ringer) reproduces the default path to every digit, and reg y i.i i.t i.nullv##c.ringer ib0.cell##c.dose reproduces the customvce path. Then in R3 (rewritten to use those spellings and rerun) I compared dydx, dyex, eydx and eyex across engines, and computed the help's own definition in closed form. dydx is IDENTICAL across engines (1.022234373986 everywhere, wooldid and my oracles) - so the engines fit the same model to the same data and any elasticity gap is purely the denominator. eydx: 0.034876727614 (default/reghdfe) vs 0.034066172921 (customvce/regress) vs 0.034803487530 (ccnoabsorb robust, a THIRD answer). eyex: 0.073136451868 / 0.071262964505 / 0.072724096817. The closed form the help defines - mean over treated post rows of b_cell divided by the FULL prediction - is 0.034066172921 (eydx) and 0.071262964505 (eyex), matching the customvce numbers EXACTLY and not the default-path ones. reghdfe's predict,xb has the same mean as y (27.395972 both) but a smaller sd (1.262981 vs regress 1.943938 vs y 2.626373). R5/R5b swept the magnitude over absorbed-effect dispersion and over E[y].

lens.impact: A user who asks for a semi-elasticity or elasticity on wooldid's default path gets a number that is several percent off the quantity the help defines, and that changes if they move a control between fe() and controls() or switch to customvce() — which the help says only changes the standard errors. The surface is wider than the finding title: `semielasticity` on a plain BINARY staggered-DiD run, with no contreat() at all, is hit by the same mechanism. The headline att and dydx are unaffected, so nothing in the output warns the user, and the error direction is not even fixed — it flips sign with the design.

title: Phantom straddler: a row the estimator discards decides which variance the bootstrap computes
surface: bootstrap(standard) + cluster() + cell-weighted estimand; wooldid_bootrun's `smp` construction
claim: The regime predicate runs on `smp` (ado:8910-8916), which is only the user's `if`(==1) plus a non-missing cluster value, and does NOT screen rows the estimator drops. A unit that carries a second cluster code on a row with a MISSING OUTCOME therefore flips the whole run to the keep-i regime, even though e(sample), the point estimates and the att standard errors are bit-identical to the un-flipped run.
observed: Arms A and D both set y = . for unit 1 at t = 3; arm D additionally records that row under industry 2. reps(199). e(N) = 179 in both. b(att_i) = 2.755071041835752 in both. se(att) = 0.4338581068233801 (A) vs 0.4338581068233803 (D) - identical to 15 significant figures, so the resamples and fits are the same draws. se(att_i) = 0.4348901884075443 (A) -> 0.3308192001858818 (D), a fall of 23.9%; second rseed 0.4724939276687015 -> 0.3655332376168671, 22.6%; second dataset .43498/.47448 -> .33027/.36696.
expected: A row that contributes nothing to the estimation sample should not change the standard error at all. ado:8980-8986 argues the `if smp` qualifier is load-bearing because evaluating the predicate on the raw frame could misclassify a coarser cluster and 'silently take the keep-i rule and collapse att_i's composition variance' - but `smp` is the design sample, not the estimation sample, so that exact misclassification remains reachable through any row the markout later drops. sthlp:431 documents this design-vs-estimation gap for permute() ('rows wooldid later removes by its deterministic markout, e.g. missing outcomes or zero weights, still count toward the design'); nothing states it for the bootstrap regime.
refuter_note: Reproduces on realistic input, with a cleaner isolation than the prober's. Pairs (se(att_i) A -> D): .24803561 -> .21190601 (ratio .854); .26059414 -> .22797831 (.875); .24650980 -> .20780768 (.843). In every pair e(N) = 419 in both arms, b(att) and b(att_i) agree to all 8 printed figures, and se(att) is IDENTICAL to every printed digit (.23407218, .24655838, .30014947) — which proves the two arms drew the same clusters and fitted the same rows, so the 13-16% fall in se(att_i) is attributable to the unit-identity rule alone and to nothing else. Magnitude correction only: 13-16% here rather than the 23.9% they report from a near-degenerate DGP. This is the sharpest statement of the root cause — the regime predicate runs on the DESIGN sample, so a row the estimator provably discards decides which variance is computed — and it needs no straddling estimable row to fire.
refuter_did: First verified the source claim independently: ado:394 passes ifr(`wdp_if') and ado:615 sets wdp_if to the raw user `if', so bootrun's `smp' is (user if == 1) & nonmissing cluster with no markout. Then built my own realistic panel (same generator as r01a), set firm 1's t=3 outcome to missing in BOTH arms, and in arm D additionally recorded that one unestimable row under county 2. reps(199), paired rseeds, three completed A/D pairs (log: r02_phantom_PARTIAL_3pairs.log; the run was killed for budget after three pairs and the do-file has since been trimmed to that scope).

lens.impact: Bootstrap standard errors on att_i / att_it / att_itime come back 13-24% too small (measured 14.6% on my own pair), always in the anti-conservative direction, with identical point estimates, identical e(N), no caution anywhere in the output and nothing in e() to record it - triggered by a single unestimable row (missing outcome, missing control, zero weight) carrying a different cluster code than its unit's other rows. wooldid's own header even prints "1 obs dropped from initial sample" about that row while letting it choose the variance.

title: bootstrap() resamples the `smp` universe, not e(sample): units with no usable outcome count as resampling clusters, inflating e(boot_df) and silencing both documented few-cluster cautions
surface: bootstrap(standard) / bootdf(clusters) / e(boot_df) / bootsave() w_ columns / the <10-cluster and <6-treated-cluster cautions
claim: On two runs with an IDENTICAL estimation sample (same e(N), same e(N_clust)), merely leaving units whose outcome is entirely missing in the data file changes bootstrap() inference: e(boot_df) (the default bootdf(clusters) = G-1) counts those units as resampling clusters, and both of the few-cluster cautions the help promises are suppressed. The count leg also stops matching Stata's own bootstrap prefix replication for replication, which sthlp:532 says it does.
observed: repro_br4.log, 14 units x 8 periods, 5 treated 2003 / 4 treated 2005 / 5 never, with 5 units (3 treated, 2 never) whose outcome is missing on every row. ARM A (phantoms left in): e(N)=72, e(N_clust)=9, e(boot_df)=13 -> G=14; NEITHER caution printed. ARM B (phantoms dropped): e(N)=72, e(N_clust)=9, e(boot_df)=8 -> G=9; BOTH printed ('Caution: only 9 clusters are available for the bootstrap'; 'Caution: only 4 treated cluster(s) are available for resampling'). probe14.log isolates the cause on a 60-unit panel with 15% missing outcomes plus one all-missing unit: ARM A e(N_clust)=59 / e(boot_df)=59 and wooldid-vs-Stata-prefix MAXRELDIF = 1.0678e-01 (every one of 40 replications differs); ARM B, same unit physically dropped, e(boot_df)=58 and MAXRELDIF = 2.6110e-08, which is the float precision of Stata's own saving() file, i.e. an exact match. probe13.log additionally shows bootsave() writing a w_5 column for the all-missing unit with mean multiplicity 1.2, i.e. the phantom cluster is actually drawn.
expected: wooldid_bootrun builds its resampling universe at ado:8915-8925 as smp = (user if) & nonmissing cluster, then resamples that; rows and whole clusters the estimation drops (missing outcome, missing control, singleton, outside the ES window) stay in it. Stata's own bootstrap prefix resamples e(sample), which is why the two agree exactly on complete data (probe4.log) and disagree on every replication once anything is dropped. G should be the number of clusters that contribute to the estimation: e(boot_df)=G-1 is then 8, not 13, and both cautions in wooldid_bootctl (computed on the same smp count) fire. Consequence of the wrong df, per sthlp:1340: t(13,.975)=2.160 against t(8,.975)=2.306, 6.8% narrower, moving the Wald family (e(boot_ci_normal), e(boot_wald_mainresults)), everything reading e(V) with e(df_r) (a hand test/lincom, esttab, coefplot, the honestdid handoff), and under bootdisplay(wald) the displayed interval and p-value. The default percentile columns are rank-based and do not move. sthlp:532 promises both cautions unconditionally.
refuter_note: Three sharpenings, none of which overturns the claim. (a) Their EXPECTED says 'The default percentile columns are rank-based and do not move.' That is wrong: the replication DRAWS come from a different universe, measured as the real-cluster mass varying 22-36 instead of being fixed at 30, so the percentile p and interval move too; only the df path is percentile-immune. The systematic size is second-order, E[G/m] = 1 + Var(m)/G^2, about +4% on variance at the 9-real/6-phantom geometry, and at reps(40) it is swamped by Monte Carlo noise, so I do NOT claim their 10% arm-A-vs-arm-B SE gap is systematic. (b) The realistic routes are singleton units and a control missing for a whole unit, not units with an entirely missing outcome; those are what make this high rather than a curiosity. (c) The wrong df is DISPLAYED, not merely stored: the run's own footer prints 'e(V) and e(df_r) carry the standard-deviation family referred to the t(14) distribution ... and so do the tools that read e(V) without being asked: esttab, coefplot and honestdid' (probe_br4.log:171) against 't(8)' on the clean arm (probe_br4.log:243). Note also on framing: this does NOT contradict known_bydesign section 4 literally, since the exact-one `if` rule genuinely does apply identically to all three samples. What it contradicts is the broader claim in the code comment at ado:663-670 that 'the estimation sample, the permutation design and the bootstrap frame agree' - so it is a contradiction of a load-bearing comment, not a rediscovery of a ruled design.
refuter_did: Built my own two-arm panel from scratch (9 real units: 2 treated 2004, 2 treated 2006, 5 never; plus 6 extra units whose outcome is missing on EVERY row). ARM A leaves them in the file, ARM B deletes them. Measured: e(N)=90 and e(N_clust)=9 in BOTH arms, att bit-identical (+1.5e1e5ebcbec84X-001), but e(boot_df)=14 / e(df_r)=14 in ARM A against 8 / 8 in ARM B, and NEITHER few-cluster caution printed in ARM A while BOTH printed in ARM B. Sharper statement than the original: one and the same ereturn posts e(N_clust)=9 and e(boot_df)=14. Second block (30 real + 10 phantom, bootsave(), reps 200): 40 w_ columns for e(N_clust)=30, phantom unit 35 drawn with mean multiplicity 1.02 and max 4, and the total drawn mass over the 30 REAL clusters has mean 29.9, SD 2.60, min 22, max 36 where a correct cluster bootstrap holds it at exactly 30. Then probe_br4c.do tested the two realistic routes out of e(sample) instead of all-missing outcomes: SINGLETON units (one period each, dropped by reghdfe) and units whose controls(x) is missing on every row. Both reproduce it exactly: e(N)=90, e(N_clust)=9, att bit-identical, e(boot_df) 8 -> 14, both cautions silenced. Pinned the mechanism in source: ado:682 and ado:704 zero `ifvar` for missing y/i/t/w and for missing controls, but ado:615 forwards the RAW user `if` as wdp_if, which bootrun (ado:8917) and permctl/permrun (ado:5957, ado:7479) rebuild as their sample with the markout never applied. ado:10233 then sets e(df_r) = nclus-1 off that count. Also checked e(boot_failed): 0 in all four routes, so no failure-count inflation at this geometry.

lens.lens: INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION — built the case a third time from the claim alone, with my own DGP, my own geometry, and three independent exclusion routes; did not open either prior agent's do-file before my own log was written.
lens.impact: A user with a small-G clustered design who leaves unusable units in the data file — units observed in a single period, units missing a control, units that never report the outcome — gets e(df_r) and e(boot_df) inflated by the count of those units even though e(N), e(N_clust) and the point estimate are unchanged. The Wald-family interval is then too narrow (6.3% at 9 real clusters with 5 excluded) everywhere e(V) and e(df_r) are read: esttab, coefplot, the honestdid handoff, a hand test or lincom, and the printed table under bootdisplay(wald). Both documented few-cluster cautions are silenced, and because the count is taken on the whole file rather than the estimation sample, a SINGLE excluded unit at 9 clusters is enough to lose the first one. The same run posts e(df_r_analytic)=8 beside e(boot_df)=13, so the program contradicts itself in its own e() without saying so.

title: bootsave()'s _rep = 0 row for jointW_* holds an event-study coefficient, not the observed joint statistic
surface: bootsave() + boottstat + jointtests (and advW*)
claim: In a bootsave() file the row documented as carrying the observed statistic for the jointW_<family> columns is filled by POSITION from a matrix with an entirely different column set, so it holds an observed pre-treatment event-study COEFFICIENT. Recomputing the joint p-value from the saved file -- exactly what the file is sold for -- gives a silently wrong number.
observed:
20 states, cluster(state), bootstrap(standard) reps(199) boottstat jointtests bootsave(dj):
  e(joint_horiz) reported by wooldid          = 0.682119205
  replications with a usable W_r              = 150
  implied #{W_r >= W_obs} from the printed p  = 102  ->  W_obs must lie in (16.64803143, 17.12810703]
  bootsave _rep==0 value of jointW_att        = -0.33935852   (NEGATIVE)
  min / max of the replication W_r            = 0.40553037 / 8896.12
  -0.33935852 is exactly e(b_es_att)['pre3']
  p recomputed from the file as documented    = 1.000000000 ; FAIL = 1
A joint W statistic is a quadratic form and cannot be negative, so the wrong value is detectable in principle -- but nothing in the file or the run says so.
expected: wooldid.sthlp, bootsave() entry: 'Under boottstat the replication joint-test statistics are added as jointW_name and the adversarial statistic as advW, WITH THE OBSERVED STATISTICS ON THE _rep = 0 ROW', and the same entry sells the file as self-sufficient ('so the draws can be recentred from the file alone'). Cause: wooldid_bootsavemk ado:14915-14923. JW = e(boot_jointW) has one column per FAMILY (wdb_jfk: att, att_it, ame, ame_it and their _s# twins); `jobs` is built by wooldid_bootjobs (ado:14666) and has one column per (family, PRE-HORIZON) pair holding e(b_es_<fam>)[1,j]; the loop writes JO[1,k] under JW's column index k. The engine itself never uses JO that way -- wooldid_bootjnt obtains the observed statistic through the NAME-keyed wooldid_bootjwobs(fk, jobs, wobs) at ado:15310. SCOPE: the jointW_* leg is measured; the advW* block six lines below (ado:14925-14931) has the identical positional shape with the same kind of coefficient vector (wooldid_bootjobs with allh=1) against awacc's <family>_a0/_a1 columns, so the same defect is expected there, but I did not run `adversarial`, so that half is read, not measured.
refuter_note: Severity revised UP from medium. The bootsave() entry sells the file as self-sufficient ('so the draws can be recentred from the file alone') and explicitly documents the _rep = 0 row as carrying the observed statistics; recomputing the documented statistic from it returns a silently wrong number on BOTH the jointW_* and the advW legs, and the only tell is that a quadratic form came out negative. That is a silently wrong number in a documented artifact, the brief's top category. The finding's SCOPE note ('the advW block is read, not measured') is now closed by measurement.
refuter_did: My own 22-state panel, cluster(state), bootstrap(standard) reps(199) boottstat jointtests bootsave. e(joint_horiz)=0.6865671642 while the file's jointW_att at _rep==0 is -0.6261495363, exactly e(b_es_att)['pre3']; the replication W_r range is [0.4342965283, 3.56e+04], so recomputing the documented add-one share from the file gives p=1.0000000. I then MEASURED the advW half the finding could only read: a second run with `adversarial` writes advW at _rep==0 = -0.6261495363, the same coefficient, against a replication range of [0.0006373550, 4.1633e+02], and the file-recomputed p is again 1.0000000. Read-side: wooldid_bootsavemk writes JO[1,k] under the accumulator's column index k while jobs (wooldid_bootjobs, ado:14666) has one column per (family, pre-horizon); the engine itself uses the name-keyed wooldid_bootjwobs (ado:15310), so wooldid's own printed p is unaffected.

title: fastnose publishes subgroup ame event-study rows the full run drops as non-estimable — including a POST-treatment horizon reported as exactly 0 — contradicting sthlp:292's guarantee that the row sets match
surface: fastnose x contreat()/contreatcontrols() x subgroups() x esprelength()/espostlength(); e(b_es_ame_s#), e(numpre_ame_s#), e(wdidsgresults_#) and the printed subgroup tables (ado:3290 vs ado:2912/1981)
claim: With contreat() + subgroups() + an event-study window, a fastnose run posts and prints event-study rows in the ame family that the identical analytic run drops as not estimable. The extra rows carry the regression's structural zeros, e(b_es_ame_s#) changes shape, and e(numpre_ame_s#) changes from 0 to 4. sthlp:292 states the opposite verbatim: 'fast mode therefore reports the same event-study rows as the full run'. SEEDED CAVEAT: seeded lead 3 named this exact interaction but predicted the fast-collapse (fcdeg) mechanism; the actual mechanism is the SI-7 estimability filter on the CONTINUOUS subgroup-by-horizon call.
observed: SHARPEST FORM (repro_FN03.log, contreatcontrols(basic) arm, subgroup 2): analytic e(b_es_ame_s2) = 1x1, colname post0, value -.300694594. fastnose e(b_es_ame_s2) = 1x6, colnames pre4 pre3 pre2 pre1 post0 post1, values 0 0 0 0 -.300694594 and 0. The extra post1 column is a POST-TREATMENT horizon the full run drops as non-estimable and fast mode reports as an average marginal effect of exactly zero. e(numpre_ame_s2): 0 (analytic) vs 4 (fastnose). UNTREATEDZERO ARM, same repro: analytic e(b_es_ame_s1) colnames post0 post1 post2 post3, e(numpre_ame_s1)=0; fastnose colnames pre4 pre3 pre2 pre1 post0 post1 post2 post3 with the four pre entries exactly 0, e(numpre_ame_s1)=4; e(wdidsgresults_1/2) gain a pretreatment:ame row; the printed subgroup table gains 'pretreatment | ame | 0' and 'ES_ame | pre4..pre1 | 0'. CONTROL, same spec WITHOUT subgroups(): both modes give pre4..post3 and numpre_ame=4 — identical, so the divergence is subgroup-specific. First discovered in p4_sgrows.log ARM C (lines 1870-1905 analytic, 2100-2260 fastnose). MECHANISM (inferred from code, not measured): ado:1974-1981 (BS-26) forces sgmarginsdof to df(df_r) under fastnose for the BINARY subgroup-by-horizon call at ado:2912, so margins' not-estimable marker survives for wooldid_sglbl to filter on; the CONTINUOUS twin at ado:3290 still threads marginsdof, which fastnose sets to nose (ado:1973). My direct margins-level demonstration that nose strips the marker (p13_nosemarker.do) was inconclusive — both constructions left the level out of margins' over() entirely — so the mechanism rests on ado:1974's own comment plus the marginsdof/sgmarginsdof asymmetry. The DIVERGENCE itself is measured three times (p4 ARM C, repro untreatedZero arm, repro basic arm).
