Subgroup 1 holds i=1 (effect 10, four post cells of 5 rows, all labelled) and i=2 (effect 2, post cells of 5,5,2,2 rows labelled on 1,1,2,2 rows -> cell shares .2 .2 1 1). Clean arm: att=6.7058823529, att_it=6.0000000000, att_i=6.0000000000, att_itime=6.0000000000. Partially-labelled arm: att=8.1538461538, att_it=7.0000000000, att_i=7.6000000000, att_itime=7.0000000000. Every one of these lands on its cell-share-weighted prediction to within 1.3e-14 (att_it target 44.8/6.4=7.0, att_i target 10.857143/1.428571=7.6, att_itime target 11.2/1.6=7.0, att target 212/26=8.1538461538) and misses the documented equal-cell / equal-unit target of 6.0 by +16.7% (att_it) and +26.7% (att_i). 8 of 234 rows lost their label. No caution of any kind; the header reads 'N = 234 (0 obs dropped from initial sample)'.
expected: att_it should give each cohort-period cell equal weight -- 6.0 here -- because that is the definition the option's own help entry states and the only thing that distinguishes att_it from att. wooldid REFUSES the structurally identical case (a unit split across subgroups over time) with r(459), and its error text names precisely this distortion ('weighted by its share of sample weight there, rather than with the equal unit weighting those estimands normally imply'), so the project's own standard for this consequence is a refusal, not silence. IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this does NOT contradict sthlp:887's sentence that 'by-subgroup att and att_it are unaffected' -- that sentence is about the cross-period SPLIT under safety(off), where F13 has already guaranteed each cell sits wholly in one subgroup, and it is correct there. What this contradicts is the help's SILENCE: its only sentence about missing subgroup values, 'Observations with missing subgroup values remain allowed and belong to no subgroup', says nothing about the cell those observations sit in being down-weighted to its labelled share. It also refutes the seeded finding's generalization that att and att_it are 'CORRECT' in the missing case.

title: poisson + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) breaks on the DEFAULT engine too: a true xb-scale ame of 0.400 is reported as 0.100
surface: contreat() + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) + poisson (default ppmlhdfe engine); ado:1233 ringer trigger, ado:1313 untreatedZero branch
claim: The DF-1 ringer trigger at ado:1233 includes `poisson`, so `contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) poisson` installs the pooled dose control inside ppmlhdfe's absorb() (or, after the rc-3200 fallback, in the main equation). margins never switches that term off, so the reported ame and att on the default engine lose the pooled dose effect. Falsifiable: on a log-linear count DGP with a known xb-scale dose effect of 0.400, poisson + contreatcontrols(basic) must recover ~0.40 on BOTH engines while poisson + untreatedZero must come back far below it.
observed: DGP mu = exp(1.0 + 0.10*t + 0.40*dose*post) over 9 cohorts (6 treated), 7 periods, 14 records per cohort-period; truth on the xb scale is ame = 0.400000, att = 0.565295. CONTROL: poisson + contreatcontrols(basic), default engine -> att 0.5442619, ame 0.4377304; poisson + basic + customvce(robust) -> att 0.5442619, ame 0.4377304, bit-identical. DEVIANT: poisson + contreatcontrols(untreatedZero), default engine -> att 0.0771772, ame 0.1003708 (second seed, repro_uz_ringer.log: att 0.0771772 / ame 0.1003708; pD_ringer.log other seed: att 0.1205256 / ame 0.0737182). Verbose prints the command as `ppmlhdfe ycount i._i#i._t#i.TF#c.d2 i._i#i._t#i.TF , absorb(i.i i.t  i.__000009##c.(__000008)) tol(1e-9) d` -- the ringer i.__000009##c.(__000008) is inside absorb(). The run then takes the documented rc-3200 fallback, which moves the ringer into the main equation; either placement leaves it margins-invisible. No multicollinearity caution and no other warning fires on this arm.
expected: contreatcontrols(untreatedZero) is defined at sthlp:1033 as 'by not including a g() function at all, identification of marginal effects of Contreat_jt will occur using only within treated cohort-period variation'. A pooled dose control IS a g() function, so it must not be in the model at all; and whatever the parametrisation, the reported average marginal effect of the dose must equal the true 0.400 that the basic-controls arm recovers on the same data. The ado:1233 condition `strpos(contreatcontrols,"basic") | unconditionalse | customvce() | poisson` was written for a ringer that the DF-1 comment calls 'a numerical twin of columns the margins-visible block already carries ... It adds no rank' -- a premise that holds under basic and fails under untreatedZero, where nothing else carries the dose outside the treated cells.

title: The bootstrap's cluster count comes from the DESIGN sample, so a cluster whose outcome is never observed still buys a degree of freedom — and the same table prints both numbers
surface: bootstrap() cluster() — wdb_C / wdb_r_nclus, bootdf(clusters) default, e(df_r), the few-cluster and few-treated-cluster cautions
claim: Under bootstrap(), e(df_r) and the few-cluster cautions are computed from clusters present in (user if == 1) & nonmissing cluster, not from clusters present in the estimation sample; so on a panel where some clusters carry no estimable rows, wooldid posts a degrees-of-freedom number that its own header contradicts and that the analytic path on identical data does not produce.
observed: 14-county panel, T=7, 4 units/county, bootstrap(standard) cluster(cty) reps(99). C0 (all 14 counties measured): e(N)=294, header 'N clusters = 14', e(df_r)=13. C7 (outcome collected in 7 counties, the other 7 all-missing y): e(N)=147, header 'N clusters = 7', footer 'e(V) and e(df_r) carry the standard-deviation family referred to the t(13) distribution', e(df_r)=13 — while the ANALYTIC run on the identical data reports e(df_r)=6. C12 (2 counties measured): e(N)=42, header 'N clusters = 2', 55 of 99 replications failed, e(df_r) still 13, and the 'only N clusters are available for the bootstrap; bootstrap inference is unreliable with very few clusters' caution never prints because the design count 14 is >= 10. Source: wooldid_bootrun builds its map frame on `smp' (ado:8910-8925), counts wdb_C there, c_locals it as wdb_r_nclus (ado:9537); ado:423 makes bootdf default 'clusters' from that count; ado:6502 and ado:6520 key the two few-cluster cautions on the parallel `smp2'.
expected: Cluster-robust degrees of freedom are G-1 with G the number of clusters contributing to the estimation sample — which is what wooldid itself reports on the analytic path on the same data (6, not 13), and what its own bootstrap header reports ('N clusters = 7'). t(13)=2.160 against t(6)=2.447, so every bootdisplay(wald) interval and everything that reads e(V)+e(df_r) without asking — the footer names esttab, coefplot and honestdid — is about 12% too narrow, and worse in C12. The 2026-09-02 ruling at ado:415-421 defines G as 'the number of resampling clusters', which is defensible as a description of the draw, but the draw is drawing clusters that can never contribute (that is what the 55 of 99 failures in C12 are), and the table states the other number two lines above. This is the same root cause as FCW-01/FCW-02 — the design sample standing in for the estimation sample — on a surface that needs no straddling cluster and no cell-weighted estimand: building `smp' on the estimation sample closes all three.

title: esfixedbaseperiod silently deletes any treated unit that does not OBSERVE the exact relative period named by esrelativeto()
surface: esfixedbaseperiod x esrelativeto() x missing outcome; sample construction; ado:855-861 and 868-875; sthlp:722-727 and sthlp:73
claim: Under esfixedbaseperiod, a treated unit is removed from the estimation sample in its entirety -- post-treatment observations included -- with no message of any kind, unless it observes the exact relative period esrelativeto() names (default -1). A single missing outcome year, at relyr == -1 and no other year, therefore deletes a unit that still has five usable pre-periods and five post-periods; the pooled-reference branch on identical data keeps it and estimates it correctly. No paragraph of wooldid.sthlp states this rule.
observed: 30 firms, 2000-2010, 12 treated in 2006; firms 1-4 given a true effect of 4 and firms 5-12 of 1, so the TRUE ATT over all 12 treated is 2.0. Firms 1-4 have the outcome missing in 2005 (relyr -1) and in NO other year. A) complete outcome, esfixedbaseperiod esrelativeto(-1): att=1.997455, N=330, N_dropped=0, 12 treated i in e(gteffects). B) the one-year hole, same command: att=1.016014, N=286, N_dropped=44, only 8 treated i in e(gteffects). C) identical data, pooled reference branch: att=1.994924, N=326, N_dropped=4, 12 treated i. D) identical data, esfixedbaseperiod esrelativeto(-2): att=2.150968, N=326, N_dropped=4, 12 treated i -- which pins the mechanism to 'must observe that exact relative period'. E) with timetrends (r02_drops.do P2F/P2G) a hole at EITHER -1 or -2 deletes the unit, att=0.502213. grep -c Caution over the whole repro log: 0. Mechanism at ado:855-861: refperiodobserved = max(_t == refperiod) by i, then replace ifvar = 0 if refperiodobserved == 0 & ttre != . ; timetrends twin at ado:868-875.
expected: A Caution naming the count, exactly as the anticipation twin already does -- wooldid_anticesf is invoked at ado:862 on THIS VERY DROP SITE to attribute reference-period drops when anticipation() causes them, so the author has already decided this drop is worth naming; it goes unnamed only when the cause is a hole in the data. Failing that, a sentence in the esfixedbaseperiod / esrelativeto() help. Neither exists: sthlp:722-727 is silent and sthlp:73 promises only that 'cohorts treated before the sample begins are dropped', which is not what happens to a firm observed continuously from 2000 whose 2005 outcome is missing. The drop is econometrically necessary once the base period is fixed at -1 -- necessary is not the same as silent. Honest caveat: the 2.00 -> 1.02 swing is DGP-engineered; in a real application the magnitude is whatever the dropped units' heterogeneity is, and zero only if missingness at the reference period is unrelated to treatment effects.

title: gteffects reports numerically-zero cell variances as real standard errors: se ~ 1e-15, p down to 8e-258, confidence intervals of width ~1e-14
surface: gteffects cell se/p/ci x cluster-robust VCE with few clusters relative to treated cohort-by-period coefficients; ado:13496 (mata wooldid_gtx) and ado:1767; the gteffects help sentence 'degenerate zero variances are always reported as missing, never zero'
claim: The gteffects help states verbatim that 'degenerate zero variances are always reported as missing, never zero'. The guard implementing it (ado:13496, mata wooldid_gtx: se = (v < . & v > 0) ? sqrt(v) : .) tests for EXACT zero with no relative or absolute floor. When the cluster-robust stage-1 covariance is rank-deficient in the direction of a cell coefficient, the diagonal residue is of order 1e-30 rather than 0, so it passes the guard and the cell is printed as an ordinary row carrying a standard error of ~1e-15, a p-value as small as 8e-258 and a 95% confidence interval whose endpoints equal the point estimate.
observed: 40 states, 20 years, three adoption waves plus 10 never-treated, clean balanced data, i = onset cohort, cluster(cohid) i.e. cluster AT the level of i. 39 gteffects rows, 9 of them degenerate, e.g. i=4 relyr=-2 b=1.09932691 se=1.035e-15 p=1.839e-45 ci=[1.09932691 , 1.09932691]; i=4 relyr=-1 b=-0.96059515 se=1.748e-15 p=1.329e-44; i=4 relyr=0 b=1.65373779 se=2.685e-15 p=9.440e-45. Every cell of that cohort degenerates, PRE-TREATMENT rows included. Controls on the same data: cluster(state), below i, min se 3.213e-01 and 0 degenerate; robust, min se 7.468e-01 and 0 degenerate. No Caution prints in any arm (grep -c Caution = 0), e(es_ndegen_att) is not posted, and e(wdid_vcvstate) reads the ordinary 'analytic-blocks'. Reach map (r05_map.do, K onset cohorts + never-treated, 30 units each, 24 periods): K=3 21/66 degenerate min p 5.97e-44; K=6 18/123 min p 2.65e-87; K=12 12/210 min p 9.32e-167; K=20 4/270 min p 8.36e-258. cluster below i: 0 at every K. A 3-group CROSS-CUTTING cluster variable at K=20 also produces 4/270 with min p 1.66e-27, so cluster-at-i is not the only route. Fires with and without timetrends; does not fire under iid, robust, cluster below i, or unit-level i + cluster(unit) (14 clean arms across r03/r04/r05).
expected: The gteffects paragraph's own sentence -- those rows carry a MISSING se, and hence a missing p and interval. A relative floor of the kind the package already uses elsewhere would catch every row above: the project's IM degeneracy guard is se < 1e-10*|b|, and the worst se/|b| ratio in my degenerate rows is 1.9e-14. Why this is not the ruled aggregate result rediscovered: ado:1767 is 'cap matrix gtsed = vecdiag(e(V))', so the cell SEs are read straight off the same stage-1 covariance that feeds margins for the aggregates. The aggregate consequence IS ruled (analytic SEs understated to 0.66-0.75 when cluster() is at or above i, sthlp:251); an aggregate averages many cells and lands at 0.7x, which looks plausible, while an individual cell lands at 1e-15, which does not, and which the help explicitly promises will be shown as missing. One surface was ruled; the other contradicts a verbatim promise in its own paragraph. Concrete misread: the pre-treatment rows degenerate too, so a user reading pre-trends off e(gteffects) -- which the help sells as 'directly comparable to the group-time tables of csdid or xthdidregress' and as 'the one inference surface that survives fast mode' -- sees p = 1e-41 on a placebo cell and concludes a catastrophic pre-trend violation. Headline aggregates are unaffected, which is why this is high rather than critical.

title: permute()'s fast-mode DEFAULT publishes a whole subgroup ame event study the analytic run skips entirely, as zeros carrying permutation p-values and shift intervals
surface: permute() fast-mode default x contreat()/contreatcontrols() x subgroups() x esprelength()/espostlength(); e(wdidsgresults_#), the printed subgroup tables, ado:3290 vs ado:2912/5448
claim: With contreat() + subgroups() + an event-study window, `permute()` without any `fastnose` on the command line (the fast-mode default, ado:5448) posts and prints ame event-study rows that the identical analytic run drops as not estimable, with each fabricated row carrying a permutation p_perm and a shift interval, and with every drop Caution and the e(es_ndegen_ame_s#) flag suppressed.
observed: ARM P of r3_escalate.log (`wooldid y cohort t ttre , contreat(dose) contreatcontrols(basic) fe(unit) cluster(cohort) subgroups(region) esprelength(3) espostlength(2) permute(shuffle) permreps(20)`, rc 0) prints for subgroup 2: main:ame 0 (p_perm .4, CI [-.1923960217, .0001773005]); pretreatment:ame 0 (p 1, CI [0,0]); ES_ame:pre3 0 (p 1, CI [0,0]); ES_ame:pre2 0 (p 1, CI [0,0]); ES_ame:pre1 0 (p 1, CI [0,0]); ES_ame:post0 0 (p 1, CI [-.1923960217, 0]). The analytic run on identical data (r4_controls.log ARM V) reports NO ES_ame row at all for subgroup 2 and says why: 'no continuous-treatment relative period effect is estimable for subgroup 2, so its continuous-treatment event study is skipped entirely.' Subgroup 1 is hit too: ES_ame:pre3/pre2/pre1 = 0 with p_perm 1, 1, .952 where the analytic run reports only post0 and post1. Under permute() none of the analytic run's four 'not estimable ... dropped' Cautions is printed, and e(es_ndegen_ame_s#) is absent. Sharpening: subgroup 1's ES_ame:pre1 returns p_perm .952 with shift interval [-.1859513891, 0] — the observed statistic is a structural zero while the replications mix structural zeros with genuine estimates from reassignments that made the horizon estimable, so that p is not a permutation p-value of anything.
expected: The analytic subgroup run's SI-7 estimability screen exists precisely because reporting a non-estimable margin as an estimate is wrong, and sthlp:292 promises fast mode 'reports the same event-study rows as the full run'. permute() is the headline randomization-inference feature and takes the fast path BY DEFAULT, so a user never opts into this and is never told to re-run. Explicitly NOT the complaint: on the POOLED (no-subgroups) path the analytic run also reports pre3/pre2/pre1 = 0, flagged by a Caution and e(es_ndegen) — that is documented design at sthlp:1325/903. The defect is the SUBGROUP row set, published with inference and with no flag of any kind. Root cause shared with FASTNOSE-03: ado:3290 threads `marginsdof` (= `nose` in fast mode) on the continuous subgroup-by-horizon call, while ado:2912's binary twin was given `df(df_r)` back by BS-26 and this one was not; `nose` strips margins' `o.` omission marker that wooldid_sglbl (ado:12575) filters on, proven directly in r6_omarker.do.

title: bootstrap() and permute() permanalyticse abort r(459) on contreat() + subgroups() + an event-study window, with a 'this is unexpected - please report it' message
surface: bootstrap() and permute() permanalyticse x contreat() x subgroups() x esprelength()/espostlength(); the rep-0 column-set check, ado:322 / ado:126 (reps run under fastnose) vs ado:3290
claim: `bootstrap()` (any display type) and `permute() permanalyticse` fail with r(459) on every continuous-treatment run that combines subgroups() with an event-study window, because the analytic observed run drops the non-estimable ame horizons while the rep-0 comparator runs under fastnose and keeps them, so the column sets cannot align.
observed: r4_controls.log, one panel, bootstrap(standard) reps(20): B1 contreat + ES, NO subgroups -> rc 0; B2 contreat + subgroups, NO ES window -> rc 0; B3 BINARY + subgroups + ES -> rc 0; B4 contreat + subgroups + ES -> rc 459; B5 the same as B4 with robust instead of cluster() -> rc 459. The message is 'Error: the rep-0 coefficient vector does not match the observed run's column set; bootstrap accumulation would be misaligned. This is unexpected - please report it.' r3_escalate.log ARM PA gives the identical failure under permute(shuffle) permreps(20) permanalyticse with 'permutation accumulation' in place of 'bootstrap accumulation', e(perm_reps_done) missing. So the abort is exactly the three-way interaction contreat x subgroups x ES window, and is not cluster-dependent.
expected: The run should complete. This is the very failure the BS-26 comment at ado:1976-1978 says it fixed — 'under fastnose a structural-zero horizon was reported (and ranked by permute()) and the observed and replication column sets diverged, aborting bootstrap()/permute() permanalyticse with r(459) at rep 0' — fixed at ado:1981 for the binary subgroup-by-horizon call at ado:2912 (confirmed working by control B3) and never applied to the continuous twin at ado:3290. It is not an edge case in the data: the structural zeros exist because dose is 0 in untreated periods, which is exactly what sthlp:897 instructs ('Must be defined for all observations (set to 0 if not naturally defined within untreated cohort-periods)'). Continuous-treatment DiD with heterogeneity by subgroup, an event study and a bootstrap is a mainstream applied specification and it cannot be run at all. The error's own 'This is unexpected - please report it' wording confirms it is an unmet internal assertion rather than a design refusal. Root cause shared with FASTNOSE-03.

title: The documented remedy geometry (coarsen `i` so that cluster() is finer than `i`) silently biases the POINT ESTIMATE on an unbalanced panel
surface: `i` / `fe()` / the 'What level to cluster at' remedy at sthlp:255
claim: sthlp:255 names 'a finer cluster()' as THE remedy for the at-or-above-i SE understatement and says 'The intended practice is to cluster BELOW the level of i - at a level whose units are nested inside cohorts'. In a state-policy panel with one row per state-year the only way to reach that geometry is to pass the onset WAVE as `i`, which replaces the state fixed effects with a single wave intercept. On a balanced panel that is harmless (the point estimate is bit-identical). On an unbalanced panel it silently changes the point estimate by an amount proportional to the dispersion of the sub-i permanent heterogeneity, with no caution of any kind. fe(state) and controls(i.state) each repair it exactly, and the 'What level to cluster at' passage never mentions either.
observed: Zero-noise DGP (y = s_g + 0.2t + 1*(t>=ttre), s_g = 2*mod(state,7)-6, 40 states, T=12, states 1-3 adopt at t=5, 4-6 at t=7, rest never), so every departure from 1.000000000000 is arithmetic. balanced: i=state 1.000000000000, i=coh 1.000000000000. One treated state attrits after t=8: i=state 1.000000000000, i=coh 1.210526315789 (+21%). One treated state enters late at t=5: i=state 1.000000000000, i=coh 0.428571428571 (-57%). Ordinary ragged panel, 8% MCAR across all 40 states: i=state 1.000000000000, i=coh 1.214732454068 (+21%), printed as 'att 1.2147325  se .12963004  t 9.37  p 0.000  95% CI [.95253096, 1.476934]' with no caution at all (probe_fe.do). On the same ragged data, i=coh cluster(state) fe(state) returns 1.000000000000 with se 0, and controls(i.state) likewise. probe_unbal3.do shows the bias scales linearly with sub-i dispersion: sd(s_g) 0.5/1/2/4 gives i=coh 1.0154/1.0309/1.0617/1.1234 while i=state and i=coh+fe(state) are exactly 1.0000000000 at every dispersion.
expected: The true att is exactly 1 by construction and the estimator with `i` at the panel unit returns it to the last printed digit on every one of these panels. A user who follows sthlp:255's remedy on a ragged administrative panel - the normal case - gets a 21% error reported with p<0.001 and nothing said. sthlp:64-70 does document the pairing ('Choose i by the treatment heterogeneity ... not by the level at which you want fixed effects - those are specified separately in fe(), so a coarse i combines with unit-level ones'), and the SI-8 runtime caution at ado:1371 also names fe(), so the behaviour is not undocumented - but both present fe() as a modelling PREFERENCE rather than a correctness requirement, the Standard-Errors remedy sentence that pushes users into the geometry omits it entirely, and nothing fires at runtime when `i` holds sub-units, the panel is unbalanced and no fe() was given. This is category 1 by the brief's ranking: a silently wrong number on input a real applied economist has.

title: The joint pre-trend test is severely oversized in the exact geometry the help and the runtime caution name as its REMEDY, and prints nothing there
surface: jointtests under analytic clustered SEs with cluster() strictly finer than the cohort-by-period cells (sthlp:743; caution at ado:1443)
claim: sthlp:743 says jointtests 'is unreliable under wooldid's analytic clustered SEs when clustering is at the level of the cohort variable i or above' and names the fixes: 'use bootstrap-based clustered standard errors or randomization inference (see permute()), or cluster strictly finer than the cohort-by-period cells'. The runtime caution at ado:1443 ends with the same clause. In that named remedy geometry, with three clusters inside each treated cohort-by-period cell, the joint pre-trend test rejects a TRUE null 61.7% of the time at nominal 5%, and no caution prints - the caution predicate at ado:1421-1432 (distinct `i` vs distinct (i, cluster) pairs) is the strictly binary test 'every i lies wholly inside one cluster', so it is silent at 2, 3 or 5 clusters per cell.
observed: mc1_ladder.do, 120 draws per rung, tau = 0 in every pre-treatment period so the joint pre-trend null is exactly true; 40 states, cluster(state), 40 clusters in every rung. Rejection rates at nominal 5% / 10%: K=3, i=coh cluster(state) [FINER, no caution] 0.617 / 0.683; K=3, same with the pooled reference 0.617 / 0.667; K=3, i=state cluster(state) [AT i, caution prints] 0.925 / 0.933; K=10, i=coh cluster(state) [FINER, no caution] 0.108 / 0.192; K=10, i=state 0.550 / 0.675. The obvious alternative explanation is ruled out: probe_rank.do dumps the 4x4 pre block of e(V_es_att) and in the remedy geometry it is FULL RANK and well conditioned (K=3 i=coh rank 4/4, cond 2.23e+01, det 1.63e-06; K=10 i=coh rank 4/4, cond 1.64e+01), so this is not a singular matrix being inverted anyway - it is a full-rank covariance that is simply too small in the directions the test uses. (For contrast the at-or-above-i arm is rank 3/4 with cond 6.2e15 and wooldid prints a p-value from it; that case is the documented, cautioned one.) The pre-period point estimates are unbiased (means -0.072, +0.021, +0.011, -0.022 over 120 draws at K=3), so no real pre-trend is being detected.
expected: A pre-trend test on data with no pre-trend should reject at about 5%. The help and the caution both direct the user to exactly this geometry as the cure for the at-or-above-i oversizing, so a user who follows the advice gets a test that is 12x oversized with nothing printed. known_bydesign s1 records the oversizing only at or ABOVE i (11-36% at G=40, 65.7% at G=10) with a named caution; this is the finer-than-i geometry at G=40 that the caution predicate cannot see, and known_bydesign s7 lists 'any finer-than-i arm that FAILS coverage' as genuinely new. The help already contains the right idea in the wrong scope: the second reliability condition in the same jointtests paragraph says that 'in the continuous treatment case ... designs with only a handful of observations per cohort-period cell yield oversized joint tests EVEN UNDER ROBUST OR FINELY CLUSTERED SEs' - which is this failure, except that this is BINARY treatment, the cells hold twelve observations, and what is scarce is CLUSTERS per cell rather than observations.

title: e(gteffects) cell standard errors, p-values and confidence intervals are understated ~3.5x at cluster() at-or-above i: the cell's printed 95% interval covers its own true effect 45% of the time, with no caution anywhere
surface: gteffects (e(gteffects) se / p / lb_95ci / ub_95ci columns) x cluster() at-or-above the level of i
claim: On an ordinary one-row-per-state-year panel with i = state and cluster(state) and a HOMOGENEOUS true treatment effect, the standard error e(gteffects) reports for a cohort-by-relative-period cell is 0.287 of the cell estimate's true sampling standard deviation, and the cell's own reported 95% confidence interval (columns lb_95ci/ub_95ci of e(gteffects)) covers the cell's true effect 45.0% of the time. Nothing is printed to warn the user. The failure is confined to cluster() at-or-above i: on the identical data with i = the onset cohort and cluster(state) finer than i, the same cell's se/sd is 1.012 and its interval covers 0.950.
observed: r11_gtcell_se.do, 60 draws, 30 states x 10 years, onsets 2004/2006/2008, 9 never-treated, y = a_i + 0.03*(year-2000) + 1.0*post + 0.7*N(0,1), i = st, cluster(st), gteffects. For the cell (i = 1, relyr = 0), whose true effect is exactly 1: TRUE sampling sd 0.74714, mean reported se 0.21431, se/sd = 0.287; the reported se ranges 0.14684 to 0.28492 across draws, so it is not a constant, merely far too small; 95% interval coverage of the true effect = 0.450 at nominal 0.95. The att row on the same runs is fine (TRUE sd 0.15138, reported se 0.14064, se/sd 0.929). `grep -ci caution` on that log returns 0. Corroborated on a different 80 draws with different seeds (r10_sesd_het.do, arm 0): cell TRUE sd 0.8671, reported se 0.2166, se/sd 0.250; and with a unit-level effect shock of sd 1.5 the reported se does not move at all (0.2166) while the true sd rises to 1.5269, se/sd 0.142.
expected: The columns are documented as the cell's standard error, p-value and confidence interval (sthlp:1136-1151) and are printed and returned as such, so the interval must cover at its nominal level. The mechanism is the one sthlp:255 names - 'at or above the level of i the cluster-robust covariance stops seeing the treated cells' own variation' - but that sentence enumerates exactly TWO consequences 'that the table does not announce', the att-row standard errors at 'roughly 0.66 to 0.75' and oversized joint pre-trend tests; e(gteffects) is not among them, and the gteffects help block's own two reading notes are about interactivecontrols() and the inwindow column. A reader following sthlp:255 would infer the cells are understated by about a third, not by a factor of three and a half. The scope control settles that this is not an intrinsic limit of per-cell inference: r12_gtcell_finer.do runs the identical data and the identical cell with i = the onset cohort - the help's own recommended 'cluster BELOW the level of i' - and gets se/sd 1.012 and coverage 0.950, exactly nominal. So the surface, the magnitude and the absence of any caution are all undocumented, on a design (state policy panel, cluster on state) that is the package's central use case.

title: A treated cohort whose identifier is literally 0 is silently downweighted in the pretreatment att_i / att_itime (and ame_i / ame_itime) rows
surface: safety(off); contreatwithin + contreat(); the att_i / att_itime weight classifier at ado:1602/1620; the i-positivity screen at ado:4959
claim: Whenever the positive-integer screen on i is down - by an explicit safety(off), which the help documents only as 'proceeds', or by contreatwithin + contreat(), which relaxes it without the user asking - a treated cohort labelled i == 0 has _i == 0 on every row (ado:928-929), so ado:1602's classifier never promotes its pre-window rows from posttreatment 0 to 2, ado:1620 pools its pre-window and reference rows into one w_per_i denominator, and the cohort's pre-period att_i weight sums to less than one. The reported pretreatment att_i / att_itime (and under contreat the ame_i / ame_itime) estimates are then wrong, and depend on nothing but the identifier's label.
observed: r5_izero_strong.log. 20 cohorts x 3 units x 8 periods, onset t=5 (cohorts 1-7) and t=6 (8-14), 15-20 never treated, a distinctive pre-trend in cohort 1 only. Leg A labels cohort 1 as identifier 0; leg B adds 1 to every identifier - same panel, same partition, so every number must agree. Binary + safety(off): pretreatment:att_i A +1.467a7e6eb4400X-006 (0.01993) vs B +1.68c9f81132080X-005 (0.04404), att_itime identical pair, se/t/p/CI all move. contreatwithin + contreat() with NO safety() option typed: pretreatment:att_i A -1.e5e49fbd85000X-004 vs B -1.c475586cc1ce0X-004, pretreatment:ame_i A -1.8ff7eb0f66b71X-001 vs B -1.8e4c52036407dX-001; leg A printed no caution and no error of any kind (grep of log 303-423 matches only the results header). WHICH LEG IS WRONG is pinned by an identity, not by preference: the panel is balanced, so pretreatment:att_i must equal pretreatment:att. Leg B satisfies it to the last hex digit (log 660/662, and 872/874 for ame); leg A does not (log 228 vs 230, 440 vs 442). Leg A reports 0.01993 where 0.04404 is correct - 2.2x too small. The same panel with NO relaxation gives leg A r(411) and leg B rc 0, so the guard is the only thing between an ordinary user and these numbers. Every other row - main:att, main:att_i, main:att_it, main:att_itime, pretreatment:att, pretreatment:att_it and every ES_* row - is bit-identical. PRECONDITION: the guard must be down, i.e. an explicit safety(off) or contreatwithin + contreat().
expected: Relabelling identifiers cannot change an estimate: cohort membership, not the integer used to name it, defines the estimand. sthlp:1208 places 'the cohort identifier not being a positive integer' under 'refuses, and safety(off) proceeds' and says nothing more; 'proceeds' is a statement about the run continuing, not a licence to report a label-dependent pretreatment coefficient. The pretreatment row is precisely the number readers use to judge whether the design is credible, so a silent 2.2x error there is worse than a crash. Either ado:1602 should classify on the user's own i (or a treated flag) rather than on `_i != 0`, or the positive-integer refusal should be unconditional.

title: pretrendpower() uses known-covariance references throughout, so the joint pre-trend test's size, the GLS slope CI's coverage and the mdt_wald column are all off by a deterministic function of (k, df_r) — at every cluster count
surface: pretrendpower() -- the joint pre-trend test's reference distribution (ado:10516), mdt_wald/bias_wald (ado:10557-10562), roth_slope_se/ll/ul (ado:10510-10514); any analytic or bootstrap path
claim: wooldid_ptp forms W = b'S^-1 b on the ESTIMATED pre-period covariance S = e(V_es_*) and then refers it to F(keff, df_r) (ado:10516), takes invF(keff,df_r,.95) as the cutoff mdt_wald powers (ado:10559), and builds the slope CI from the plug-in se = 1/sqrt(m'S^-1 m) with invttail(df_r,.025) (ado:10512-10514). All three are exact only when S is the TRUE covariance. With S estimated at df_r degrees of freedom the exact reference for b'S^-1 b is Hotelling's, W*(df_r-k+1)/(df_r*k) ~ F(k, df_r-k+1). Consequently a test the run labels 5% has true size 0.0784 at k=3/df_r=15 and 0.1034 at k=4/df_r=15 even under ideal Gaussian conditions, the level() slope CI covers 0.911 rather than 0.95, and the reported mdt_wald is a downward-biased estimate with the exact law mdt_hat/mdt_true ~ sqrt(chi2(df_r-k+1)/df_r).
observed: PART A (closed form, in Stata) exact size of wooldid's own cutoff, k x df_r: k=1 -> 0.0500 at 15/23/39/79/279; k=2 -> 0.0611/0.0570/0.0540/0.0519/0.0505; k=3 -> 0.0784/0.0673/0.0597/0.0546/0.0513; k=4 -> 0.1034/0.0813/0.0670/0.0579/0.0521. PART B (100,000 Mata draws of b~N(0,I), S~Wishart(I,df_r)/df_r, independent — no panel, no clustering, no DiD): k=3,df_r=15 size 0.0770, slope CI coverage 0.9108, reported se / MC sd 0.8448, median mdt_hat/mdt_true 0.9083; k=3,df_r=79 0.0544 / 0.9429 / 0.9706 / 0.9822; k=3,df_r=279 0.0498 / 0.9488 / 0.9935 / 0.9955; k=4,df_r=15 0.1033 / 0.8831 / 0.7776 / 0.8686. PART C: a 16-state DiD with i = onset cohort, fe(st), cluster(st), esprelength(3) lands exactly on the k=3/df_r=15 row (e(df_r)=15, e(roth_keff_att)=3, e(N_clust)=16). On the panel itself (s3_mc_null.do / s4_mc_power.do, 250+250 null and 400 power reps, own seeds): size 0.1120 and 0.1280, slope CI coverage 0.9120, se/sd 0.775, median mdt_hat/mdt_true 0.8919 and 0.8667, mean c2_hat/c2_true 1.4645, and power at the median reported mdt_wald(80) of 0.7350 (CI [0.690,0.777]) against a documented 0.80. Comparator on the same 250 datasets: a plain pooled event study, reghdfe ... absorb(st t) cluster(st), testparm on 3 pre-period dummies, rejects at 0.0680.
expected: sthlp:789 documents mdt_wald as 'the minimum linear pre-trend each pre-test would detect with the requested power' with 'both pre-tests conducted at the 5% level', and sthlp:1380-1384 documents e(roth_slope_ll/ul_*) as a level() confidence interval. A 5% test should have size 0.05 and a 95% CI should cover 0.95 — which is what the same code delivers at k=1 (exactly 0.0500 at every df_r, because Hotelling collapses to F(1,df)) and at large df_r (0.0498 / 0.9488 at df_r=279). The failure is therefore not an inherent limit of clustered inference: it is the specific arithmetic of plugging an estimated S into formulas that assume S is known, and it is exactly correctable by the Hotelling scaling. Two fairness qualifications belong on the record: F(q,df_r) is Stata's own test/testparm convention after any clustered fit, so wooldid did not invent the liberal reference for the joint test; what is wooldid's own is that pretrendpower() turns the same known-Sigma arithmetic into REPORTED DESIGN QUANTITIES (mdt_wald, bias_wald, roth_slope_ll/ul, roth_nissize_*), where the error is systematic and one-directional rather than one test's slightly-off p-value. sthlp:789 also says the MDT 'depends only on the design's precision, never on the estimated coefficients', which reads as a design constant; its exact 5-95% range at k=3/df_r=15 is [0.63, 1.22] x truth.

title: bootsave() under boottstat writes an observed COEFFICIENT, not the observed Wald statistic, into the _rep = 0 row of jointW_* and advW
surface: bootsave() + boottstat + jointtests / adversarial; the jointW_* and advW columns of the saved .dta
claim: In a bootsave() file written by a boottstat run, the _rep = 0 row of every jointW_<family> column and of advW -- which sthlp:557 and the writer's own comment at ado:14905 both say holds 'the observed statistics' -- instead holds element k of the observed event-study coefficient vector, because wooldid_bootsavemk pairs the k-th column of e(boot_jointW) (one column per test FAMILY) with the k-th column of wdbjobs (one column per pre-treatment HORIZON per family). The value can be negative, which a Wald statistic cannot be, and a user who reconstructs the reported p-value from the file as the help invites gets a completely different number.
observed: wooldid y unit year ttre, att cluster(unit) jointtests esprelength(2) espostlength(2) bootstrap(standard) reps(25) boottstat bootsave(bj) replace  on a 60-unit/11-year staggered panel. Reported e(joint_horiz) = .03846154 (= 1/26, i.e. no replication reached W_obs). e(boot_jointW) is 25 x 1, colname att. In bj.dta: jointW_att[_rep==0] = -.09398543 (hex -1.80f6dee4819bfX-004) -- NEGATIVE -- while the 25 replication values run from .06599616 to 6.7419682, all non-negative as Wald statistics must be. e(b_es_att)[pre2] = -.09398543, hex -1.80f6dee4819bfX-004: bit-identical. Reconstructing the add-one rank p from the file using row 0 as W_obs gives (1+25)/(25+1) = 1.000 against the reported .03846154. The adversarial twin behaves identically: with esfixedbaseperiod adversarial, e(adversarial_pval_att) = .42307692 while advW[_rep==0] = -.17179509, negative, against replications 0.17107281 to 37.347159. Mechanism at ado:14919-14931: JO = st_matrix(jobs); for (k=1; k<=cols(JW); k++) { nm = "jointW_" + strtoname(jcs[k,2]); st_store(., idx, (cols(JO)>=k ? JO[1,k] : .) \ JW[., k]) } -- jobs is wdbjobs, the observed coefficient vector wooldid_bootjwobs (ado:15310) reads to compute W_obs, not a vector of W_obs values. advW does the same with aobs = wdbaobs.
expected: Row _rep = 0 of jointW_<family> should hold that family's observed joint Wald statistic, and advW's row 0 the observed adversarial statistic. The expectation holds for three independent reasons: (1) sthlp:557 states it in terms -- 'Under boottstat the replication joint-test statistics are added as jointW_name and the adversarial statistic as advW, with the observed statistics on the _rep = 0 row'; (2) the writer's own comment at ado:14905-14906 says 'the per-replication joint and adversarial statistics under boottstat, with the observed statistic in row 0'; (3) the same help entry sells the file as self-sufficient ('so the draws can be recentred from the file alone'), and the observed statistic is the only thing in it that converts the replication statistics into the p the table printed -- every other _rep = 0 entry in the file (coefficients, se_*, w_*) really is the observed counterpart of its column, so this one column family breaks the file's own invariant. A negative value in a column documented as a Wald statistic is a sufficient tell on its own.

title: subgroups() silently rescales every exported standard error in e(V) - identical estimates, identical printed table, up to -36% on the export
surface: bootstrap(standard) + subgroups() / e(V) / wooldid_bootfin ado:14536-14576
claim: Adding subgroups() to a bootstrap run changes no estimate and no printed standard error, but shrinks e(boot_N_V) (52 -> 16 on a matched pair) and therefore moves sqrt(diag(e(V))) - the number esttab, coefplot, lincom and test use - by tens of percent on the main event-study coefficients.
observed: Two wooldid calls on the same panel (gen_skep.do), same rseed(6201), same reps(60), cluster(state); the second differs only in dropping subgroups(reg). Both printed Main Results blocks are identical line for line, estimates and standard errors alike. e(boot_N_V): 52 without subgroups, 16 with. sqrt(diag(e(V))), printed | no-sg | with-sg: ES_att_pre6 .111737 | .117609 | .082039 (-30%); ES_att_post8 .179295 | .152829 | .107046 (-30%); ES_att_post9 .150121 | .150121 | .096468 (-36%); ES_att_post0 .082181 | .078058 | .064258 (-18%); main_att .076951 | .076059 | .077015. The direction is corroborated by four independent reps(60) seeds with subgroups (run-level median exported/printed ratios .832/.876/.910/.885); the per-coefficient magnitude in any one matched pair is part bias, part 16-draw noise.
expected: An option that adds subgroup rows to the output is not a statement about the main event study. Two runs that print the same table should export the same covariance for the coefficients in that table. They do not, because subgroups() adds columns to the listwise complete-case intersection at ado:14536-14576 and every extra column costs replications. Nothing in the run says so, and the one line that names the realised count prints the token (hv-bootrank-04).

title: e(V) carries e(boot_N_V)-1 degrees of freedom but is referred to e(df_r)=G-1; on a plausible spec N_V is 4 of 60 and a nominal-95% interval covers 86.5%
surface: bootstrap(standard) / e(V) / e(df_r) / e(boot_N_V) / wooldid_bootfin ado:14536-14576
claim: Tests and intervals built from e(V) after a bootstrap run are anti-conservative by a large and computable amount, because the covariance's degrees of freedom are e(boot_N_V)-1 while test/lincom/esttab refer it to e(df_r) = G-1; e(boot_N_V) can fall to 4 of 60 completed replications on a realistic specification with no caution naming it.
observed: r4_collapse.do: my 36-state panel with SIX subgroups (census-division-sized), esprelength(5) espostlength(10), cluster(state), bootstrap(standard) reps(60): completed 60, failed 0, e(boot_N_V) = 4, K = 107, rank(e(V)) = 3, e(df_r) = 35, boot_v_posted = 1, every diagonal positive (no sentinel). The whole run prints one caution and it is about identical analytic SEs. lincom main_att returns exactly b +/- t(.975,35)*se (.564799 +/- 2.0301*.073936 = [.41470, .71490]) and `test ES_att_pre2 ES_att_pre3` returns F(2,35) with p = .00136 on a panel whose pre-trend is exactly zero by construction. r6_df.do (pure Monte Carlo, no wooldid) gives the size and coverage of exactly that construction - covariance from N_V draws, referred to F/t with df_r: (N_V=4, df_r=35) q=1 13.7%, q=2 31.2%, CI coverage .8647; (6,35) q=2 18.7%, q=4 53.8%, coverage .9032; (14,29) q=6 29.4%, coverage .9374; (30,35) q=6 10.8%, coverage .9473; (60,35) q=6 6.1%, coverage .9536.
expected: e(df_r) is documented as aligned with the reference distribution actually reported so that a hand-run test or lincom reproduces the bootdisplay(wald) numbers. It describes the cluster count, not the covariance, and after the listwise rule the covariance may rest on 4 draws. Either e(V) should rest on the replications the printed SEs rest on, or e(df_r) should describe the covariance, or the run should say what e(boot_N_V) was. wooldid's own joint and equality tests are unaffected (rank tests on a fixed metric: p = .73 and .95 on the same run), so the damage is confined to the hand-run and exported path - the very path the footer tells the user to expect numbers from.

title: The phantom bootstrap cluster needs no missing data and no singleton: a cohort treated before the estimation window opens mints one, and the obvious user-side `if` does not remove it
surface: bootstrap() cluster counting, bootdf(clusters), the <10-cluster and <6-treated-cluster cautions, permute() design size and its treated-cluster caution
claim: On a perfectly balanced panel with every variable present on every row, a cohort whose onset precedes the estimation window - which wooldid drops by documented design (sthlp:73) - is still counted as a bootstrap resampling unit and as a permutation design unit, so e(boot_df) is inflated, the few-treated-cluster caution is suppressed, and the reported number of possible permutation assignments is overstated by orders of magnitude. Unlike the missing-outcome trigger, the natural hygiene filter `if y < .` does not fix it.
observed: r7_novel.do A (16 states, 4 with onset 1996, window 2000-2011, NO missing data): e(N)=288 and e(N_clust)=12 with and without those states; e(boot_df)=e(df_r)=15 with them, 11 without. permute(shuffle): reported possible assignments 10,810,800 vs 5,940. r10_alwaystreated.do A (20 states, 6 always-treated): e(N)=336, e(N_clust)=14 both sides; e(boot_df)=19 vs 13; the 'only 4 treated cluster(s) are available for resampling' caution fires on the ORACLE only (r10_alwaystreated.log:181). r10 B (permute, three seeds): possible assignments 465,585,120 vs 12,012 with e(N)=336 both sides; p .0732/.0832, .3661/.3827, .0033/.0100. r11_remedy.do B: `if y < .` leaves e(boot_df) at 15 (no change at all); only `if missing(onset) | onset >= 1999` brings it to 11.
expected: e(boot_df) should be the live cluster count minus one and the guards should see the live treated clusters, because the estimation sample is identical either way (e(N) and e(N_clust) prove it). The expectation holds for the same reason HV-BOOT-01's does: a cluster contributing zero rows to e(sample) is not a resampling unit. What makes this the important case is that it requires no data defect whatsoever, and wooldid's own remedy for pre-sample onsets - truncate the estimation window - is precisely the operation that creates these clusters.

title: Nothing anywhere records which of the two bootstrap unit regimes ran

claim: The regime flag `wdb_nest` is c_local'd back to the shell (ado:8997) and used only to decide whether to print the A10 covariate caution (ado:407). title: sthlp:1307 documents the wrong e(b)/e(V) row names for subgroups (_s# suffix vs the actual _SG<value>_ infix)
surface: subgroups() + e(b)/e(V) naming contract (sthlp:1307)
claim: sthlp:1307 states 'Under subgroups() each subgroup's rows take the suffix _s#.' The e(b)/e(V) column names actually use an INFIX _SG<value>_ and carry the subgroup VALUE, not a sequence number. That paragraph is precisely the one that says these names 'are what esttab, coefplot, lincom, test and the permtstat/bootsave() tables address a coefficient by', so a user who follows the help to build a coefficient name gets a not-found error. The _s<value> SUFFIX convention is real but belongs to a different family -- the e() matrix and scalar NAMES -- which the help documents correctly elsewhere.
observed: With subgroup levels 1, 3, 7, 99 the full e(b) colname set is: main_SG1_att, main_SG3_att_it, main_SG7_att_i, main_SG99_att_itime, pretreatment_SG1_att, pretreatment_SG99_att_itime, ES_att_SG3_pre2, ES_att_SG99_post1, ES_att_it_SG1_post0, and so on (enumerated in full in the '=== e(b) colnames (NAMING CONTRACT) ===' section of p04_joint4.log). Meanwhile e(b_es_att_s99), e(V_es_att_it_s3), e(escomp_s7) and e(numpre_att_s99) do use the _s<value> suffix. Note that even there the token is the VALUE (s99), never an index (s4).
expected: main_att_s1, main_att_s2, ... per sthlp:1307. Neither the infix form nor the use of the raw subgroup value is stated anywhere in that paragraph.
refuter_note: Core claim exactly true; one sub-point is not a defect. 'The names carry the subgroup VALUE, not a sequence number' does not by itself diverge from the help: '#' is Stata help idiom for 'a number', so _s99 satisfies _s#. The real and sufficient defect is POSITION (an infix _SG1_, not a suffix) and SPELLING (SG, not s). Severity medium stands because that paragraph is the naming contract for every downstream consumer. NOTE FOR THE COORDINATOR: this is a DUPLICATE -- agent hv-sg-names filed the identical divergence independently as HV-SGNAME-01 with broader coverage (including grep -c '_SG' wooldid.sthlp == 0, i.e. the true convention appears nowhere in the 326 KB help). Two independent discoveries, one defect; they should be merged.
refuter_did: Own panel, subgroup levels 1/3/7/99, 80-column e(b). Typed the six names a user gets by following sthlp:1307 -- main_att_s1, main_att_s2, main_att_it_s1, pretreatment_att_s1, ES_att_post0_s1, main_att_s99 -- into lincom: ALL SIX return r(111). Typed the five infix names main_SG1_att, main_SG3_att, main_SG99_att, ES_att_SG1_post0, pretreatment_SG1_att: all five rc 0. Confirmed the _s<value> token is real but belongs to the e() NAME family, by fetching e(b_es_att_s1), e(b_es_att_s99), e(escomp_s3), e(numpre_att_s99) -- all rc 0. sthlp:1307 is verified on the pinned build as the one paragraph that tells lincom/test/esttab/coefplot users how to address a coefficient.

title: simultaneousbands: the analytic sup-t band covers 0.752 at nominal 0.90 and 0.843 at nominal 0.95 with 12 clusters
surface: simultaneousbands, analytic engine (e(esband_engine)==analytic-simulated); e(esband_<fam>) and e(esband_crit_<fam>)
claim: The analytic simultaneous-band engine builds its critical value as the level() quantile of max_j |Z_j| over 10,000 draws of Z = L * rnormal(m, nd, 0, 1) (wooldid_esbanda, wooldid.ado:16695-16746) -- a standard-normal sup quantile taken over the ESTIMATED correlation matrix treated as known -- while the pointwise intervals printed on the same table use invttail(G-1). The band is therefore too narrow and its measured simultaneous coverage falls materially below level(), with the deficit growing as the cluster count falls.
observed: mc_band10.txt (i=cg, cluster(unit) G=12, 10 periods, 6 horizons, R=400): band simultaneous coverage 0.752 at nominal 0.90 (3 binomial SE 0.045; ~9 SE of deficit) and 0.843 at nominal 0.95 (3 SE 0.033; ~9 SE). On the same runs the analytic POINTWISE intervals are correctly calibrated per horizon (0.877-0.951 at nominal 0.90; 0.944-0.975 at nominal 0.95), so the covariance and the pointwise machinery are fine. Mean band critical value 2.2031 (L=90) and 2.4886 (L=95) against invttail(11,.025)=2.2010. mc_band.txt repeats it at G=40, R=400: 0.875 at nominal 0.90 and 0.930 at nominal 0.95 -- 1.7 and 1.8 SE low, below nominal at both levels in the same direction, the size predicted by t(39)/z=1.010. Verified repro run at level(90), G=12, R=200: 0.780 simultaneous coverage, mean crit 2.20272, invttail(11,.05)=1.79588, invnormal(.95)=1.64485.
expected: The help states that "a simultaneous band covers every horizon of the family at once with that probability [level()]". It does not. CONFIDENCE IS SPLIT ON PURPOSE: that the band under-covers is certain (R=400, ~9 binomial SE at both levels, with correctly calibrated pointwise intervals on the same runs). That the cause is the z-versus-t reference is only probable -- rescaling the same sup multiplier from z to t(G-1) buys about 12% extra width at G=12, and whether that closes the whole 10.7-point deficit or whether the rest comes from taking the sup over an estimated correlation matrix as if it were known is not established here.
refuter_note: No correction to the claim -- the split confidence was the right call and the mechanism is now established as the dominant term. Quantified: the t-versus-z reference accounts for 0.068 (common scale factor) to 0.100 (independent per-horizon scale factors) of the 0.112 deficit, the truth lying between because cluster-robust SEs across horizons share cluster draws and so have correlated but not identical scale errors; plugging the ESTIMATED correlation in as if known contributes ~0.016 more (it biases the crit DOWN 2.7%, since sample correlations from 12 clusters are too large in magnitude, which shrinks a sup quantile); at most ~0.03 is left unattributed. The prober's 'about 12% extra width from rescaling z to t(G-1)' is the right order: the sup-quantile t/z gap is 12.8% at G=12. Their G=40 figure remains measured; my ~3% at G=40 is computed from t(39)/z, not measured.
refuter_did: Own MC on a DGP built so the true effect is a function of the RELATIVE period only, identically across cohorts and units, which makes every weighting scheme give the same horizon truth and removes all estimand ambiguity from the coverage number. 250 draws (p3_mcband.do), 12 clusters, i=cg, cluster(unit), esprelength(3) espostlength(2), simultaneousbands level(90), 5 banded horizons, e(esband_engine)=analytic-simulated, e(df_r)=11: measured simultaneous coverage 0.788 at nominal 0.90 (3 binomial SE 0.057, ~6 SE low), while POINTWISE coverage on the same runs is 0.872-0.928 per horizon with se/sd 0.96-1.16, so the covariance and pointwise machinery are sound. Mean reported e(esband_crit_att) = 2.1536; the ORACLE crit (empirical q90 of max_h |b_h-truth_h|/se_h) = 2.7574, so the band is 78% of the width it needs. The self-contained repro reproduces it independently on its own 200 draws: coverage 0.780, mean crit 2.1537, oracle 2.8292, ratio 0.761, pointwise 0.875-0.950. I then ANSWERED the question the prober explicitly left open, with 400,000-draw simulations on the MC's own empirical horizon-error correlation and coverage recomputed by rescaling each draw's own reported crit: normal sup on the TRUE correlation 2.2112 (+2.7%, coverage 0.804); t(11) sup with a common scale 2.4950 (+15.8%, 0.856); t(11) sup with per-horizon scales 2.6054 (+21.0%, 0.888); oracle 2.7574 (+28.0%, 0.904).

title: The two all-zero-VCV cautions blame analytic clustered standard errors that were never requested and point the reader at a caution that did not print
surface: the all-zero-VCV cautions (wooldid_amescreen mode(vzero), ado:12983 and ado:1567) under contreat() with a non-clustered VCE
claim: When the estimation command returns an all-zero covariance under contreat(), ado:12983 prints 'The issue is likely related to continuous treatment effect estimation coupled with use of analytic clustered SEs, with clusters occuring at a high level of aggregation. Consider ... if finer clustering levels are non-viable' -- gated only on contreat() being non-empty and on the R1 screen not having fired, with no condition on a cluster-type VCE being in force. ado:1567 then prints 'This is a property of the specification, not a numerical accident: see the cell-containment caution above for the mechanism and for the alternatives'. Under bare robust there are no clusters, the named remedy does not exist, the referenced cell-containment caution never printed (the R1 detect only runs over clusvars, which is empty), and the plain-regress leg of finding B shows the zero IS an artifact of the engine.

The issue is likely related to continuous treatment effect estimation coupled with use of analytic clustered SEs, with clusters occuring at a high level of aggregation. Consider switching to use of bootstrap SEs, IM p-values, or randomization inference if finer clustering levels are non-viable.' followed by 'Caution: the estimation command returned an all-zero variance-covariance matrix ... This is a property of the specification, not a numerical accident: see the cell-containment caution above for the mechanism and for the alternatives'. So all three pieces of advice on that run are unreachable - a finer clustering level for a run with no clustering, a cell-containment caution that never printed, and conditional robust SEs that are already in force. refuter_did: Ran lattice(all 3) + contreat() + bare robust with no cluster() token anywhere in the command on my own fixture, NOT quietly, and read the full caution block in the log. Confirmed that the only caution printed above the two all-zero-VCV cautions is the fastcollapse one, i.e. no cell-containment caution exists on the page the second caution points at.

title: fastnose silently overrides permanalyticse under permute(), and the run then asserts in three places that the analytic SEs and e(V)/e(V_es_*) are there
surface: permute() x fastnose x permanalyticse
claim: Under permute(), wooldid refuses fastnose+permtstat and fastnose+permtci with r(198) ("permtstat/permtci randomize on t-statistics, which fastnose does not compute") but ACCEPTS fastnose+permanalyticse, which asks for the same object. fastnose then wins silently: no analytic standard errors are computed, no e(V), no e(V_es_*), no e(b_es_*). The run nevertheless posts e(perm_analyticse)=1, prints the header "se_analytic = the analytic cluster(unit) standard error, shown for reference only" over an entirely blank se_analytic column, and prints the footer "The standard-error column is the ANALYTIC standard error (se_analytic, permanalyticse) ... e(V) and e(V_es_*) hold the analytic covariance, so test or lincom run by hand on them are analytic, not permutation, quantities" — an instruction that cannot be followed because no covariance exists.

title: The reps() resolution Caution is unreachable without cluster(), contradicting the help's unconditional promise
surface: reps() / bootstrap() cautions
claim: sthlp:534 states that wooldid 'prints a Caution naming that grid whenever it is coarser than .05'. The entire caution block at ado:6455-6478 sits inside `if "`clus'" != "" {`, so an unclustered bootstrap never gets it, however coarse the grid.
observed: repro_br2.log: `att cluster(unit) bootstrap(standard) reps(12)` prints 'Caution: with reps(12) the coefficient p-values fall on a grid of 0.167 (2/reps)...'. The identical `att bootstrap(standard) reps(12)` prints nothing. `att bootstrap(standard) boottstat reps(4)` (floor 2/5 = .4, so no coefficient p can reject at 5% whatever the data say) also prints nothing. probe2.log adds the bootdisplay(wald) unclustered case, also silent. The string 'Caution: with reps(' occurs exactly once in repro_br2.log, under the clustered run.
expected: Either the caution fires on unclustered runs too, or the help stops promising it unconditionally. The block was deliberately relocated on 2026-09-13 (RF-2) so that it is printed BEFORE the replications run, precisely so a user is warned before spending the time; the unclustered user loses that and the actionable 'use at least 39/40 replications' guidance. permute()'s sibling caution in wooldid_permctl is NOT conditional and fires on every run (seen in probe2.log). Mitigation that limits severity: the post-run footer still names the realized resolution.
refuter_did: Ran five arms on my own 40x10 panel. A: `att cluster(unit) bootstrap(standard) reps(12)` prints 'Caution: with reps(12) the coefficient p-values fall on a grid of 0.167 (2/reps)' (probe_br2.log:90). B: the identical call without cluster() prints nothing before the run. C: `att bootstrap(standard) boottstat reps(4)` (floor 2/5 = .4) prints nothing. D: `att bootstrap(standard) bootdisplay(wald) reps(6)` prints nothing. E: permute()'s sibling caution at permreps(20) DOES print. The string 'Caution: with reps(' occurs exactly once in the log, on arm A. Confirmed the structural cause by reading: the whole caution block at ado:6455-6478 sits inside the `if "`clus'" != "" {` opened at ado:6456. The help's promise is at sthlp:535 (the finding cites 534, one line off, immaterial) and is unconditional. Mitigation is real and I verified it: the post-run footer still names the realized resolution on the unclustered arms (probe_br2.log:184, :203). What is lost is RF-2's entire purpose - warn before the replications are paid for - plus the actionable 'use at least 39/40 replications' guidance.

title: bootdf(clusters) counts clusters that contribute no rows to e(sample); one printout says 'N clusters = 17' and 't(19)'
surface: bootdf(clusters) / bootstrap() cluster map frame
claim: G for bootdf(clusters), and the pool bsample draws from, is the number of clusters with a non-missing cluster() value inside the user `if` -- NOT the number of clusters in the estimation sample. A cluster whose rows are all removed by markout (suppressed outcome, missing control) is counted in the degrees of freedom and is drawn as an empty slot, so e(boot_df)=e(df_r) disagrees with e(N_clust)-1 on the same run.
observed:
20 states, 3 units each, 6 years, outcome suppressed (missing) in 3 states.
  A (suppressed states left in the data): e(N_clust)=17, e(boot_df)=e(df_r)=19
  B (same estimation sample, 3 states physically dropped): e(N_clust)=17, e(boot_df)=e(df_r)=16
  identical point estimate in A and B; FAIL_DF=1.
The printed header of run A reads 'N clusters = 17; N = 306 (54 obs dropped from initial sample)' while the footer of the SAME run reads 'e(V) and e(df_r) carry the standard-deviation family referred to the t(19) distribution'. invt(19,.975)=2.093 vs invt(16,.975)=2.120.
Also measured: the dead clusters are still drawn, so 3, 2 and 2 of 499 replications failed outright across three seeds in A.
RETRACTED sub-claim: a +4.4% bootstrap-SE gap I first read at reps(99) did NOT survive: at reps(499) over three seeds the A/B ratio is 0.97312 / 0.99366 / 1.04714 (mean 1.00464, sign inconsistent). The standard error itself is not materially inflated.
expected: wooldid.sthlp:554: 'bootdf(clusters) instead uses the t distribution with G-1 degrees of freedom, where G is the number of cluster() groups', and 'Under every setting e(df_r) is aligned with the reference distribution actually reported ... so a test or lincom run by hand afterwards reproduces the reported p-values'. The run's own e(N_clust) is 17, so the reference distribution should be t(16) as run B shows. Cause: wooldid_bootrun ado:8911-8955 builds `smp` as (ifr==1) & !missing(clusv) with no markout against the estimation sample; wdb_C is counted on it (ado:8954), returned as wdb_r_nclus (ado:9537), and becomes wdbdf = nclus - 1 in wooldid_bootwire (ado:9573).
refuter_note: No correction to the claim; two extensions. The mechanism is not specific to a suppressed outcome -- ANY markout source does it, including a missing control variable and a zero analysis weight, and the zero-weight case (a zero-population cell) is the most ordinary of the three and is not a data error. The retracted SE-inflation sub-claim stays retracted: I did not re-test it, and their own 3-seed measurement is consistent with a null.
refuter_did: Built my own 26-state panel and drove clusters out of the estimation sample by THREE different routes, each paired with a control run where the same states are physically dropped: (A/B) outcome suppressed in 4 states -> e(N_clust)=22 with e(boot_df)=e(df_r)=25 vs 21 in the control, identical point estimate 1.5699826238; (C/D) controls(xctl) missing in 3 states -> 23 vs df 25, control df 22; (E) analysis weight exactly 0 in 3 states -> 23 vs df 25. The boottstat arm of A carries the same df. I also confirmed the printed contradiction on one page: header 'N clusters = 22; N = 528 (96 obs dropped from initial sample)', footer '... referred to the t(25) distribution'. Read-side: wooldid_bootrun ado:8911-8925 builds smp as (ifr==1) & !missing(clusv) with no markout, ado:8954 counts wdb_C on it, and the error three lines below calls that same object 'the estimation sample'.

title: A treated i that enters an unbalanced panel at or after its own onset is dropped silently, and the help describes the rule at the sample level
surface: sample construction / which cohorts reach e(gteffects); ado:12018-12020 and 12055-12059; sthlp:73
claim: wooldid removes, with no message of any kind, every treated `i` whose OWN first observed period is at or after its effective onset (ado:12018-12020 computes `mint' = gegen min(t), by(i); ado:12055-12059 zeroes `ifvar' where ttre <= mint). sthlp:73 documents this as "cohorts treated before the sample begins are dropped", which does not describe a firm treated in 2004 that enters a 2000-2010 register in 2004. Those units never appear in e(gteffects) either, so the cohort-by-period table gives no hint, and the reported ATT silently becomes the ATT over the subset of treated units that happen to have pre-treatment coverage.
observed: One 70-firm register 2000-2010, 30 firms treated in 2004, only the first-observed year of ten of them varied, i = unit (repro_lateentry_silentdrop.log): entrants from 2000 -> e(N)=770, N_dropped=0, 30 firms in e(gteffects), att=2.598970; from 2003 -> 740, 0, 30, att=2.532414; from 2004 -> 660, N_dropped=70, only 20 firms in e(gteffects), att=1.818684; from 2005 -> 660, 60, 20, att=1.715990. Grepping the whole 2004/2005 blocks for "Caution" finds none (the 2003 block does print an unrelated reference-period-forcing caution, so cautions are not suppressed generally). p15_lateentry.log adds the granularity comparison on IDENTICAL data: i=unit gives att=1.7223 with 10 firms dropped, i=cohort gives att=2.4337 with 0 dropped - a 41% swing between two legitimate choices of i. The only trace is the generic "(70 obs dropped from initial sample)" line, which is shared with if-drops and markout drops.
expected: Either the drop is announced, or the help says what the rule actually is. The expectation is anchored twice: (1) sthlp:73 promises a SAMPLE-level rule ("treated before the sample begins"), and the sample begins in 2000 while these firms are treated in 2004 with seven post-treatment years each; (2) the IDENTICAL drop performed twelve lines earlier for anticipation() at ado:12045 DOES print "Caution: anticipation(#) places the effective onset of N unit(s) at or before their first usable pre-period; those unit(s) and their M observations are dropped from the sample" - so the package already treats this drop as worth naming. Under timetrends the stricter two-pre-period version IS documented (sthlp:1055) though still silent at runtime.
refuter_note: Two legs of the prober's argument should be dropped or rewritten. (1) The '41% swing between two legitimate choices of i' is not evidence of a defect. With a coarse i, min(t) is the COHORT's minimum, so a cohort with any early-entering member survives and the late entrants' post-onset rows are retained inside its cells -- my arm P1C (same data, i = onset cohort) gives N_dropped=0 and keeps everyone. That is a different estimand by construction, not a bug. (2) The reported number is not wrong given identification: a treated unit with no pre-period cannot contribute a DiD contrast, and csdid/did_imputation drop it too. The defect is exactly and only the silence plus the help wording. Medium severity is nevertheless correct, resting on the package's own internal precedent (the anticipation() twin is announced).
refuter_did: Built my own 30-firm 2000-2010 register (12 treated in 2004, 18 never-treated) with engineered heterogeneity so the TRUE ATT over all 12 treated is 2.0. Arm P1A (all firms observed from 2000): att=1.995807, N=330, N_dropped=0, 12 treated i in e(gteffects). Arm P1B (firms 1-4 enter the register only in 2004, their own onset year): att=1.004200, N=286, N_dropped=28, only 8 treated i in e(gteffects). Programmatic grep of the P1B block for 'Caution' returns 0 -- the only trace is 'N = 286 (28 obs dropped from initial sample)', the same line an if-drop or a markout produces. Mechanism verified in code: ado:12020 gegen mint = min(t) if ifvar==1, by(i); ado:12055-12057 nopre = max(ttre<=mint) then replace ifvar=0, unit-level, no message. Also verified sthlp:73 says only 'cohorts treated before the sample begins are dropped', and that the arithmetically identical anticipation() drop twelve lines earlier (ado:12039-12047) DOES print a named Caution.

title: permanalyticse is a complete no-op under fastnose, and the run prints a header and a footer asserting the analytic standard errors are in the table and in e(V)
surface: fastnose x permute() x permanalyticse; e(wdid_vcespec), e(perm_analyticse), the replay footer at ado:11679, wooldid_validate's fast-mode gates at ado:5374-5412
claim: permute() + permanalyticse + fastnose is accepted by wooldid_validate, computes no analytic standard error at all, and is byte-identical to the plain permute() fast-mode default — yet it selects the permanalyticse header, prints the permanalyticse footer claiming e(V) and e(V_es_*) hold the analytic covariance, and posts e(perm_analyticse)=1. e(V) does not exist and test/lincom return r(321).
observed: repro_FN01_FN02.log: `wooldid y cohort t ttre , fe(unit) cluster(cohort) permute(shuffle) permreps(40) permanalyticse fastnose ...` returns rc 0 with e(wdid_vcvstate)=='absent', e(V) absent (confirm r(111)), `test main_att = 0' r(321), e(perm_analyticse)==1, and e(wdid_vcespec) == 'randomization inference (permute(shuffle), 40 replications); se_analytic = the analytic cluster(cohort) standard error, shown for reference only'. The printed se_analytic column is '.' on every row, and the footer (ado:11679) prints 'The standard-error column is the ANALYTIC standard error (se_analytic, permanalyticse), shown for reference only; ... e(V) and e(V_es_*) hold the analytic covariance, so test or lincom run by hand on them are analytic, not permutation, quantities.' The same run WITHOUT fastnose gives vcvstate 'analytic-blocks', e(V) present, test rc 0. QUANTIFIED with the RNG pinned (p11_permseed.log, set seed 777777 before each call, permreps(60), full %21x differencing): the fastnose arm differs from the plain permute() fast-mode default in EXACTLY THREE items and in NO number at all — e(cmdline), e(wdid_vcespec), and the presence of e(perm_analyticse)=1. Every matrix and cell (e(perm_p), e(perm_ci), e(perm_kernel), e(b), e(wdidmainresults)) is byte-identical. So permanalyticse is a complete no-op under fastnose; its only trace is a false header, a false footer, and a machine-readable flag a replay or downstream tool would believe. The code assumes otherwise at ado:8246: 'Fast mode only: under permanalyticse an e(V) exists and the tools already work from it.'
expected: Either a refusal (the way permtstat and permtci are refused with fastnose at ado:5882, and unconditionalse/impvalues/pretrendpower at ado:5383-5406), or permanalyticse winning over fastnose so the analytic standard errors it exists to restore are actually computed. What must not happen is a requested option being dropped in silence while the output asserts it took effect.
refuter_note: The claim is right and slightly UNDER-stated on two points the prober missed. (1) They argue only from code. sthlp:1234, the engine-compatibility table, says: 'fastnose — refused / it IS the default. Fast mode is what makes the permutation affordable; permanalyticse opts back in.' The help therefore promises that permanalyticse opts the analytic SEs back in; the code lets a typed fastnose override it (ado:5448 sets the fast default only when permanalyticse is absent, but a user-typed fastnose survives and drives marginsdof=nose). So this is a documented-vs-actual divergence, not merely an internal inconsistency. (2) The run does not print the fast-mode header either: the header line is 'Standard Errors: randomization inference (...)', and 'SEs and related materials are not estimated in fast mode.' is absent — nothing anywhere in the output says fast mode is in force. Severity stays medium: every posted number is a correct permutation quantity, and the missing e(V) fails loudly (r321), so the damage is the false footer, the false e(wdid_vcespec) and the machine-readable e(perm_analyticse)=1.
refuter_did: My own binary panel (96 units, T=2001-2012, four treated cohorts + never-treated), three arms with 'set seed 4242' pinned before each, permreps(40), cluster(cohort), esprelength(2) espostlength(2). ARM A permute+permanalyticse: rc 0, e(wdid_vcvstate)='analytic-blocks', e(V) present, test rc 0, e(perm_analyticse)=1. ARM B permute+permanalyticse+fastnose: rc 0 (accepted, not refused), e(wdid_vcvstate)='absent', confirm matrix e(V) r(111), test r(321), lincom r(321), yet e(perm_analyticse)=1 and e(wdid_vcespec) is the permanalyticse string verbatim ('se_analytic = the analytic cluster(cohort) standard error, shown for reference only'). The footer at ado:11679 prints 'The standard-error column is the ANALYTIC standard error (se_analytic, permanalyticse) ... e(V) and e(V_es_*) hold the analytic covariance' while e(V) does not exist; the printed se_analytic column is '.' on every row. ARM C plain permute: same vcvstate/e(V) state but the honest footer and no e(perm_analyticse). Diffed ARM B against ARM C: e(perm_p) in %21x and e(wdidmainresults) are identical line for line, so permanalyticse is a complete no-op, exactly as claimed.

title: A weight written as a +/- expression is pasted verbatim into the estimand-weight arithmetic: silently wrong att_it/att_i/att_itime on the customvce()/unconditionalse paths, and an uninformative error everywhere else
surface: weight expression x customvce() / unconditionalse x att_it/att_i/att_itime (plus the error-message surface on the default reghdfe path)
claim: wooldid keeps the raw weight-expression TEXT in `w' (ado:607) and pastes it into arithmetic at ado:1619/1630/1637/1644/1650, so a weight whose top-level operator is + or - binds wrong: [aw = wf+wm] makes w_att_it = wf + wm/W_it instead of (wf+wm)/W_it. TWO DISTINCT BEHAVIOURS: (a) on the DEFAULT estimation path reghdfe's own guard (`unab exp : wf+wm, min(1) max(1)`) refuses the expression first, so the user gets r(198) "+ invalid name" / r(111) "variable 2*k not found" / r(101), none of which mentions weights, and safety(off) does not change it; (b) on the customvce() and unconditionalse paths, which estimate with plain regress, the expression is ACCEPTED and the three cell-weighted estimands are silently wrong while att (whose weight has no denominator) is exact.
observed: probe17, customvce(robust), no safety(off), with wf+wm constructed to equal wtot on every row (asserted): att 1.35806635445 vs 1.35806635445 (reldiff 0); att_it 1.35539110268 vs 1.35837510195; att_i 1.36654660882 vs 1.35953352747; att_itime 1.36252940698 vs 1.35932150079. Max relative 5.132e-03, max absolute 7.013e-03. customvce(cluster i) moves 2.202e-03; unconditionalse robust safety(off) moves 5.132e-03. rc 0, no error, no caution. On the default path: [aw=wf+wm] r(198) "+ invalid name"; [aw=2*k] r(111) "variable 2*k not found"; [aw=k/2] r(198); [aw=int(k)] and [aw=cond(k>2,k,1)] r(101); [aw=(ka+kb)] r(198). Plain `regress y post i.i i.t [aw=wf+wm]` accepts the same expression rc 0.
expected: Identical results, because wf+wm equals wtot on every row. Every official Stata command materialises a weight expression before using it, and Stata's weight syntax is universally [weight = exp]; wooldid's help (sthlp:57) says [aw/pw=weights] and nowhere restricts the weight to a bare variable name. The mechanism is visible in the source: ado:1644 is `qui gen double `w_att_it' = `w' `customweighttext'/`w_per_it'` and `customweighttext' is `* cwm', so with customweightmultiplier() even att becomes wf + wm*cwm.
refuter_note: Three additions/corrections, none of which unseat the claim. (1) The default-path error is INHERITED FROM reghdfe VERBATIM and the cell collapse is not implicated: for every one of nine expressions, wooldid-default, wooldid-nofastcollapse and bare `reghdfe' return the IDENTICAL rc and message (2*k->111 'variable 2*k not found'; k/2, k*2, wf+wm, (wf+wm), 1/pscore->198; int(k), cond(k>2,k,1)->101), while bare `regress' accepts all nine. safety(off) cannot help for the same reason (I inferred this rather than measured it). (2) The finding under-sells its own realistic half: [pw=1/pscore] -- inverse-probability weighting, the commonest weight expression in applied work -- dies r(198) '1 invalid name' on the DEFAULT path with no mention of weights. The silent-wrong branch needs customvce()/unconditionalse AND a top-level +/-, which is narrow; the crash branch is any expression at all. (3) New symptom worth naming: when the second term is small the three cell-weighted estimands silently CONVERGE ON att (1.46815/1.46806/1.46804 instead of spanning 1.4204-1.4618), so the visible symptom is 'all my estimands agree', which reads as reassuring rather than as a bug.
refuter_did: Did NOT run their script. Rebuilt the case from the claim with an asymmetric prediction only the text-paste mechanism can satisfy, on my own 40-unit x 10-period staggered panel. [aw=wf+zero] with zero==0 everywhere: att, att_it, att_i, att_itime all BITWISE identical (+1.76fb4bd29be62X+000 = 1.464771975439270), SEs identical too; the same data as [aw=wf] gives four distinct values (1.464771975, 1.458344351, 1.415271428, 1.417598312). Mirror: [aw=zero+wm] is bitwise identical to [aw=wm] on all four estimands and all four SEs. That is exactly the signature of `gen double w_att_it = wf+zero/w_per_it' -> wf, i.e. the cell division is annihilated and every cell-weighted estimand silently becomes att. On the finding's own setup (wtot==wf+wm asserted row by row, customvce(robust), rc 0, no caution) my magnitudes are LARGER than reported: att exact; att_it reldiff 4.33e-03; att_i 1.425732958 vs 1.468059194, reldiff 2.97e-02; att_itime 1.420357847 vs 1.468041601, reldiff 3.36e-02. unconditionalse robust safety(off): SE(att_it) 0.126915925 vs 0.143077097, a 12.7% SE error. customweightmultiplier(cwm) breaks att too (1.455847603 vs 1.464679018, 6.07e-03). Separately (p1_exprgrid.do) I ran a 9-expression x 5-engine grid to attribute the crash branch.

title: contreatwithin silently disables two data-integrity screens the help says gate on the user's own safety() value
surface: contreatwithin / safety() working-value rewrite (ado:4829, 4959, 4973)
claim: The safety-value rewrite at ado:4829 (contreatwithin + contreat() sets the WORKING safety value to off) disables the positive-integer `i` assert (ado:4959) and the float-above-2^24 caution (ado:4973). The help states the opposite: sthlp:1188-1200 says "Roughly half the sites gate on your own value and are therefore untouched by that rewrite - every data-integrity assert ...", sthlp:913 says "the data-integrity screens ... still run unless safety(off) is given explicitly", and sthlp:1207 lists "the cohort identifier not being a positive integer" among the checks bypassed only by an explicit safety(off). The help's enumeration of working-value-gated sites (sthlp:1209) covers only the collinearity family, the relative-time range asserts and the control-availability count.
observed: With t and ttre stored as float 8-digit calendar codes (tdate = 20000101 + (t-2000)*10000), the binary run prints the float-rounding caution twice (p02b_ctw_map.log:922 and :928); adding `contreat(dose) contreatcontrols(basic) contreatwithin` prints it ZERO times on the same variables, with no safety() typed by the user. Separately, `i` coded 0 (0-indexed cohort codes, e.g. a pandas or merge export) is refused r(411) "cohort0 must consist of positive, non-zero integers" on the binary path and accepted with no message under contreatwithin. A non-integer `i` under contreatwithin dies r(452) - an uninformative Stata error where the named r(411) would have fired.
expected: Per the help, both are data-integrity screens and should survive the contreatwithin rewrite; only the estimability relaxations and the collinearity family should not. title: A wooldid failure after the internal regression leaves reghdfe's (or ppmlhdfe's) saturated model in e(), destroying the user's previous results
surface: shell rc-gated epilogue (ado:67-97) / every failure raised between ado:1476 and ado:4051; reached here via contreat()+contreatcontrols(untreatedZero), fe(), ccc_absorb(), poisson
claim: wooldid never clears, holds or restores e() around its worker. Any error raised between the internal estimation command (reghdfe at ado:1476, ppmlhdfe at ado:1462/1468) and wooldid's own `ereturn post` (ado:4051) leaves that internal saturated model as the session's current estimation results, silently replacing whatever the user had in e() -- including a previous successful wooldid run. `grep -c "ereturn clear" wooldid.ado` = 0 and `grep -c "_estimates hold|_est hold" wooldid.ado` = 0; the shell's rc-gated epilogue (ado:79-97) restores the frame, emptycells and level and drops scratch estimates, but never touches e().
