The movement is above the project's stated 1e-10 indifference threshold, which is why it is reported rather than silently dropped; it is almost certainly reghdfe's alternating-projections path rather than anything in wooldid's own arithmetic, and it never reaches the point estimates. Recorded so a future bisect does not mistake it for a regression.
refuter_note: The phenomenon is real but the claim as stated does not generalize. 'Point estimates invariant to 1e-16 everywhere' is false: on my simple design the point estimate is the only thing that moves and the SE is bit-identical. The magnitude does not reproduce: the largest SE movement I could reach across five designs is 7.4e-11 relative, BELOW the project's 1e-10 indifference threshold and ~350x smaller than the claimed 2.6e-8. The prober's attribution guess is right and I confirmed it directly - reghdfe alone moves both b and se under a sort reversal - so nothing here is wooldid's own arithmetic. 'regtol did not shrink it' reproduces (it slightly enlarges it), and regtol IS genuinely wired to reghdfe's tol(1e-N) at ado:1476, so that leg tested something real. Severity stays low.
refuter_did: Applied the project's pristine-twice doctrine first: three repeats of the same weighted/clustered/controlled event-study call on identical data are bit-identical, and two repeats on the reversed sort are bit-identical, so the pairs are clean and nothing is nondeterministic. Then measured two designs. Simple design: under gsort -i -t the SE is BIT-IDENTICAL (+1.60335fc695684X-004 both ways) while the POINT ESTIMATE moves (...e990 -> ...e98b, ~1e-15 relative) - the opposite of the claimed pattern. Hard design (ill-conditioned absorb, weights over ~3 orders of magnitude, near-collinear controls x1/x2, cluster(region)): both move, rel|db| = 7.8e-15 and rel|dse| = 6.7e-12 at regtol(9), 2.3e-14 and 7.4e-11 at regtol(12) and regtol(13). A monotone id relabel (i = i*7+3) is bit-identical. Attribution: plain reghdfe y x1 [aw=fwt], absorb(i t) vce(robust) tol(1e-9) forward vs reverse on the same data returns b identical=0 and se identical=0 by itself.

title: Under fastnose the ame dose-slope void screen never runs: wooldid prints and now returns eight fabricated zeros the analytic twin refuses, under a caution saying "The estimates stand"
surface: fastnose + contreat(); the R6/SI-A4 dose-slope void screen at ado:11958; e(b_es_ame), e(wdidmainresults), the printed ame rows
claim: On a continuous-treatment design where every treated cohort-period dose-slope term drops for multicollinearity (the help's own named case: the dose is constant within each cohort), the analytic run withholds e(b_es_ame), blanks every ame cell and names the non-identification; adding `fastnose` prints every ame cell as exactly 0, posts e(b_es_ame) with eight exact zeros, suppresses the naming caution, and asserts that the estimates stand.
observed: 30 cohorts x 6 units x 12 periods, i = cohort, dcoh = exp(0.2*mod(i,5)) constant within cohort (range 1.00-2.23), yV = y0 + 0.5*dcoh*D, command `att robust contreat(dcoh) contreatcontrols(basic) esprelength(4) espostlength(4) esfixedbaseperiod`. ANALYTIC: prints the R6 caution ("every treated cohort-period dose-slope term ... was dropped for multicollinearity ... the within-cell average marginal effects (ame) ... are NOT IDENTIFIED in this design - the regression's ame entries are structural zeros, not estimates"), main:ame = ., pretreatment:ame = ., all eight ES_ame rows = ., e(b_es_ame) rc 111. +FASTNOSE: the R6 caution is ABSENT; main:ame = 0, pretreatment:ame = 0, all eight ES_ame rows = 0; e(b_es_ame) rc 0 with all eight entries exactly +0.0000000000000X-3ff; e(numpre_ame) = 4; and the only ame message printed is "Caution: no horizon of the ame event study has an identified variance, so e(b_es_ame) posts without e(V_es_ame). The estimates stand...". The att side is bit-identical between arms (main:att .95929975 both), so nothing separates the fiction from the sound half. FAIR MITIGANT (measured, not suppressed): both arms DO print the generic caution "a treatment period coefficient interacted with something ... was dropped for multicollinearity. This could imply your results are not identified ... triggered 165 times total" — but it names no block, fires on many benign designs, and under fastnose is immediately followed by "The estimates stand". Mechanism: ado:11958 gates the whole R6/SI-A4 screen on `"`fastnose'" == ""`, so amevoid stays 0 and the guard at ado:4148 `!(amevoid & strpos(f2ky,"ame")==1)` lets the matrix through. REACH (probe7_permvoid.do): permute() without permtstat/permanalyticse sets `local fastnose fastnose` internally at ado:5448, so its OBSERVED run skips R6 too and prints the same zeros with p_perm 1.000 and [0,0] intervals — but permute names every affected row in its own degeneracy caution, so plain fastnose is the worst case. bootstrap() is CLEAN, measured in probe8_bootvoid.do: R6 fires, ame rows print ., e(b_es_ame) withheld, and the engine adds "the following estimates have no identified observed value and are excluded from bootstrap inference: main_ame pretreatment_ame ES_ame_pre3 ES_ame_pre2 ES_ame_post0 ES_ame_post1", even though every replication and the rep-0 comparator run under fastnose and return ame = 0.
expected: The R6 caution's own closing sentence reads "You can ignore this check if you specify safety(off), but be careful: with safety(off) the ame output will contain the structural zeros" — the author has already ruled that these zeros may reach the output only behind an explicit opt-out AND a warning. fastnose is not an opt-out from safety; its documented promise (sthlp:40) is only that standard error estimation is skipped for specification search. It should not silently inherit the safety(off) outcome on this screen minus the warning. The printed 0 is not a near-miss: the DGP's structural dose coefficient is 0.5 and the design simply does not identify the within-cell ame, which is exactly why the analytic path refuses. The sthlp entry for e(b_es_*) also states flatly that on such a design "both e(b_es_ame*) and e(V_es_ame*) are withheld ... the structural zeros surviving only in the raw e(b)" and that a honestdid/pretrends handoff "finds no ame input at all" — false under fastnose since 6fe814d. And sthlp:1325's own closing clause, "the estimates remain meaningful even where their uncertainty is unavailable", is true of the att family and false of the ame family here.
refuter_note: The claim's propositions are all true and reproduce, but its framing - an undocumented divergence in which fastnose 'silently inherits the safety(off) outcome on this screen MINUS the warning' - is false on both halves. (1) The skip is DOCUMENTED, in the option entry for the very option that creates the design: sthlp:902, the contreat() paragraph, ends '...Only the raw e(b) coefficient vector retains the structural zeros, since Stata cannot post missing coefficients, and the check is skipped under {it:fastnose}.' The prober cited sthlp:40 and sthlp:1325 and missed this. git log -S dates that sentence to 81c284b (2026-09-10), a week before the pinned build. (2) safety(off) is EQUALLY silent - measured in arm A3: no caution names the zeros there either, because the safety(off) sentence lives INSIDE the R6 caution that safety(off) skips. sthlp:1209 says so in advance: 'the ame rows print the regression's structural zeros instead of missing values, and without the caution that names them. This is the same output an explicit safety(off) produces.' So fastnose inherits the safety(off) outcome exactly, not minus a warning. (3) The convention is deliberate and repeated: the interactivecontrols twin carries the same gate and sthlp:1068 documents it too - '(that check does not run under {it:fastnose} or {it:safety(off)}, where the reduction is silent)', same commit. What survives is NOT a doc-vs-code divergence at high severity but a low-severity INTRA-HELP inconsistency plus a UX wart: the fastnose option paragraph (sthlp:286-297), the paragraph a fastnose user actually reads, promises 'only point estimates are produced' and that point estimates differ from a full run by 'absolute differences on the order of 1e-15', whereas on a d3 design the difference is . -> 0; that paragraph never mentions the collinearity screens. One clause there closes it. Blast radius is bounded: the same paragraph instructs re-running without fastnose before reporting, and that re-run refuses the ame; bootstrap() refuses fastnose; permute() names every affected row.
refuter_did: Reproduced the BEHAVIOUR exactly on my own administrative-shaped d3 design (i=state, dose = state policy generosity constant within state, measured max within-state SD 1.9e-14, range 0.5-3.0, structural dose effect 0.40), three arms on the same panel. A1 analytic robust: the full R6 caution prints, every ame cell is missing, e(b_es_ame) rc 111. A2 +fastnose: R6 caution ABSENT, main:ame=0, pretreatment:ame=0, all seven ES_ame rows print 0, e(b_es_ame) posts with seven exact zeros (%21x +0.0000000000000X-3ff), e(numpre_ame)=3, and the only ame message is 'no horizon of the ame event study has an identified variance ... The estimates stand'. att side identical in both arms (.70128565). Mechanism as stated (ado:11958 gates R6 on fastnose==""). BUT I then ran the arm the prober did not: A3 robust safety(off) - IDENTICAL output to fastnose, ame rows print 0, e(b_es_ame) posts, and NO caution names them. I also ran the permute arm myself (p4_permute_d3.do): permute(shuffle) permreps(20) does put ame=0 / p_perm=1.000 / [0,0] into a reportable table, but the engine names every affected row ('the permutation distribution is degenerate (every completed draw equal) for: main_ame pretreatment_ame ES_ame_pre4 ... ES_ame_post3; those permutation p-values are uninformative'), so FN2 does not escalate. And I probed the sibling screen (p3_permute_and_ic.do): the BS-3 interactivecontrols twin at ado:12005 has the identical fastnose gate and behaves identically.

title: Under boottstat the studentized joint/equality statistics are not ereturned, though the help lists them; boot_sgW is computed and discarded
surface: bootstrap() + boottstat + jointtests + subgroups(); e(boot_jointWobs)/e(boot_sgW)/e(boot_sgWobs)/e(boot_advWobs)
claim: On the studentized (boottstat) joint-test branch wooldid posts e(boot_jointW) and e(boot_advW) but never e(boot_jointWobs), e(boot_sgW), e(boot_sgWobs) or (on any path) e(boot_advWobs), while the fixedmetric branch posts all four and the permute() twin posts all six. sthlp:1340 lists e(boot_sgW) as where the replication equality statistics live in BOTH families (carving out only the *obs pair) and claims a boottstat run stores enough that "every reported studentized number is reconstructable from e() by name"; sthlp:1391 promises e(boot_jointWobs) under bootstrap() with no carve-out at all.
observed: Same data, same options apart from boottstat. boottstat: e(boot_jt_family)=studentized, HAS boot_jointW=1, boot_jointWobs=0, boot_sgW=0, boot_sgWobs=0 — and the run nonetheless PRINTS `p-value for joint test that all SGs have the same att: 0.2500`. No boottstat: e(boot_jt_family)=fixedmetric, all four present. `grep 'ereturn matrix boot_'` shows boot_advWobs posted nowhere; the permute twin posts perm_jointW/Wobs (ado:8443-4), perm_sgW/Wobs (ado:8570-1), perm_advW/Wobs (ado:8638-9). THE FOUR ABSENCES ARE TWO DIFFERENT GAPS, which matters for the fix: (1) boot_jointWobs/boot_advWobs exist at run time as the tempnames wdbjobs/wdbaobs (ado:365, handed to wooldid_bootsave at ado:437) and I measured the observed statistic in row 0 of jointW_att = .2704913 in a bootsave file — a two-line posting omission; (2) wooldid_bootsgw (Mata, ado:15380+) takes only `outloc` and `nloc` as outputs, builds Wobs and the Wr colvector internally and discards them — there is no matrix to write them to, so the studentized equality statistics are computed and thrown away, a design gap rather than an oversight. The reading of sthlp:1340's "(the latter two without boottstat)" does not matter: under the natural reading (the *obs pair) boot_sgW is promised and absent; under the alternative reading (the two sg* matrices) boot_jointWobs is promised and absent. Either way one promised matrix is missing, and sthlp:1391 carries no carve-out.
expected: Either the four matrices exist under boottstat as sthlp:1340/1391 say, or the help states the studentized carve-out completely. The expectation holds because (a) the fixedmetric branch of the SAME engine posts all four, (b) the permute() engine posts all six companions including perm_advWobs, so the intended convention is unambiguous, and (c) the reported studentized joint and adversarial p-values are add-one ranks of W_r against W_obs, and W_obs is nowhere in e() by name, so the sthlp:1340 sentence "every reported studentized number is reconstructable from e() by name" does not hold for them (it can be recomputed from the preserved analytic covariance, but not read).
refuter_note: The absences are real and the doc-vs-code divergence stands, so the claim's headline is right and severity low is right. But the stated MECHANISM is wrong in a way that matters for the fix. The prober wrote that boot_jointWobs/boot_advWobs 'exist at run time as the tempnames wdbjobs/wdbaobs (ado:365, handed to wooldid_bootsave at ado:437)' and that they 'measured the observed statistic in row 0 of jointW_att = .2704913 in a bootsave file', concluding it is 'a two-line posting omission' distinct from the boot_sgW design gap. wdbjobs and wdbaobs are NOT observed W statistics: they are the observed EVENT-STUDY COEFFICIENT vectors (two-level stripe, equation = family key, one column per pre-treatment horizon) that wooldid_bootjwobs (ado:15310) and wooldid_bootadvobs consume to COMPUTE W_obs = b' V^+ b, returning it in a Mata-set local that is then discarded. So all three studentized gaps are the same kind of design gap as boot_sgW, not a posting oversight -- a two-line `ereturn matrix` of wdbjobs would post a coefficient vector under a name promising a Wald statistic. The value the prober measured in their bootsave file is itself an instance of a separate, worse defect I found while checking this (see new finding hvr-bootsave-jointwobs-01): the bootsave writer pairs those two objects positionally, so row 0 of jointW_* is a coefficient, not a statistic. Also a minor point: sthlp:1340's 'the latter two without boottstat' is ambiguous, but only under the alternative reading; under the natural reading boot_sgW is promised under boottstat and is absent, and sthlp:1391 promises boot_jointWobs under bootstrap() with no carve-out at all -- both measured absent, so the divergence holds either way, as the prober said.
refuter_did: Built a 60-unit/11-year panel with a subgroup and ran five paired fits, listing the presence of all twelve boot_*/perm_* W matrices after each. boottstat+jointtests: boot_jointW PRESENT, boot_jointWobs ABSENT, jt_family=studentized, joint_horiz=.6923 printed. Same without boottstat: boot_jointW and boot_jointWobs both PRESENT, jt_family=fixedmetric. boottstat+jointtests+subgroups(): boot_jointW PRESENT, boot_jointWobs/boot_sgW/boot_sgWobs all ABSENT, yet joint_att_allsgssame=.0556 is printed. Same without boottstat: all four PRESENT. permute()+subgroups(): perm_jointW/perm_jointWobs/perm_sgW/perm_sgWobs all PRESENT. The adversarial row came from the heavy arm r3_bootW.do, whose first run flushed before its deadline kill: R1_BOOTTSTAT|boot_advW|PRESENT and R1_BOOTTSTAT|boot_advWobs|absent, with e(adversarial_pval_att)=.09677419 printed (r3_bootW.log:365-380). I also read wooldid_bootsgw (ado:15380+) and confirmed it emits only outloc and nloc, building Wobs and Wr as Mata locals and discarding them.

title: Nine options are accepted, do nothing and say nothing without their parent — contradicting the help's own stated policy
surface: saveplots(), cfxplottypes(), cfxplotnose, makecfxplotsbysg, latticeignoreweights, ccnoabsorb, contreatpoly(), suppresssgprimaryeffects; sthlp:1181 refuse/caution/skip policy
claim: Nine wooldid options (saveplots(), saveplots()+makeplots with no horizon request, ccnoabsorb, contreatpoly(), suppresssgprimaryeffects, cfxplottypes(), cfxplotnose, makecfxplotsbysg, latticeignoreweights) are accepted with rc 0, leave the entire returned e() byte-identical, print nothing, and write no file, when the option they modify is absent. wooldid.sthlp:1181 states as policy 'No accepted option is a silent no-op'.
observed: All ten paired cases report `===VERDICT ...: results-identical=1 output-identical=1` — full e() dumped in exact %21x hex (every scalar, macro and matrix) is identical, and the isolated named log is byte-identical. suppresssgprimaryeffects is the one exception and only in its own echo macro e(wdid_suppresssgpe); every estimate is identical. File evidence: `saveplots(pfx1)` with no plot option, `saveplots(pfx2)` with makeplots but no esprelength()/espostlength(), and `saveplots(pfx4)` with horizons but no makeplots all write NOTHING; the control `makeplots esprelength(2) espostlength(2) saveplots(pfx3)` writes pfx3_ES.dta and pfx3_ES_att.gph. cfxplottypes() is worse than inert: its own token validator sits INSIDE the makecfxplots block (ado:5188), so `cfxplottypes(psot 1.5 nosuchvariable)` is accepted in silence without the parent and refused r(198) with it. REFUTATIONS of the seeded list: (a) contreatcontrols() without contreat() IS screened — 'Error: you cannot request continuous treatment controls without specifying a continuous treatment variable.' r(198); (b) lattice() without contreat() (ado:4818) and makecfxplots without contreat() (ado:5268) ARE screened, so the cfx orphans are only reachable on a run that already has contreat(); (c) makecfxplotsbysg and cfxplotnose ARE documented as silently inert at sthlp:976 and sthlp:978, so only the behaviour half of the recon claim holds for those two (and sthlp:976's 'no caution' is itself slightly wrong — makecfxplotsbysg tightens the subgroup-value-length caution from 8 digits to 7 at ado:12294 even with no makecfxplots). NEW members the recon did not name: suppresssgprimaryeffects, and contreatelasticitytype() (see hv-noparent-F2).
expected: wooldid.sthlp:1181, the {marker refusepolicy} section, states: 'No accepted option is a silent no-op, and no check downgrades itself: safety(off) is the single documented way to move a refusal to a caution or to skip a check... It has never suppressed a disclosure about what was estimated - if the run changed your specification, it says so whatever safety() is set to.' The author has treated this as a defect class five times already, with screens of exactly this shape: lattice()->contreat() error (ado:4818), makecfxplots->contreat() error (ado:5268), cfxlattice()->makecfxplots CAUTION (ado:5307), esrelativeto()->esfixedbaseperiod CAUTION (ado:5371), and poisexpresults->poisson error (ado:5479) whose own comment reads 'SI-9 (author-ruled 2026-08-25): formerly accepted silently with zero effect'. The nine above were simply missed by that sweep.
refuter_note: The documentation half is refuted for FIVE of the nine, not two. They are explicitly documented as inert and silent, in the very words the finding says the help forbids: ccnoabsorb (sthlp:1121, 'the option is inert and silent on a run with no continuous treatment'); contreatpoly() (sthlp:917, 'without contreat() the option is otherwise inert: nothing reads it and nothing is said about it'); cfxplotnose (sthlp:978, 'Without makecfxplots the option is inert: nothing reads it, and no message is printed'); makecfxplotsbysg (sthlp:976, 'silently inert without either: no error and no caution'); and makeplots with no horizon request (sthlp:807, 'No plot is drawn unless at least one event-study horizon is requested'). With five explicit entries by the same author in the same file, sthlp:1181's 'No accepted option is a silent no-op' cannot be read as the promise the finding needs; its own closing clause scopes it to runs where 'the run changed your specification', and an unreached child option changed nothing. What survives is (i) a narrow doc-internal inconsistency: four members (saveplots alone, suppresssgprimaryeffects, cfxplottypes, latticeignoreweights) are inert by implication only and sthlp:1181 overstates against its own entries; and (ii) the cfxplottypes() VALIDATION GAP, which is not a no-op claim at all and is the one genuinely live item - filed separately in new_findings. My own unseeded sweep of every other valued option found that wooldid DOES announce ignored options elsewhere (esrelativeto prints 'has no effect without esfixedbaseperiod and is being ignored'; cfxlattice draws a caution), so the author's practice is mixed rather than uniform in either direction.
refuter_did: Wrote my own 80x10 staggered panel and ran nine paired legs (saveplots alone; makeplots+saveplots with no horizon; ccnoabsorb; contreatpoly(3); suppresssgprimaryeffects; cfxplottypes(post 1); cfxplotnose; makecfxplotsbysg; latticeignoreweights) against a common baseline, plus a file-existence test and a control run that does request horizons, plus a separate paired test of the cfxplottypes token validator. BEHAVIOUR HALF REPRODUCES EXACTLY: all nine rc 0, mreldif(e(wdidmainresults), baseline) = 0 for every one, nothing printed beyond the ordinary table, saveplots(p1) and makeplots saveplots(p2) wrote NO files, while the control makeplots esprelength(2) espostlength(2) saveplots(p3) wrote p3_ES.dta and p3_ES_att.gph. I then read every one of the nine option entries in the help rather than only the policy sentence at sthlp:1181. I did not independently check e(wdid_suppresssgpe); I accept the prober's observation on that macro and my silence claim covers printed output and the results matrices.

title: bootsave()'s observed row is on the wrong scale, contradicting the help by a measured factor
surface: bootsave() under bootstrap(bayes) bootalpha(size)
claim: sthlp:557 states that under bootalpha(size) the bootsave file's _rep=0 row holds 1/N, 'N the number of observations in the estimation sample'. It actually holds 1 over the unscreened frame's row count (wdb_nrows, ado:8949), so the observed row cannot be used to recentre the draws as documented.
observed: Section C, same run as HV-BOOT-02: the saved file's _rep==0 row holds w = .00297619 = 1/336, while e(N) = 164. The oracle file correctly holds 1/164. The companion identity the same help paragraph states ('it is the rows, sum over c of n_c times w_c, that sum to 1') is likewise an identity only over the unscreened frame.
expected: 1/164, i.e. 1/e(N), as the help says in those words.
refuter_note: The divergence is real and verbatim, but one sentence of the claim overreaches: 'the observed row cannot be used to recentre the draws as documented' is wrong, because recentring the coefficient draws uses the COEFFICIENT columns of the _rep==0 row, not the w_ columns; only the weight-scale identity is affected. And ado:8949 shows 1/N_frame is precisely the scale on which the help's own companion identity (sum over c of n_c times w_c equals 1) holds, so the file is internally consistent. What is wrong is the help's phrase 'estimation sample'. This is a help-text fix on a diagnostic file, so low rather than medium.
refuter_did: Same run as HV-BOOT-02, with bootsave(). Read the saved file: the _rep==0 row holds w_1 = 0.0029761905, which is exactly 1/336 (the unscreened frame row count) while e(N)=160; the oracle file holds 0.00625 = 1/160. Checked the help text verbatim: sthlp:557 says the _rep=0 row 'holds 1/N, N the number of observations in the estimation sample'. Then read ado:8949 to see what scale the file is actually on.

title: permexact reports 'exact shares with no Monte-Carlo error' over a reference set it pruned, and the p moves 4x with a preprocessing step that cannot change e(sample)
surface: permute() + permexact; the possible-assignment count and the exactness claim in the randomization-inference footer
claim: Under permexact the enumeration ranges over the unscreened cluster set, so assignments that put every onset on clusters with no outcome data are enumerated, found non-estimable and dropped. The reported p is therefore conditioned on estimability while being labelled exact, and the footer names a reference-set size that is neither the set used nor the set the analysis supports.
observed: Section D: 7 units (unit 1 treated 2003, unit 2 treated 2004, units 3-7 never treated); units 1 and 7 report no outcome. cluster(unit) permute(shuffle) permexact. Full data: '40 of 42 replications completed; 42 possible assignments', plus 'Elements not estimable in every enumerated assignment (exact shares over a reduced reference set) ... main_att'; exact att p = 0.1000. title: The maxvar preflight omits lattice() and contreatpoly(), so its bound is short by a multiplicative factor and a textbook continuous-treatment run dies r(907) at Stata's DEFAULT maxvar with the guard silent
surface: lattice() / contreatpoly() / contreat() with the safety() maxvar preflight (ado:1342-1374, si8demand at ado:1371); documented at sthlp:1167 and sthlp:1207
claim: si8demand (ado:1371) = si8cells*(1 + (contreat!="")) + si8ilev + si8tlev + 200 models exactly one dose slope per treated cohort-by-period cell, but the estimated block (ado:1476) is the full factorial i._i#i._t#i.targetflag ## i.latticevar ## c.dose(^1..^p). The true column count is therefore ~(1+L)(1+p)/2 times the bound. On a 50-state county panel with lattice(all 5) the preflight predicts 1320 variables and stays silent while the run needs 6115 and dies r(907) at the default c(maxvar)=5000. This contradicts sthlp:1167's unqualified promise that 'if the count of variables the specification requires exceeds the current maxvar setting, wooldid halts with an informative error before estimation rather than failing mid-run with r(907)'.
observed: Run end-to-end (log alongside). 50 states, 45 with staggered 2005-2012 onsets, 15 counties each, 20 years, continuous time-invariant county exposure. Stata 19, UNTOUCHED default c(maxvar)=5000. PREFLIGHT PREDICTS si8demand = 1320 (cells=525, ilev=50, tlev=20). ACTUAL columns no lattice = 1053; ACTUAL columns lattice(all 5) = 6115 (confirmed independently by fvexpand at maxvar 20000 in p2b_default_maxvar.log). RUN1_RC = 0 (42 s, no lattice). RUN2_RC = 907 (same spec + lattice(all 5)). 1320 < 5000 < 6115: the bound is short by 4.63x and the gap straddles the default limit exactly. Bisection on a smaller panel (25 states, si8cells=213, si8demand=671, p1_bisect.do/p1b_extend.do): rc 907 at maxvar 2048/2500/3000, rc 0 at 3500 and at 12000 (162 s, att=1.0478 vs design truth ~1.02) -- true demand in (3000,3500], miss factor 4.5x-5.2x. Structural fvexpand counts on the same panel: 429 columns for cell##c.dose, 2579 for cell##i.lat5##c.dose (exactly x6.01 = 1+L), 3439 for lattice(all 3)+contreatpoly(3), 3869 for lattice(all 5)+contreatpoly(2). contreatpoly is omitted by the same formula: at maxvar 2048, lattice(all 3) gives rc 0 while lattice(all 3) contreatpoly(3) gives rc 907, with si8demand = 671 on both rows. My reconstruction of the formula is validated exactly, not assumed: a 120-state design made wooldid print 'requires at least 2882 variables (about 1271 treated cohort-by-period interaction terms)', matching my hand computation on both numbers. Under verbose the death is located at the reghdfe call itself, i.e. mid-run. NOTE on what is NOT contradicted: the code comment's zero-false-positive invariant survives (lattice only adds columns, so the bound stays below the truth) -- the retracted 2026-09-16 defect stays retracted. What is broken is that the bound is vacuous on this family, and that sthlp:1167/1207 promise more than a lower bound delivers.
expected: sthlp:1167 states without qualification that the preflight halts before estimation whenever the required variable count exceeds maxvar, and sthlp:1207 lists it among the refusals that prevent a mid-run r(907). The code comment at ado:1342-1348 calls si8cells*(1+contreat) the count of the treated interaction terms. For the guard to serve its stated purpose the bound must at least scale with the specification; instead it is invariant to the single steepest scaling axis the help itself names ('lattice() is the steepest axis, at roughly the 1.9th power of K' -- sthlp:1272). The blind spot is worst exactly where wooldid's own advice sends the user: measured on one panel varying only which variable is i, coarse i (state, 20 rows/cell) gives si8demand 671 vs 2579 actual (3.84x, guard silent) while unit-level i (county, 1 row/cell) gives 9240 vs 17063 (1.85x, and the guard fires because 9240 > 5000). ado:1371 and sthlp:1163 both tell a user whose specification is getting big to 'specify unit-level fixed effects via fe() and swap i to a coarser level of aggregation' -- which is precisely the move into the blind spot.
refuter_note: Three corrections. (a) SEVERITY: medium -> low. The mechanism is not a defect but a ruled design with a written retraction; only the unhedged help sentence survives, and Stata's own r(907) text supplies the `set maxvar` remedy. (b) 'MID-RUN' OVERSTATES THE COST: my RUN 2 died in 0.194 seconds (timer list 2). The r(907) is raised at factor-variable expansion, before any fitting, so nothing expensive is wasted -- what is lost is wooldid's pre-estimation prep (validation, _i/_t construction, the three gegen tag passes, collapse setup), 0.19 s on 8,800 rows and proportionally more on a large panel. sthlp:1167's own phrase 'failing mid-run with r(907)' overstates it too. (c) The ruling that closed this mechanism rests on a zero-false-positive premise that my new finding sk-maxvar-fp falsifies, so the closure is unsupported -- but that belongs to the new finding, not to a re-litigation of this one.
refuter_did: Read the ruling record first, then rebuilt the claim on my own data twice. (1) RECORD: the mechanism half is already closed. known_bydesign.md section 5, review_process/open_defects.md:63-85 (the retraction, read verbatim), and review_process/guard_cost_2026-09-16.md:172-175 and :342 already record that si8demand is a deliberate lower bound, that a run can pass the preflight silently and then die on Stata's own r(907), and that the under-prediction exceeded 2x on a 200x20 panel (cells=2004 ilev=200 tlev=20 demand=2424 vs maxvar 5000). The prober's 4.6x on the lattice axis is a sharper measurement of a closed item. (2) DOC: the retraction is SILENT on the help. sthlp:1167 promises halting whenever the required count exceeds maxvar, sthlp:1207 lists it among refusals, and `grep -c "lower bound" wooldid.sthlp` = 0 -- the hedge exists only in an ado comment. That half is a genuine doc-vs-code divergence and it survives. (3) OWN REPRO, my own shapes, not theirs: s4_lattice_own.do (40 states x 10 counties x 18 years, i=state, lattice(all 4)/(all 5)) gave si8demand 1030 vs realized ~3685/~4191 columns (3.6x/4.1x); s6_lattice_big.do (50 states x 8 counties x 22 years, lattice(all 5), untouched default maxvar 5000) gave si8demand 1568 -> preflight SILENT, realized ~6827 columns, RUN1 no-lattice rc 0 in 44.0 s, RUN2 rc 907. 1568 < 5000 < 6827 reproduces the arithmetic on a panel the prober never used.

title: The omission is a FAMILY, not a lattice special case: interactivecontrols() and coarsecohortcontrols() break the same bound with no lattice at all
surface: interactivecontrols(), coarsecohortcontrols() (and ccc_absorb(), unmeasured) vs the si8demand preflight at ado:1371
claim: si8demand models one term family only -- cells x (1 or 2). Every other construct that multiplies the cohort-by-period cell block is outside the formula: lattice() (ado:1087/1117), contreatpoly() (ado:1107-1116), coarsecohortcontrols() -> i._i#i._t#(vars) (ado:1138), and interactivecontrols() -> i._i#i._t#1.targetflag#c.(vars) plus i.t#c.(vars) (ado:1171). Patching si8demand for lattice() alone would leave three further multipliers uncovered.
observed: Same 25-state county panel, NO lattice anywhere, si8demand = 671 on every row, set maxvar 2048. Baseline (att contreat(exposure) contreatcontrols(basic)): 429 columns, rc 0. Adding interactivecontrols(x1 x2 x3 x4 x5 x6 x7 x8): 2293 columns, rc 907. Adding coarsecohortcontrols(i.reg) with a 12-level region factor instead: 2997 columns, rc 907. Neither option moves si8demand by a single variable. Eight interactive controls is an ordinary demographic vector and a 12-level region or industry factor is an ordinary coarse control, so both arms are realistic specifications.
expected: A preflight whose stated job is to predict the specification's variable demand should read the assembled regressor macros (contreatinj, interinject, coarsecontrolinserter, contreatcontrolinserter) rather than a fixed cells*(1|2) formula. The structurally right fix is either to count from those macros, or -- far cheaper -- to wrap the estimation command in capture and translate rc 907 into wooldid's own message naming the option that blew the budget. Reported because it changes the shape of the fix implied by hv-lat-01.
refuter_note: The observation is true and reproduces on my own data, but it is the SAME root as hv-lat-01 (si8demand models one term family) and is covered by the same ruling. It is fix-scoping information rather than a second defect, so medium -> low. It matters because it rules out the narrow 'patch si8demand for lattice()' fix -- and, combined with my new finding, because a correct fix has to move the bound in BOTH directions, not just up.
refuter_did: Confirmed by inspection that interinject (ado:1171), coarsecontrolinserter (ado:1138) and ccc_absorbinserter (ado:1145) are all appended to the same reghdfe call at ado:1476 while si8demand (ado:1371) reads none of them, then measured it on my own data: 30 states x 8 counties x 14 years = 3,360 rows, 26 treated, `set maxvar 2048`, NO lattice anywhere. si8demand = 642 on EVERY arm (cells=199, ilev=30, tlev=14), so the preflight is silent throughout. ARM 1 `att contreat(exposure) contreatcontrols(basic)` -> rc 0. ARM 2 same + `interactivecontrols(x1..x8)` -> rc 907. ARM 3 same + `coarsecohortcontrols(i.reg)` with a 12-level region -> rc 907. ARM 4 plain binary att + interactivecontrols(x1..x8) (si8demand 443) -> rc 0. Eight demographic controls and a 12-level region factor are ordinary specifications and neither moves si8demand by one variable.

title: The few-cluster caution keys on the TREATED cluster count, so a 10-cluster panel with 6 treated and 4 never-treated is warned about nothing while its bootstrap rejects at 12-20%
surface: few-cluster caution message (wooldid.ado:6491-6499)
claim: The few-cluster caution at wooldid.ado:6491-6499 triggers on the number of TREATED clusters being below 6. A G=10 design with 6 treated and 4 never-treated clusters therefore prints no caution at all, even though on exactly that design bootstrap(standard) rejects a true sharp null at .122 and bootstrap(bayes) at .163-.204.
observed: grep of the pinned build at ado:6491-6499 shows the guard condition is on the treated-cluster count < 6. My design has exactly 6 treated clusters, so the caution never prints in any of the ~500 wooldid invocations across the study — verified by grepping every .log in the probe directory for the caution text: zero hits. Meanwhile the measured levels on that silent design are bootstrap(standard) .122 [.057,.242] and bootstrap(bayes) .163-.204.
expected: A caution about few-cluster inference should key on the quantity that governs the bootstrap's behaviour — the total cluster count, or at least both counts — rather than the treated count alone. As written there is a band of designs (6-9 treated clusters, any number of controls) that are squarely in the regime the caution exists to flag and receive no warning. This is a UX/guard-threshold issue, not a wrong number, hence low severity; I rate confidence certain because the trigger condition is read directly off the pinned source and the absence of the message is verified across every log.

title: semielasticity on the default engine lets margins' raw Mata traceback through: r(3598) 'variable __00001O not found' with no wooldid-level diagnostic
surface: semielasticity on the default reghdfe engine (and contreatelasticitytype(eydx)/(eyex) by the same route); margins failure trapping
claim: When reghdfe's FE-free prediction _cons+Xb goes non-positive, margins' factor-variable eydx dies r(3598) with a Mata stack naming an internal tempvar. wooldid does not trap it, so the user sees `variable __00001O not found / st_data(): 3598 / __marg_cr_eval(): ...` and nothing that names semielasticity, the prediction, or the option responsible. Falsifiable: on strictly positive y with strictly positive true fitted values, the default engine dies r(3598) while customvce(robust) returns the correct semi-elasticity on the same data.
observed: Design (part X2): 40 units, 10 periods, treated units high-baseline (alpha 26.5..34) with onset t=6, controls low-baseline (~6), effect -20, sigma 0.3. min(y) = 5.47 (strictly positive); the true fitted value from `reg y i.i i.t post` has min 5.98 and is positive on all 400 rows; but reghdfe's _cons+Xb is NEGATIVE on 80 of 400 rows (min -3.57), because _cons = mean(y) - b*mean(post) = 16.4 while b = -20. `wooldid y i t ttre, att semielasticity` -> r(3598), printing `variable __00001O not found / st_data(): 3598 Stata returned error / __marg_cr_eval(): - function returned error / deriv__call2user_v(): ... / st__marg_cr_compute(): ...`. `wooldid y i t ttre, att semielasticity customvce(robust)` -> -1.107274232 with rc 0, which is the correct answer (mean ln((alpha-20)/alpha) over the treated-post cells is about -1.1). PROVENANCE CHECKED (pE_checks.log E2): the traceback is Stata's own margins behaviour, not wooldid's -- with no wooldid at all, `reghdfe y i.post, absorb(i.i i.t)` then `margins, eydx(post)` prints the identical stack (`variable __000013 not found / st_data(): 3598 ...`), while the continuous spelling gives the informative r(459) 'could not calculate numerical derivatives -- discontinuous region with missing values'.
expected: sthlp:243-245 warns only that semielasticity 'tends to require large samples and a y-variable that is not sparsely distributed'. A user whose y is strictly positive and well spread has met that condition, so an r(3598) Mata traceback naming an internal tempvar is uninformative on its face and gives no route to the real cause (the prediction margins divides by has gone negative because the absorbed fixed effects are missing from it). wooldid traps and renames other engine failures -- e.g. the ppmlhdfe rc-3200 fallback at ado:1463-1469 -- so leaving this one raw is inconsistent with the package's own error-handling posture. Severity is LOW rather than higher precisely because the error is upstream and loud: nothing silently wrong is reported. The root cause is FP-SEMIELAS-FE, which stays high.

title: permsave()'s failed replication rows are not "all missing", though the help says they are
surface: permsave() file layout; wooldid.sthlp:493 (and, untested, bootsave() at sthlp:557)
claim: The help's permsave() entry (wooldid.sthlp:493) states that a failed replication 'keeps its row, all missing'. It does not: the onset_<clustervalue> columns the same paragraph documents are populated with the drawn assignment on a failed replication's row, so a user who identifies failed replications as 'the rows where every value is missing' finds none of them on a file that has several.
observed: On a run with e(perm_reps)=100, e(perm_completed)=93, e(perm_failed)=7 and permsave(pF_save): the file has 101 rows and 16 non-_rep columns (6 coefficient, 10 onset_). Testing 'every non-_rep column missing' (the help's wording) finds 0 failed rows. Testing only the 6 coefficient columns finds all 7 (_rep = 24 53 71 80 81 82 90). _rep 24 lists main_att, pretreatment_att, ES_att_pre2, ES_att_pre1, ES_att_post0, ES_att_post1 all missing, beside onset_6 = 2017 and onset_10 = 2017 -- the assignment that failed, intact (hand-refitting it errors r(459); see pD_draworacle.do, PD_FAILREFIT_RC=459).
expected: Either the sentence says what the file does, or the file does what the sentence says. The expectation holds because the sentence is the only statement in the help about how to recognise a failed replication in the file, and it is in the same paragraph that introduces the onset_ block, so the two halves contradict each other. The practical consequence is in exactly the workflow PERMSEM-01 concerns -- reconciling the permsave file with e(permdist_b) and e(perm_jointW). It cost me one wrong probe: pB2_rowalign.do reports PB_SAVE_FAILEDROWS = 0 because it swept the onset_* columns into the all-missing test. Keeping the assignment on a failed row is arguably the better behaviour (you can see WHICH assignment failed), so the fix is to the sentence plus a note that the failed-row test is on the coefficient columns. bootsave() at sthlp:557 makes the same statement about a file that also carries w_<cluster> resample columns; not tested here.

title: The IM degeneracy message blames 'deterministic or noiseless data' on a panel whose idiosyncratic sd is 0.55; the real cause is the cluster geometry
surface: impvalues degeneracy scrub message (ado ~2066-2075); impvalues with a cluster() crossing i
claim: When every cluster has the same composition over the i-by-relative-period cells -- a cluster crossing i, e.g. regions each holding equal numbers of every cohort -- the per-cluster reads collapse to a single value, impvalues blanks every se/t/p/lb/ub, and the message tells the user their data is deterministic or noiseless and asks them to verify their input. The collapse is a property of the cluster geometry, not of the data's noise, so the message sends the user to look in the wrong place and there is nothing in the data for them to verify.
observed: PART 3 of the repro (also p4_mech.do block C): i=cg, cluster(reg) with 5 regions crossing the cohorts, on a panel with unit random intercepts sd 0.70 and AR(1) idiosyncratic errors sd 0.55. Output: 'Caution: for one or more Ibragimov-Muller estimates the per-cluster estimates were numerically identical, so the cross-cluster (IM) standard error is not identified; ... A collapsed IM standard error usually reflects deterministic or noiseless data - please verify your input if this was not expected.' The att row prints with se, t, p, lb_95ci and ub_95ci all missing; e(df_r)=4 is still posted. The analytic run on the same data reports se 0.166731876 without difficulty.
expected: A diagnostic message should name the condition that actually fired. The guard's predicate is that the per-cluster reads are numerically identical, which under this geometry happens because each cluster's weight profile over the cohort-by-relative-period cells is identical -- no amount of noise in y changes that, as the reads are a deterministic reweighting of one pooled fit. A message naming the geometry ('every cluster has the same composition over the cohort-by-relative-period cells, so the per-cluster reads carry no information; use a cluster variable whose clusters differ in cohort composition') would point at the fix. This is an observable failure rather than a silent wrong number, hence low, but it is the same root cause as mcci-01 at its limit.

title: The RF-6 comma refusal for bootsave() prints a remedy that itself writes a silently mis-named file
surface: bootsave() comma refusal message (ado:6287)
claim: The error message that exists to stop `bootsave(name, replace)` writing a file literally called 'name, replace.dta' instructs the user to write `bootsave(name  replace) replace`, and following that instruction returns rc 0 and writes 'name replace.dta' - a different silent mis-naming of the same kind.
observed: probe_br1.log:106 prints 'Error: bootsave() takes a plain file name and no comma; replace is a separate option of wooldid, so write bootsave(skboot  replace) replace.' - built by `subinstr("`wdbfn'", ",", " ", .)` at ado:6287, which turns 'skboot, replace' into the two-token string 'skboot  replace' rather than into the file name. Following the instruction literally in probe_br2.do: `bootsave(skb2  replace) replace` -> SK1_RC=0; `confirm file "skb2.dta"` -> 601; `confirm file "skb2 replace.dta"` -> 0.

The whole point of RF-6 (2026-09-13) was that a comma-bearing argument was 'swallowed whole and wrote a file literally called name, replace.dta at rc 0'. title: The unclustered bootstrap is not reproducible across a re-sort of the same data at a fixed rseed(), while the clustered bootstrap is - and nothing says so
surface: rseed() / bootstrap(standard) without cluster() / both resampling legs
claim: At one rseed(), the same rows in a different order give completely different bootstrap draws when no cluster() is given, on BOTH the count leg and the re-identification leg, whereas both clustered legs are order-invariant to 2e-15. rseed() is documented as what makes a run reproducible, with no distinction between the two cases.
observed: 30x8 panel, rseed(777001), reps(80), panel order vs a shuffled copy of the identical rows. count leg (att) cluster(unit): mreldif(e(bootdist)) = 1.641e-15. re-id leg (att att_i) cluster(unit): mreldif = 1.745e-15. count leg (att) no cluster(): mreldif = 0.48457418, se_att 0.214508 vs 0.209947. re-id leg (att att_i) no cluster(): mreldif = 0.77309209, se_att 0.198795 vs 0.189499.
expected: Cause is structural: with no cluster(), wooldid_bootrun sets the resampling cluster to the row number (ado:8921 `qui gen double `obsclus' = _n`), so 'cluster 7' means whatever row is seventh today, and the same draw sequence lands on different observations. I am NOT calling this a code defect - observation resampling is positional by construction, and Stata's own bootstrap prefix draws row positions the same way (that last point is by construction, not something I measured). The defect is the silence and the asymmetry: the clustered runs really are order-invariant, so a user who learned to trust rseed() on clustered specifications carries a false expectation into unclustered ones, and a re-sort or a re-ordered merge silently changes the reported SE. Remedy is one sentence in the rseed() help entry, not code. My original hypothesis - that the physical legs' unsorted `frame copy` would break clustered reproducibility - was WRONG and I record that as a negative: bsample with cluster() sorts internally.

title: The explanation the 2026-09-16 prereg retracted 'so it does not propagate' is still standing in the file that records the measurement

title: permute()'s nesting refusal r(459) is diagnosed on rows that are absent from e(sample), with a count dominated by consistent live rows and no remedy for the offending ones
surface: permute() cluster-onset nesting screen (wooldid_permctl ado:5969-5981); error message wording
claim: permute()'s cluster-onset-homogeneity screen (wooldid_permctl, ado:5969-5981) evaluates on insmp = ((if)==1) & !missing(cluster), which includes rows wooldid's own markout will discard, so a specification that runs clean without permute() is refused r(459) the moment permute() is added; the error's observation count is the whole offending cluster's rows, most of which are perfectly consistent live rows, and the rows actually responsible cannot be located through e(sample), e(N) or e(N_clust), all of which are identical to the version that runs.
observed: e4b_nesting.log. 8 states x 3 counties x 8 years; state 3 adopts in 2006 but its county 9 is a merge miss kept in the panel skeleton, with ttre == . AND y == . on every one of its 8 rows. Onset is constant within every i, so wooldid's general within-i screen (ado:772) does not fire. V1a, without permute(): runs clean, e(N)=184, att +1.8da894f951c6eX-001. V1c, county 9's rows dropped: e(N)=184, permute(shuffle) permexact runs, e(perm_npossible)=168. V1d, keep versus drop in one run: identical=1, N 184 both. V1b, keep them and add permute(shuffle) permexact: r(459), 'permute() requires clusters to be subsets of treatment-onset groups (levels of the timing variable, with never-treated its own group), but 24 in-sample observation(s) sit in clusters that mix onset values or mix treated and never-treated rows.' The 24 is state 3's whole row count; 16 of those are consistent live rows and only 8 are the dead ones. V2b: the same refusal when the dead county carries a stale onset (2010) rather than a missing one.
expected: The refusal itself is defensible and I do not claim otherwise: sthlp:430 puts markout-dead rows in the design and sthlp:431 requires every design cluster to be onset-homogeneous, and a never-treated (or 2010) county inside a 2006-adopting state genuinely is an onset coding inconsistent with cluster-level assignment. What is not documented and is a UX defect is the diagnostic. A user who runs the specification without permute(), sees it work, adds permute() and is told that 24 observations mix onsets has nothing in the output to point at county 9: e(N), e(N_clust) and the point estimate are identical to the version that runs, the 8 responsible rows are outside e(sample), the count names 24 rows of which 16 are innocent, and the message's remedies address the onset coding rather than the rows the estimator has already discarded. Contrast wooldid's own within-i screen at ado:772, which names the smallest offending i and lists three common causes.

title: The package has a named few-treated-cluster caution with a numeric threshold, but only on the engine whose own help says it is not a remedy for few treated clusters
surface: analytic clustered path vs the bootstrap() cautions (ado:6479, ado:6497, ado:1443)
claim: ado:6497 fires 'Caution: only N treated cluster(s) are available for resampling ... with few treated clusters the literature finds this bootstrap badly sized (MacKinnon and Webb 2017, 2018)' when fewer than six treated clusters exist, and ado:6479 cautions below ten clusters in total. Both live inside wooldid_bootctl and fire only under bootstrap() - the engine sthlp:532 describes as 'Neither mode is a remedy for few treated clusters'. On the DEFAULT ANALYTIC path, the one sthlp:255 calls the remedy, there is no few-treated-cluster caution at all, and the only cell-geometry caution (ado:1443) fires on the strictly binary predicate 'every i lies wholly inside one cluster'.
observed: One dataset, 40 states, cluster(state), i = the onset wave, TWO states in each treated cohort-by-period cell and FOUR treated states in the whole panel. Analytic run (i=coh, cluster(state), jointtests) prints 'N clusters = 40; N = 1920 (0 obs dropped from initial sample)' and no caution of any kind, with the joint pre-trend p-value printed as an ordinary test. The SAME data under bootstrap(standard) prints 'Caution: only 4 treated cluster(s) are available for resampling ... with few treated clusters the literature finds this bootstrap badly sized'. For contrast, the i=state arm prints the jointtests nesting caution.
expected: If four treated clusters are worth a named literature citation on the bootstrap path, the identical geometry on the analytic path - where the measured consequences are an 0.869 SE/SD ratio, 0.858 coverage and a 61.7% joint-test rejection rate (SK-FC-C) - warrants at least as much. The hazard class is already named in the package, with a numeric threshold, on the wrong engine. This is the corroborating half of MC-FC-1's 'the run gives the user no signal about what K they have'.

title: On the unconditionalse path e(vce)/e(vcetype) name the stage-1 regression's vce, not the covariance e(V) actually is: one matrix, two names
surface: unconditionalse x e(vce)/e(vcetype) label ladder (ado:4291-4300, ado:4676; contract stated at ado:4283)
claim: ado:4291's label ladder tests `robust' and `cluster()' BEFORE `unconditionalse', so the unconditionalse branch at ado:4300 is reachable only by the one call that supplies neither -- a bare [pw=] run, which ado:4676 exempts from the 'requires robust or clustered' refusal. Consequently the SAME unconditional covariance is posted under two different names depending only on whether the user typed the (under a pweight, redundant) `robust' option, and every ordinary unconditionalse user gets e(vce)="robust"/e(vcetype)="Robust" for a margins vce(unconditional) matrix. ado:4283 states the contract being broken: 'e(vce) and e(vcetype) name what e(V) IS'.
observed: 24-state x 12-period panel, att only. (i) [pw=w], unconditionalse robust: se 0.2855386999 (+1.246441c7f884cX-002), e(vce)=[robust], e(vcetype)=[Robust]. (iii) [pw=w], unconditionalse (no robust/cluster): se +1.246441c7f884cX-002 -- BITWISE THE SAME MATRIX -- e(vce)=[unconditional], e(vcetype)=[.]. Secondary and weaker: (ii) [pw=w], robust with no unconditionalse: se 0.2437086534, a different covariance 17.2% away, carrying the identical e(vce)=[robust]/e(vcetype)=[Robust]; (iv) [aw=w], unconditionalse robust: se 0.2865183827, e(vce)=[robust]; (v) [aw=w], robust: se 0.2437086534, e(vce)=[robust]. All rc 0.
expected: One covariance should carry one name. ado:4283's comment declares exactly that contract, and PS-1 (2026-09-07) posted these macros precisely so estout-class consumers could key on them; a name that flips with a redundant option defeats that. Because every unconditionalse user other than a bare-pweight one MUST supply robust or cluster() (ado:4676), in practice e(vce)="unconditional" is nearly unreachable and the unconditional VCE is almost always advertised as the stage-1 regression's vce instead.

title: The printed relyr column rounds distinct fractional horizons onto the same integer, showing -2 / -0 / 0 for -1.5 / -0.5 / +0.5
surface: result table display / relyr column under safety(off) with a fractional onset
claim: Under the safety(off) fractional-onset bypass, e(wdidmainresults) stores the relyr values correctly as -1.5, -0.5 and +0.5, but the display format renders that column as -2, -0 and 0: two distinct event-study horizons print as visually identical values, and one prints as the uninformative '-0'.
observed: Leg L3 (ttre+0.5, safety(off), esprelength(2) espostlength(2)). The printed table's relyr column reads: pre1.5 -> -2, pre.5 -> -0, post.5 -> 0. Reading the same cells out of e(wdidmainresults) with %12.7f gives -1.5000000, -0.5000000 and 0.5000000. See r3_fracOnset.log lines 265-285 for the table and lines 284-288 for the matrix values.
expected: The row stubs (pre1.5 / pre.5 / post.5) carry the fractional horizon correctly, so the display format on the relyr column should not contradict them. Printing '-0' and '0' for the two horizons either side of onset is the one place in the output where the half-integer grid is actively obscured rather than announced. Cosmetic only, and reachable only behind a bypass the default safety setting refuses with r(459), which is why this is low and not realistic.

title: The same rows in a different physical order change an event-study standard error by 3.7e-08 relative, on the reghdfe path with continuous weights only
surface: [aw=]/[pw=] weights on the reghdfe path with an event-study window (esprelength()/espostlength()); numerical reproducibility across row orderings
claim: With a weight variable whose values are not exactly representable in binary (any ordinary survey/administrative weight), wooldid's reghdfe path returns a different event-study standard error depending on the caller's physical row order. On a 30-state x 10-year panel with `att esprelength(3) espostlength(3) [aw=wt] cluster(st)`, sorting the identical rows differently moves one horizon's se/t/p/lb/ub by 3.732e-08 relative - 370x the project's stated 1e-10 indifference threshold. The point estimates do not move. The root cause is reghdfe's weighted clustered VCE, which I isolated directly: bare reghdfe on the two orderings differs in e(V) by 8.079e-10 with continuous aweights and by EXACTLY ZERO with integer aweights or no weights. It is NOT a surviving B21-class float store in wooldid, and it is NOT the regtol() convergence tolerance.
observed: rJ_roworder.do first flagged it: unweighted att/att_i/att_it/att_itime moved 3.563e-15 (shuffled) and 8.212e-15 (reverse-sorted); microdata fast-collapse 9.910e-13; bootstrap(standard) with rseed() 5.264e-15; permute(shuffle) 7.512e-15; `set sortseed` bit-identical - but `[aw=wt]` with an event-study window moved 3.732e-08. rK_isolate_aw.do bisected it: att-only unweighted 9.100e-16, att-only [aw=wt] 6.915e-16, att+es unweighted 1.448e-14, att+es [aw=wt] 3.732e-08, att+es+jointtests [aw=wt] 3.732e-08, att-only [pw=wt] 6.915e-16. The moving cells are exactly the pre3 row's se, t, p, lb_95ci, ub_95ci. rL_attribute.do attributed it: regtol(9) 3.732e-08, regtol(12) 3.732e-08, regtol(14) 3.732e-08 (UNCHANGED - not the absorption tolerance), regtol(6) 4.793e-09, [pw=wt] 3.732e-08, robust+aw 2.496e-08, fe(st)+aw 1.662e-08, but unconditionalse 1.407e-13 and customvce(cluster st) 1.790e-14 (both bypass reghdfe and run regress on explicit dummies), integer aweights 1.019e-13, constant aweight 4.870e-15, unweighted 1.448e-14. rM_floatcheck.do finished it: gtools' untyped `gegen = total()` at ado:1619-1621 yields DOUBLE, bit-identical to an explicit `gegen double`, so the B21 float class is not regressed; `set type double` changes nothing (6.270e-13 both ways); and bare `reghdfe y post i.st#c.post [aw=wt], absorb(st yr) cluster(st) tol(1e-9)` on the two orderings gives max rel diff in e(V) of 8.079e-10 with continuous aweights versus EXACTLY 0 with integer aweights and EXACTLY 0 unweighted (e(b) ~1e-13 in all three).
expected: A deterministic estimator must return the same number for the same rows regardless of their physical order; the project's own indifference threshold is rtol 1e-10 and its battery adjudicates on bit-identity, so a weighted event-study configuration reproducible only to ~1e-8 across row orderings is a false-positive generator in baseline blessing and battery-diff adjudication. The expectation holds because every other path I measured meets it: unweighted, constant-weight, integer-weight, fast-collapse, nofastcollapse, bootstrap-with-rseed, permute-with-set-seed and sortseed variation are all at or below 1e-12, and reghdfe itself is EXACTLY order-invariant once the weights are representable.

title: The replay guard tells the user that complete, valid results of the failing call 'predate that failed call'
surface: replay branch ado:26-46 / WOOLDID_LASTRC set at ado:79-81 after a post-ereturn-post failure; reached through saveplots() without replace
claim: When a wooldid call fails after its own `ereturn post' -- the event-study graph save at ado:13325 is the user-reachable case -- e() holds the COMPLETE, VALID results of that very call, yet the shell sets WOOLDID_LASTRC and bare `wooldid' refuses the replay with 'the last wooldid call failed with r(602); the stored results predate that failed call. Refit wooldid before replaying.' The stored results do not predate the failed call: they are that call's own results, already printed on screen. Under bootstrap() the refusal additionally hides inference the user paid the replications for and was never shown.
observed: repro PART B / probeB B1: after the r(602), e(cmd)=wooldid, colsof(e(b))=6 with colnames main_att pretreatment_att ES_att_pre2 ES_att_pre1 ES_att_post0 ES_att_post1, e(N)=320, e(wdidmainresults) present (mat list rc 0), and the full result table had already printed. Bare `wooldid' -> 'Error: the last wooldid call failed with r(602); the stored results predate that failed call. Refit wooldid before replaying.' r(198). Control: with `replace' the run returns rc 0 and bare `wooldid' replays at rc 0 (probeB B1_THIRD_REPLAY_RC=0). probeC C1 measures the cost: in the bootstrap rerun the r(602) cut in after wooldid_display part(1) but before part(boot), so the whole bootstrap interpretation block that run 1 printed -- the p-resolution note, the e(V)/e(df_r) caveats, the esttab/coefplot/honestdid warning -- never appeared; the fully rewired 12-replication inference sits in e(), was never fully displayed, and the one command that would display it is refused with a false statement about what is stored.
expected: The refusal itself is design and I am not disputing it (ado:277-279; ado:10731 shows the author knows a mid-display abort refuses the replay; known_bydesign section 6 rules WOOLDID_LASTRC as NFRPL-01/02 design). The defect is the message TEXT: the guard's own comment at ado:27-46 justifies the refusal on the premise that 'the stored e() results predate the user's latest (failed) attempt', and in this failure class that premise is measurably false. The marker already distinguishes one such class -- WOOLDID_LASTRC='postloop' gets its own sentence at ado:41 -- so the machinery for a truthful message in the post-post class exists.

title: A missing customweightmultiplier() removes the row from the REGRESSION, and a participants-only multiplier makes wooldid state something false about the user's data
surface: customweightmultiplier() x missing values x the estimation-sample screen (ado:704) x the r(459) no-control-group error
claim: sthlp:218 says the multiplier "enters the margins weights only and is deliberately not folded into the regression weight", but ado:704 marks a row whose multiplier is missing OUT of the estimation screen, so the multiplier changes which observations the underlying regression uses. When the multiplier is an administrative variable that exists only for programme participants, every never-treated row is marked out and wooldid stops with "you have no never-treated control group and no not-yet-treated control group whose treatment falls outside the sample window" on a dataset that has nine never-treated counties, with nothing naming customweightmultiplier() and neither offered remedy addressing the cause.
observed: repro_cwm_missing_error.do, 20 counties / 10 years / 3 establishments, 9 never-treated counties (270 rows), multiplier progsize strictly positive (min 240, max 640, ZERO negative rows) and present only on the 11 ever-treated counties. Arm A, no multiplier: r(0), e(N)=600. Arm B, customweightmultiplier(progsize): r(459), preceded only by "Caution: estimability checks found time periods exist in sample without a control unit, causing them to be dropped" and then "Error: you have no never-treated control group and no not-yet-treated control group whose treatment falls outside the sample window. To ignore this error, specify safety(off) or modify the sample window manually." No header prints, so there is no drop count and no clue. Arm C, the first offered remedy safety(off): r(0), but the run proceeds on 231 of 600 observations off not-yet-treated controls, with the header's "369 obs dropped from initial sample" the only trace and the cause still unnamed; the second offered remedy, widening the sample window, does nothing for this. Arm D, the remedy that works and that no message names -- fill the multiplier in with 0 on the control rows: r(0), e(N)=600, att 2.2629781. On scattered missingness (r2_pre_and_missing.do): M0 nothing missing e(N)=560 and underlying regression e(N)=560; M1 multiplier missing on 148 rows e(N)=412 and underlying regression e(N)=412, with all four estimands bit-equal to M3 where the same rows are physically deleted; M2 the same rows set to ZERO instead keeps e(N)=560 and gives different estimates. The M1 header does print "N = 412 (148 obs dropped from initial sample)", which caps the severity at low.
expected: Either sthlp:218's "enters the margins weights only" should say that a missing multiplier also removes the observation from the regression, or the r(459) should name the screening variable that emptied the control group. The expectation holds because sthlp:218 is the one sentence in the help that tells the user where this option acts, and it promises post-estimation only; sthlp:1107's "missing values drop the observation" is the nearest correction and does not say drop from what. The error compounds it by asserting a fact about the user's data that is false -- the panel has nine never-treated counties -- so a user will go and rebuild their panel rather than look at the multiplier. Scope note that keeps this honest: ado:704's markout is shared by cluster(), the controls, ccc_absorb(), contreat(), lattice() and interactivecontrols(), so a treated-only controls() variable produces the identical r(459); for a regressor that is unremarkable, and customweightmultiplier() is the only member of that list whose help promises it is post-estimation.

title: sthlp:239 makes the same false event-study naming promise for the ame family (ES_ame_i / ES_ame_itime do not exist) -- a third help location, extending hv-sgname-02
surface: contreat() / ame event-study e(b) column names / sthlp:239 vs sthlp:1315
claim: sthlp:239 says that under contreat() the ame family is 'stored under the same names with att replaced by ame', listing ame, ame_it, ame_i, ame_itime. That holds for the LEVEL rows but not for the event study: att_i + contreat() posts main_ame_i and pretreatment_ame_i but the ame event-study block is named ES_ame_it_*, so ES_ame_i_post0 and ES_ame_itime_post0 never exist. The seeded finding hv-sgname-02 localized this defect to sthlp:1305-1306 and to the att family only; it also lives at sthlp:239 and in the ame family.
observed: `wooldid y grp year ttre, att_i contreat(dose) contreatcontrols(basic) esprelength(2) espostlength(2) robust` posts 12 columns: main_att_i, pretreatment_att_i, main_ame_i, pretreatment_ame_i, ES_att_it_pre2/pre1/post0/post1, ES_ame_it_pre2/pre1/post0/post1. _b[main_ame_i] rc 0; _b[ES_ame_i_post0] r(111); _b[ES_ame_itime_post0] r(111); _b[ES_ame_it_post0] rc 0. e(b_es_ame_i) r(111); e(b_es_ame_it) rc 0. With att requested instead the ame ES block is ES_ame_* (r4 log 325-337), so the ame family has exactly the two-regime split the att family has. `ame_i` is not a user-facing option ('option ame_i not allowed'), so the help is the user's only route to the name.
expected: sthlp:1315's correct account names only att_it / ame_it as the shared event-study families. sthlp:239 and sthlp:1305-1306 both contradict it by promising per-estimand ES names. A help file should not promise a coefficient name that errors r(111), and the fix has to cover all three passages, not just the one the seeded finding named.

title: The bootstrap(bayes) x cell-weighted refusal is regime-blind: it refuses where bayes is accurate and lets safety(off) through where bayes is worst, although wooldid already computes the governing predicate
surface: ado:6437 bootstrap(bayes) x {att_it, att_i, att_itime} safety gate and its caution text
claim: The gate at ado:6437 refuses bootstrap(bayes) with any cell-weighted estimand regardless of where cluster() sits relative to i, but the collapse it is guarding against happens only when cluster() NESTS i. With cluster() finer than i the bayes standard error tracks bootstrap(standard) to within 4% and the refusal is a false positive; under nesting it is 0.17-0.30 of standard and safety(off) proceeds with a caution whose second clause ('when treatment effects vary across clusters') is false, since the collapse is already 0.50-0.62 under exact homogeneity. wooldid_bootrun already computes the governing predicate as wdb_nest at ado:8987-8998, after the gate has run.
observed: Ratio of bootstrap(bayes)+safety(off) se(att_it) to bootstrap(standard) se(att_it), same panel and same rseed(77777), homogeneous arm / cluster-level-heterogeneity arm: cluster FINER than i (i = onset cohort of 5 groups, cluster = state, treated cells of 8 rows) 0.9654 / 0.8523, and bayes se(att_it) moves +53.7% with the heterogeneity - refused anyway; cluster() == i 0.5003 / 0.1671 with bayes se(att_it) bitwise invariant (r01_saturated.do); cluster COARSER than i (i = state, cluster = region) 0.6199 / 0.2975, again bitwise invariant (r02_scope.do design C); i = cluster with three rows per cell 0.6102 / 0.2350 (r05_designD.do).
expected: A gate should fire on the configuration that is broken. The nesting predicate is exactly the one that decides whether a treated cell lies wholly inside one resampling cluster, and it is the same predicate the help already uses at sthlp:255 ('the intended practice is to cluster below the level of i'). A regime-aware gate would refuse under nesting only, and its caution could there state the collapse unconditionally instead of conditioning it on heterogeneity that is not needed to produce it. As shipped, a user who clusters finer than i - the configuration the help recommends, and the one the 2026-09-16 T2/T3 work deliberately opened up - is refused a bootstrap that would have been accurate, while a user who clusters at the level of i is told by the error message itself to type safety(off) and then gets a standard error a sixth of the right size.

title: RF-2's own rule is still broken in BOTH engines: the low-draw caution precedes the caller's r(459), the very shape 813c414 was written to fix
surface: bootstrap()/reps() and permute()/permreps() - caution ordering relative to wooldid_worker's r(459)
claim: Commit 813c414 states it moved the low-reps() caution 'below every aborting validation', but wooldid_bootctl (called at ado:4941) and wooldid_permctl both run BEFORE wooldid_worker's identifying-assumption check, so on a panel with no never-treated and no not-yet-treated control group a clustered bootstrap() or permute() run still prints its p-value-resolution caution and then aborts r(459). The move therefore surrendered the disclosure's unconditionality (hv-reps-01) without achieving its stated goal on the most common abort a real user hits.
observed: probe2_ordering.log, panel 2 (60 units, every unit treated at 2009/2011/2013): LEG_K `bootstrap(standard) reps(10) rseed(203) dots(0) cluster(unit)` prints 'Caution: with reps(10) the coefficient p-values fall on a grid of 0.200 (2/reps...' and then 'Error: you have no never-treated control group and no not-yet-treated control g...', rc 459. LEG_L `permute(shuffle) permreps(20) rseed(204) dots(0) cluster(unit)` prints 'Caution: with permreps(20) the smallest attainable per-coefficient permutation p-value is 0.095 ...' and then the same error, rc 459. LEG_K2 (identical panel, no engine option) prints the r(459) alone, rc 459 - so the caution is the only added output and the run genuinely never executed. That r(459) is raised at ado:958, inside wooldid_worker (defined at ado:531), downstream of the wooldid_bootctl call at ado:4941.
expected: 813c414's own commit message: 'The low-reps() caution printed BEFORE the boottstat nesting check and the two-cluster check, both of which abort - so a user whose run never executed was advised about its p-value resolution. Moved below every aborting validation.' By the author's own standard this is the defect, not a new complaint: the rule was applied only to the aborts local to wooldid_bootctl, and the no-control-group r(459) is a documented, common user error (it is the first entry in the brief's own KNOWN BY DESIGN list, with truncating the window as the remedy). The fix that satisfies both the rule and the help is to move the block to program top level AFTER the cluster branch closes (ado:6501) and, for the ordering intent, to have it fire only once the caller's identifying-assumption checks have passed.

title: wooldid.sthlp:636 says 'neither engine has a hard minimum' three lines after saying permute() requires permreps() >= 20 - and the code errors r(198)
surface: wooldid.sthlp:632-637 ('Which p-value is which') vs ado:5889-5893 permreps() minimum
claim: In the single paragraph at wooldid.sthlp:632-637 the bolded sentence states 'permute() requires permreps() to be at least 20 and additionally refuses a run in which fewer than max(20, half the requested draws) complete', and the closing sentence of the same paragraph states 'Raising the draw count is the only fix; neither engine has a hard minimum, since a handful of draws is a legitimate smoke test.' The second is false for permute(): ado:5889-5893 errors r(198). sthlp:535 states it correctly ('without permreps()'s hard floor of 20'), so the trailing sentence is the wrong one.
observed: LEG_H of refute_reps_caution.log: `wooldid y unit year ttre, permute(shuffle) permreps(19) rseed(106) dots(0) cluster(unit)` -> 'Error: permreps() must be at least 20: the engine refuses inference on fewer than 20 completed replications, so a smaller request can only ever burn the run.', rc 198. LEG_I with permreps(20) on the same data runs clean, rc 0. No caution or note reconciles the two help sentences.
expected: A help paragraph should not contradict itself, and a user who reads only the closing sentence (the one that gives the operational advice - 'a handful of draws is a legitimate smoke test') will write permreps(10) for a timing run and get an error. A charitable reading exists - 'no minimum tied to the .05 threshold', since the paragraph is about the .05 floor - but a reader cannot recover it from text that says 'hard minimum' three lines after a bolded 'requires permreps() to be at least 20'. The sentence is correct for bootstrap()'s reps() only and needs the engine named.

title: Inert options are announced inconsistently: one prints an 'is being ignored' Caution, six are silently accepted, four are refused outright
surface: option-companion screening (contreat()/makecfxplots gates)
claim: wooldid's published policy (ado:520-522) is that no accepted option is a silent no-op, but in binary mode the treatment of inert options is uneven across two separate gates. Keyed on makecfxplots: cfxlattice() prints an 'is being ignored' Caution while cfxplottypes(), makecfxplotsbysg and cfxplotnose are silently accepted. Keyed on contreat(): latticeignoreweights, ccnoabsorb and contreatpoly() are silently accepted while lattice(), contreatcontrols(), contreatwithin and makecfxplots are refused r(198).
observed: COMPANION loop in REPRO_F01_elasticity_header.log, on a binary-treatment panel with no contreat(): 'Caution: cfxlattice() has no effect without makecfxplots and is being ignored' then rc 0 for cfxlattice(dose); rc 0 and no message at all for latticeignoreweights, ccnoabsorb, contreatpoly(2), cfxplottypes(0), makecfxplotsbysg, cfxplotnose; r(198) 'requires contreat()' for lattice(all 3), contreatcontrols(basic), contreatwithin, makecfxplots.
expected: One rule per gate. Either refuse an option that cannot act, or accept it with the same kind of 'is being ignored' Caution cfxlattice() already prints. contreatpoly(2) is the case with a consequence rather than a cosmetic: it is accepted in binary mode with no dose present, so a user can believe a quadratic dose specification was fitted when there is no dose variable in the model at all.

title: Under bootstrap(), pretrendpower()'s reference distribution is keyed only on bootdf() and never reflects reps(); under the default bootdf(normal) it is chi2(k) with no finite-sample correction at all
surface: pretrendpower() + bootstrap() + bootdf(); the ptpdfok branch at ado:10353-10360
claim: sthlp:789 says that under bootstrap() the diagnostics run on the BOOTSTRAP covariance. wooldid_ptp's branch, however, keys only on e(df_r) (ado:10353-10360), which under bootstrap() is whatever bootdf() sets. So the joint pre-trend test's reference is identical at reps(39) and reps(199), and under bootdf(normal) — the documented default whenever cluster() is absent — it falls to chi2(keff) with no degrees-of-freedom correction, on a covariance that may have been built from as few as 39 completed replications.
observed: Same 16-state panel, bootstrap(standard) with rseed(4242). reps(39): e(df_r)=15, e(boot_df)=15, e(boot_completed)=39, e(boot_N_V)=39, line reads 'F(3, 15)'. reps(39) bootdf(normal): e(df_r)=., e(boot_df)=., same e(boot_N_V), line reads 'chi2(3)'. reps(199): e(boot_N_V)=197, line still reads 'F(3, 15)'. reps(199) bootdf(normal): 'chi2(3)'. e(roth_W_att) and e(roth_slope_se_att) are identical across the two bootdf settings at a given reps (0.94693379 / 0.09775118 at reps 39; 1.1506795 / 0.12121985 at reps 199), so only the reference moves — and it moves on bootdf(), never on the replication count.
expected: The reference distribution for a Wald statistic formed on an estimated covariance should reflect how well that covariance is estimated. Here it reflects only bootdf(), a setting documented as controlling the main table's t-versus-z convention, and the chi2 branch that PTP-3 flags as the no-correction branch for poisson is silently also the DEFAULT branch for any bootstrap run without cluster(). title: REFUTED: the bootctl cell-weighted gate's reasoning is correct; the recon's "either cwm is a no-op or the gate is wrong" is a false dichotomy
