claim: The recon claim's second half -- that bootctl's cell-weighted gate comment (ado:6430-6442) reasons about cwm inconsistently, so 'either cwm is a silent no-op on cell-weighted estimands or that gate's reasoning is wrong' -- is false. Both statements hold simultaneously: cwm is numerator-only and does not cancel, while the quantity the gate is actually talking about (the bootstrap(bayes) Dirichlet draw) is applied as the SAMPLE weight and therefore cancels exactly.
observed: wooldid_bootrun builds the bayes replication weight as 'qui gen double repw = basew*drawv' and passes it as the weight expression, wooldid ... [aweight=repw] (ado:9446-9451), so the multiplier enters W_it as well as the numerator. Measured: ARM C ([aw=sw*pop], no cwm) gives w_att_it min=max=1 -- the multiplier cancels. p1 arm E ([aw=w*m] with m varying WITHIN the cell, i.e. a resampling unit finer than i) also gives min=max=1, so the cancellation is exact in both nesting regimes, since sum_cell(w*m)/sum_cell(w*m) = 1 identically. customweightmultiplier() takes a different route by design: ado:624-626 states it is deliberately NOT folded into w (folding it in would break the fweight demotion), so it appears in the numerator only. The gate needs no change. Small residual, not filed as a defect: under a cluster finer than the cell the bayes draw does perturb within-cell composition even though the cell total stays 1, so the refusal message's rationale ('cluster reweighting cannot resample treatment cells') is narrower than the refusal -- no wrong number results, since the combination is refused under default safety and the refusal was confirmed to fire with a cwm in play (p4 N3, r(198)).
expected: A claim that two code sites are mutually inconsistent should be checked against the mechanism each one actually uses. Here the two multipliers travel by different routes (numerator-only vs sample weight), so no inconsistency exists.
refuter_note: Independently reproduced. Sample-weight route: w_att_it min 0.99999999999999989, max 1.00000000000000000 -- cancels exactly, even for a multiplier finer than the cell, because sum_cell(w*m)/sum_cell(w*m) = 1 identically. cwm route on the same multiplier: w_att_it min 0.71891796227648885, max 51.94960583131855003 -- does not cancel. bootstrap(bayes) + att_it + cwm(pop) refuses r(198) with the gate's own message; bootstrap(bayes) + att only + cwm(pop) proceeds r(0). The gate comment reasons about the Dirichlet draw, not about cwm, and the two multipliers travel by different routes, so the recon's 'either cwm is a silent no-op or the gate's reasoning is wrong' is a false dichotomy. The prober's refutation stands; no defect, hence severity none.
refuter_did: Wrote my own panel with a multiplier that varies WITHIN the (i,t) cell (establishment-level epop) and ran it twice: once folded into the SAMPLE WEIGHT ([aw=sw*epop], the route bootstrap(bayes)'s Dirichlet draw takes at ado:9449 'gen double repw = basew*drawv'), once as customweightmultiplier(epop) (the numerator-only route at ado:1644). Then fired the gate itself both ways. Read ado:6432-6439 and ado:9435-9455 directly rather than taking the prober's description.

title: fe() with customvce()/unconditionalse: wooldid cautions, then enters the fe() variables as CONTINUOUS regressors and completes with rc 0
surface: fe() combined with customvce() or unconditionalse
claim: On the plain-regress paths wooldid prints a caution that absorbed fixed effects are not supported and that the user must specify them as controls with i. prefixes -- and then proceeds to paste the bare fe() varlist into the regression with no i. prefix, fitting a linear trend in the identifier instead of a fixed effect. The run completes rc 0 and reports fit statistics and an average marginal effect from that model.
observed: Leg A of probe08 (verbose): 'Caution: unconditional SEs and custom VCE specifications rely on the plain regress command and so are not compatible with absorbed fixed effects. You must specify anything in fe as controls, manually specifying any needed i. prefixes.' then the echoed command 'reg y i.i i.t unit  i.__000009##c.(__000008)  i.__000005#i.__000006#i.__000007##c.dose ... , vce(cluster unit)' -- `unit' with no i. prefix. Result: R2 = 0.332, ame = -0.178105713914, where the correctly absorbed twin (`fe(unit) cluster(unit)', same data) reports R2 = 1.000 and ame = 1.370000000000, which is the exact-fit truth.
expected: wooldid already knows at parse time that this combination is invalid -- it says so. An error would cost nothing and would stop the user from reading fit statistics off a regression on the numeric value of a unit identifier. This is surfaced rather than silent, hence low severity, but 'warn and then produce a meaningless number' is a predictable mis-read.
refuter_note: This is documented behaviour, stated in the help with the identical example. wooldid.sthlp lines 1051-1053: 'This holds on the default estimation path. Under customvce() or unconditionalse, estimation runs through regress - or poisson under poisson - rather than reghdfe, and a BARE token there is read as a CONTINUOUS variable: fe(state) fits a linear term in the state code rather than a set of state indicators. Write the prefix explicitly - fe(i.state) - whenever those options are in use, or on any specification you may later run both ways.' The runtime caution (ado:4637-4638) likewise ends 'manually specifying any needed i. prefixes'. The documented remedy works: on identical data fe(i.unit) customvce(cluster unit) gives R2 = 0.960850 while fe(unit) customvce(cluster unit) gives R2 = 0.725469. The finding's stated expectation - 'wooldid already knows at parse time that this combination is invalid - it says so' - is the opposite of what the help says: the combination is VALID, the i. prefix is the user's responsibility, and erroring would remove a documented capability. The only residual is that the caution's phrase 'specify anything in fe as controls' is looser than the help's 'write fe(i.state)' - a wording nit, not a defect, and not what the finding claimed.
refuter_did: Read the fe() entry in the pinned help rather than only the runtime caution, then ran both spellings on the same data through wooldid to check that the documented remedy works.

lens.impact: A user who writes fe(unit) under customvce()/unconditionalse without reading the fe() help entry gets a linear term in the unit code rather than unit indicators, and reads fit statistics and an average marginal effect off that model. The runtime caution flags the i.-prefix requirement at the moment it happens, the help documents the behaviour and the remedy in three separate places, and the remedy recovers the absorbed answer exactly. Nothing is lost that the documentation does not tell the user how to get back.

title: A plain run leaves three globals in the user's Mata workspace, one of them named `k` - attribution to wooldid NOT established
surface: Mata and scalar namespace on every run
claim: One plain `wooldid y unit year ttre, cluster(state) att` on a session whose Mata workspace was empty leaves it holding three real scalars - __00000L, __00000M and `k` - and leaves two scalars in the Stata scalar namespace (__gtools_gfile_ghdfeabs = 65, __gtools_gfile_gregvcov = 65). The nofastcollapse arm s2 adds nothing; permute (s5) adds __000017/__000018; bootstrap+plots (s6) adds __00000N/__000015/__000016 and removes __000018; poisson (s7) removes __00000N.

HOWEVER the code evidence points AWAY from wooldid: every `k` in wooldid's own Mata source is a declared function-local (e.g. ado:14737 `string colvector k` inside wooldid_bootcellkeym), and an undeclared name inside a Mata function is a local rather than a global, so wooldid cannot create the Mata global `k` that way; its only top-level Mata assignments are to the namespaced `wooldid_Mtmp` (ado:6689, 8121, 8791, 8795), which do not fire on a plain run. The `__gtools_` scalars appearing in the same diff make gtools/reghdfe the likely source. repro_mata_k.do and p21_matanames.do settle it in under a minute each (reghdfe alone vs gtools alone vs wooldid alone in three separate sessions, plus a direct `mata: k = 12345` clobber test); neither got a Stata slot before I ran out of time, because the shared 8-instance cap was saturated - and at times exceeded - by other agents for the last stretch. If it is a dependency's, STRIKE this finding.
refuter_note: The behaviour reproduces exactly as described but belongs to gtools, not wooldid, which is the strike condition the prober themselves set ('If it is a dependency's, STRIKE this finding'). A bare gegen+gcollapse in a session that has never loaded wooldid clobbers Mata `k` and creates both __gtools_gfile_* scalars. Not a wooldid defect; report upstream if anywhere.
refuter_did: Ran the isolation the prober could not get a Stata slot for: three SEPARATE Stata processes, each starting from 'mata: mata clear' and planting 'mata: k = 12345'. rF_mata_gtools.do runs ONLY gtools (gegen ... by(st) plus gcollapse ... by(st yr)) with no wooldid and no reghdfe: k -> 2 (CLOBBERED), Mata globals __000000/__000001/k appear, and BOTH __gtools_gfile_ghdfeabs and __gtools_gfile_gregvcov appear in the Stata scalar namespace. rE_mata_reghdfe.do runs ONLY reghdfe: k -> 12345 (INTACT), no Mata globals, no gtools scalars. rD_mata_wooldid.do runs ONLY wooldid: k -> 3, same two __gtools_ scalars. The value left in k equals the by-variable count (2 under by(st yr), 3 inside wooldid's own collapse), which is gtools' by-key machinery. gtools owns the name; reghdfe is innocent; wooldid's only involvement is calling a documented hard dependency.

Note: the multicollinearity caution above was triggered 41 times total.'

The observable reproduces exactly: 4 of 16 e(V) diagonals = -1.0000e+100 with b = exactly 0 on pretreatment_ame and ES_ame_pre4/pre3/pre2, e(V_es_ame) diagonal = 0,0,0,x,x,x, e(es_ndegen_ame)=3 (tags F5_* in the log). I then checked the governing documentation rather than the R1 ruling the prober cites.

title: The granular-i caution tells the user runtime, not the variable limit, is what will bite under lattice() -- on both designs measured the variable limit bit first, at unremarkable runtimes
surface: the >100-distinct-i runtime caution (ado:1371) and its help text (sthlp:1163, sthlp:1272)
claim: ado:1371 and sthlp:1163 assert that under lattice() 'runtime grows ... about its 1.9th power ... so a granular i can dominate runtime long before it approaches Stata's variable limits'. At the cell counts where the variable ceiling is first breached under lattice(), runtime is still tens to low hundreds of seconds, so a user reading that sentence has no reason to suspect maxvar. The caution also does not print at all at i = 50 distinct values, which is where the failure I measured happened.
observed: 50-state panel (15,000 rows, 525 cells, i = 50 levels): the no-lattice arm completes in 42 seconds; adding lattice(all 5) needs 6115 columns and dies at the default maxvar 5000. 25-state panel (10,000 rows, 213 cells, i = 25 levels): lattice(all 5) completes in 162 seconds once maxvar is raised to 12000, and dies below 3500. In both cases the variable ceiling was breached while runtime was unremarkable, and in both cases the >100-distinct-i caution never printed.
expected: SCOPE LIMIT, stated honestly: the caution's sentence is an asymptotic claim about large cell counts K and I measured two points, neither large. I did not measure where the runtime and variable-count curves actually cross, so I am not claiming the sentence is false in general -- only that at the K where maxvar first binds under lattice(), the sentence steers a user away from the constraint that actually stopped the run. Marked probable rather than certain for exactly this reason.
refuter_note: The claim is that at the cell counts where the variable ceiling first binds under lattice(), runtime is still unremarkable (tens to low hundreds of seconds), so the caution misdirects. On my panel, at column counts below the ceiling, runtime had already grown by at least an order of magnitude and had not finished. The help's sentence is supported by my data point, not undermined. Honest scope limit on my side too: my lattice arm was killed unfinished, so I have a lower bound on the ratio, not the ratio.
refuter_did: Two grounds. (1) The prober's own report concedes both halves: the caution never printed at either of their two measured points (i = 25 and i = 50, below the >100-distinct-i threshold), and the sentence is an asymptotic claim about large K that they did not test. A caution that does not print cannot steer anyone anywhere. (2) My own runtime measurement points the other way. In s4_lattice_own.do, the identical spec with and without lattice on one 7,200-row panel: no lattice, ~775 columns, rc 0 in 13.15 s; lattice(all 4), ~3,685 columns (still BELOW the default ceiling), still running after about 4 minutes when I killed it myself to free a Stata slot -- so >= 18x and climbing, unfinished, under 8-process contention. The column ratio is 3685/775 = 4.75x and 4.75^1.9 ~ 19, so my ratio is consistent with sthlp:1272's 'roughly the 1.9th power of K' rather than in tension with it.
